author: Andrea DiP
title: Maria da Penha, 20 anos: Alta de feminicídios revela fracasso estatal em proteger mulheres
content:
O Brasil segue sendo um país violento, especialmente para as pessoas negras e para as mulheres. Pelo quarto ano consecutivo, o país registra índices recordes de feminicídios e tentativas de feminicídio, de acordo com o

Anuário Brasileiro de Segurança Pública 2026

.

Apenas no ano passado, foram 1.571 vítimas desse crime, a maioria mulheres negras, assassinadas dentro de casa. A Lei Maria da Penha completa 20 anos, mas a violência contra as mulheres permanece como um dos principais desafios na segurança pública.


Nesta semana, o Pauta Pública recebe Juliana Brandão, advogada e coordenadora de Gênero e Raça do Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública. Em entrevista a Andrea Dip, ela analisa os dados do Anuário Brasileiro de Segurança Pública, o impacto do racismo nas taxas de violência, e defende a importância de políticas públicas voltadas à prevenção e ao fortalecimento da rede de proteção às vítimas.

“Quando a gente se abstém de pensar em saídas preventivas, a gente está consentindo com essa escalada”

, afirma.


Juliana Brandão é advogada e coordenadora de Gênero e Raça do Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública


Leia os principais pontos da conversa e ouça o podcast completo abaixo.


EP 228


											O fracasso do Estado em proteger mulheres – com Juliana Brandão


7 de agosto de 2026


					·


				Coordenadora de gênero e raça do Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública analisa as falhas de crimes contra a mulher


0:00


-:–


15


15


Veja mais episódios desta série


Segundo dados do último Anuário Brasileiro de Segurança Pública, em 2025, o Brasil registrou o maior número de feminicídios da série histórica iniciada em 2015, quando a tipificação do crime foi criada no país. De que tipo de violência de gênero estamos falando?


Estamos falando de uma violência que interrompe a vida das mulheres, uma violência que pode ser evitada. Porque o feminicídio, na verdade, é o ápice de um ciclo de violência que se inicia com um empurrão, um tapa, uma humilhação, com a violência psicológica, patrimonial e perseguição.

Essas violências acabam sendo naturalizadas e desconsideradas como tal. Com isso, a mulher vai se sentindo cada vez mais enredada nesse ciclo

, muitas vezes envergonhada e até se sentindo culpada por estar nessa situação.


Porque estamos falando de uma violência que é cometida por alguém que é do círculo muito próximo dessa mulher. Essa violência do feminicídio, que os dados do anuário trazem agora, é uma violência que acontece na maior parte das vezes dentro de casa, entre quatro paredes. Então, o problema está no ambiente doméstico. O problema está naquilo que acontece quando ninguém vê, quando a porta está fechada.


Quando falamos da violência que atinge também crianças e adolescentes, é também praticada por alguém que é do círculo muito próximo delas e a maior parte das vítimas são meninas negras, que repetem também o perfil das vítimas de feminicídio.

 Então, temos um endereçamento muito certo dessa violência, que já devia ser um sinal pra gente, um farol para onde a gente tem que olhar se a gente quer de fato mudar essa essa situação que a gente está vivendo.


Houve também um número alto de tentativas de feminicídio. Quer dizer que há falhas na prevenção?


Olhando para os dados, a gente vê uma escalada. Então, um recrudescimento da violência contra as mulheres, que não se explica tão só por uma melhora de enquadramento penal, mas por uma situação mais geral. Um caldo mesmo de violência que é expresso por um Brasil que é muito inseguro para as mulheres.


É muito difícil ser mulher no Brasil, porque as mulheres são vítimas de ameaça, as mulheres são vítimas de agressão, as mulheres são vítimas de perseguição. E se a gente levar em conta que essa mulher tem denunciado esses preditores de feminicídio, significa que ela vai e faz um boletim de ocorrência. Ali, por exemplo, já seria um momento de a gente dizer: “Olha, essa mulher aqui a gente tem que olhar com mais cuidado, porque ela conseguiu vencer essa barreira, ela conseguiu entender que não é culpada, ela conseguiu entender que não está sozinha. E o que acontece dentro do lar dela é algo que importa para o nosso coletivo. Vamos trazê-la para mais perto, vamos olhar o que está acontecendo, que rotina é essa, que autonomia ela tem, como é que ela sai desse enredo”, que é um enredo que vai, de alguma forma, dizimando as possibilidades de a mulher, de fato, encontrar uma saída.


Mas o que o direito penal oferece hoje? Oferece a …

author: Rizomatica
title: Detienen violentamente a dos miembros del Lof Antonio Panitrur en Bajo Malleco
content:
«Mediante violento procedimiento y con fuerte contingente policial fue detenido el Peñi Adan Huentecol Neculpan y el Peñi Dagoberto Soto Neculpan, ambos miembros de la comunidad Mapuche Antonio Panitrur, de la zona del bajo Malleko.


La detención de los peñi se produce en momentos que ambos trabajaban en reparar los caminos interiores de la comunidad, hasta donde llegan un fuerte contingente de carabineros, los que sin mediar con ellos, lo comienzan a golpear y posteriormente los detienen, y los trasladan hasta la comisaría de Collipulli. dónde quedaron retenidos hasta mañana sábado cuando serán pasados a control de detención en el tribunal de Collipulli.


Cómo comunidad Antonio Panitrur, consideramos que estas prácticas abusivas, responden a la medidas de amedrentamiento policial y persecución política del racista gobierno de José Antonio kast.


La comunidad Antonio Panitrur, acompañó hasta altas horas de la noche a la familia en la comisaria, con la finalidad de conocer el estado de salud de los peñi. Quienes presentan  lesiones evidentes de la golpiza que propinaron a ambos.


La detención según lo informado por carabineros, se dió por tener orden de detención pendiente del año 2019 en caso del peñi Adan Huentecol Neculpan, mientras que el peñi Dagoberto Soto Neculpan fue detenido por maltrato a obra de carabineros.


Hacemos un llamado a distintas comunidades Mapuche de la zona, para que nos puedan acompañar mañana en su control de detención.


Comunica: Lof Antonio Panitrur Wallmapu


Bajo Malleko. 7 de agosto 2026″.


Esta información se publicó en

Radio Kurruf

.

title: Fosas, fronteras y Palestina: las guerras contra la humanidad
content:
La segunda parte del recuento que hace Avispa Mídia del Semillero Guerra contra la humanidad. Las poblaciones y la naturaleza bajo asedio , convocado por el Ejército Zapatista de Liberación Nacional (EZLN), aborda los crímenes contra la vida humana y la idea de “lo desechable” a través de distintas violencias contemporáneas desde el genocidio en Palestina, las desapariciones y asesinatos de personas en México, crímenes vinculadas a disputas territoriales y económicas; las condiciones que enfrentan las personas en desplazamiento forzado; y sobre los trabajadores frente a tecnologías emergentes y la precarización laboral.

La primera parte, la primera entrega, puedes leer aquí .

Durante estas sesiones el Capitán Insurgente Marcos destacó “la luz de resistencia y rebeldía de las madres buscadoras, a quienes, por mucho que las amemos, siempre les quedaremos a deber. Y que ahora nos impulsan a volver a caminar fuera de nuestras montañas, porque los brazos y los besos siempre es mejor darlos en persona y no por internet (...) y de forma especial, a las luchas, resistencias y rebeldías que han sido asediadas por siglos”.

Con la proyección de la pintura ¿Dónde estás, amor mío?, de Antonio Ramírez, basada en las madres buscadoras, la periodista y académica Alejandra Guillén habló de ‘Desaparición y leva para la acumulación de capital. Grietas de resistencia ante el nuevo dominio’.

“Es para ellas (madres buscadoras) también toda mi palabra y mucha de la que recojo viene de ellas, de sus hijos y de todas las personas que anónimamente hablan para explicar lo que está ocurriendo. Este es un saludo para las madres buscadoras que, lamentablemente, cada vez son más en este país”, dijo.

Recordó la historia de Jorge, ocurrida hace casi catorce años en Jiquilpan, en 2012, que coincide con el surgimiento del Cártel Jalisco Nueva Generación que desde sus inicios recurrió al reclutamiento forzado y al trabajo esclavo para conformar sus estructuras, una práctica que entonces aún no era reconocida como patrón de desaparición.

Las pistas reunidas por la familia, relató la periodista, ubicaban a Jorge en ranchos de la región de Tapalpa, un territorio que identificó como estratégico para la consolidación de la organización criminal y de economías legales e ilegales, como la explotación forestal y minera. En ese mismo periodo, añadió, también desaparecieron defensores del territorio en la Sierra de Manantlán, entre ellos Celedonio Monroy Prudencio, hubo el desplazamiento de comunidades enteras y el despojo sistemático de ranchos y tierras mediante las llamadas "limpias".

“Estaban sacando las maderas preciosas, las especies, las minas (...) Y lo han hecho, digamos, en alianza siempre con las mineras de la región. Y todo esto salía por los puertos, no solo en Jalisco, en toda la sierra de Jalisco y toda la sierra de Michoacán. Todo estaba ocurriendo al mismo tiempo”, precisó Alejandra Guillén.

Pero la expansión respondió a una estrategia previamente diseñada, articulada con rutas comerciales que permitían el intercambio de insumos para la producción de drogas sintéticas y otras mercancías provenientes de Asia.

La periodista hizo hincapié en que los grupos criminales en México constituyen apenas el nivel más visible de una red que involucra a actores financieros, políticos y empresariales. Entonces la violencia opera como parte de un modelo económico con objetivos de largo plazo, más que como una sucesión de hechos aislados.

En ese esquema, explicó que el reclutamiento forzado y la explotación de personas no solo sirven para conformar ejércitos, sino también para consolidar ese proyecto de expansión territorial basado en el control social y la transformación de quienes son sometidos.

En ese proceso buscan desarticular el tejido social, normalizar la crueldad e incorporar personas a un esquema de dominación que ha hecho posible ejercer un control permanente sobre barrios, pueblos y regiones.

“No es la primera vez que se esclaviza a personas, pero sí de la manera en que ha estado ocurriendo tan masivamente, decenas y decenas y decenas. Es como la fábrica del mal que instalaron, muy bien pensada, para no solo construir ejércitos, sino también transformar subjetividades (...) Y esta maquinaria ha necesitado seguir alimentándose de más personas”, lamentó Alejandra Guillén.

Recordó el caso de Teuchitlán, municipio de Jalisco, pues hizo visible el reclutamiento forzado y los circuitos de lugares donde retienen a las personas y que familias …

author: Darío Aranda
title: Ley de tierras: la calle dijo basta y frenó al Gobierno con su intento de más extranjerización
content:
Por Nahuel Lag


“La tierra no se vende, no se quema ni se desaloja”, dice una bandera, también una pancarta y lo grita alguien que pasa caminando. El que “no se vende” fue una victoria de la presión popular contra la “Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada”, cuando el Gobierno cedió el miércoles y quitó el capítulo de cuasi derogación de la Ley de Tierras. Pero a las 14 horas, cuando la Cámara de Senadores comenzó la sesión para tratar los otros capítulos de la normativa, miles de personas marchan al Congreso por Avenida de Mayo y desde las calles laterales de la Plaza Congreso exigiendo todavía que la tierra tampoco “se quema ni se desaloja”.


La masiva movilización que enfrentó a la lluvia y la represión de las fuerzas federales logró también, en la madrugada, que se quite el capítulo que modificaba la Ley de Manejo del Fuego. Así, el proyecto negociado con la UCR, PRO y bloques provinciales, sin apoyo social, obtuvo media sanción y mantiene otros dos capítulos críticos: la restricción a las expropiaciones y los desalojos exprés en tierras urbanas y rurales.


"Lo que hizo cambiar todo fue la presión popular"


La sesión empezó con una declaración de principios de La Libertad Avanza. El senador

Joaquín Benegas Lynch

, denunciado por tener una empresa que vende tierras a extranjeros, usó su “cuestión de privilegio” antes de iniciar el debate. En los bares sobre Avenida de Mayo se ve lo ve por televisión desde la calle. Lo que se escucha mientras son bombos y trompetas de la convocatoria hecha por las dos CTA, la UTEP y la CGT. También hay banderas del Frente de Sindicatos Unidos, muchas partidarias del peronismo y la izquierda; y más cerca del Congreso se ve a la Unión de Trabajadores y Trabajadoras de la Tierra (UTT), que ya realizó un nuevo verdurazo.


Foto: Plaga Colectiva


Ezequiel llegó desde Avellaneda y tiró la manta sobre Avenida de Mayo para vender el pañuelo de ocasión: “¡No a la Ley de Extranjerización!”, dice.


—¿Se vende el pañuelo de la patria no se vende?


—Sí, sale.


—¿A vos qué te parece el proyecto?


—No sé qué decirte. No estoy al tanto, estoy preocupado por tener para comer. Es difícil llegar a fin de mes y eso que no tengo hijos.


Miles de personas se ven más adelante, al costado del escenario montado por las organizaciones políticas, sindicales y sociales, el camión de la UTT, que llegó del cordón hortícola de La Plata para repartir alimentos entre la gente, eso que le falta a Ezequiel. Las organizaciones campesinas, junto a la Multisectorial por la Tierra y la Vivienda, denunciaron la gravedad del proyecto cuando sólo un grupo de organizaciones se manifestaba frente al Congreso en los otros cuatro intentos frustrados por aprobar la extranjerización de la tierra, desde el dictamen del 20 de mayo pasado.


“Lo que hizo cambiar todo fue la presión popular. Había un núcleo que veníamos impulsando el rechazo y después, obviamente, la Scaloneta en el partido contra Inglaterra y la bandera de ‘las Malvinas son Argentinas’ despertó el sentimiento de soberanía. Pudimos desenmascarar al gobierno ante la situación expresa de que toda la tierra y, sobre todo los recursos naturales, podían quedar en manos de los capitales extranjeros. Eso hizo que los gobernadores tengan que retirar el voto de sus senadores”, analiza Nahuel Levaggi, de la UTT y Mesa Agroalimentaria Argentina (MAA).


Las banderas con la tipografía de la bandera que usaron los jugadores de la Selección Argentina flotó en el aire por todos lados. El grito de fondo, insistía: “La patria no se vende”.


Ana es activista ambiental y llegó desde La Plata, tiene el texto escrito en un cartel con la bandera Argentina y en un pin en su campera. “Necesitamos defender lo que es nuestro. La tierra pertenece a quien la trabaja y a nuestros ancestros. No podemos permitir que vendan nuestra soberanía”.


Foto: Plaga Colectiva


La tierra no se vende


La derrota del capítulo de tierras se completó a 24 horas antes de la marcha, en una reunión de la presidente del bloque de La Libertad Avanza, Patricia Bullrich, con los aliados de la UCR, PRO y los legisladores que responden a los gobernadores Hugo Passalacqua (Misiones), Osvaldo Jaldo (Tucumán), Rolando Figueroa (Neuquén) y Gustavo Sáenz (Salta). Ellos fueron los que bajaron el pulgar. Bullrich, un día antes, había asegurado que tenía los votos en una conferencia de prensa con los presidentes de las comisiones de Asuntos Constitucionales, Agustín Coto (LLA), y de Legislación General …

author: A.N.A.
title: [Espanha] Chamamento: Rumo a um Coletivo Silvestre e Comunal. Projeto
content:
Olá. Este é um chamamento.


Um sinal de fumaça.


“

Comunalizar,


não poderia ser de outra forma.


Reensilvestrar, ensilvestrar-se.

“


Queremos convocar pessoas que se sentem impulsionadas pela visão de contribuir para um mundo mais silvestre e comunal.


Em concreto, gostaríamos de promover a criação de um coletivo de convivência, uma comunidade de pessoas que cuidam de seu entorno natural com uma abordagem silvestre para suprir suas necessidades, reconstruindo as culturas comunitárias dentro de seu grupo e em seu território mais amplo.


Por “silvestre” entendemos uma forma de vida e de nos relacionarmos que busca voltar a fazer parte dos lugares que habitamos, diminuindo a dependência de estruturas estatais e industriais e recuperando e integrando práticas como a coleta de plantas e frutos, a caça, a pesca, ou o uso de materiais naturais para resolver as necessidades vitais. Vemos essas atividades não apenas como técnicas para suprir necessidades, mas como portas de entrada para outras formas de organização social, de autonomia e de relação com o território.


Para isso, consideramos imprescindível ocupar-se da regeneração dos processos naturais, do cuidado e do respeito ao entorno. Também propomos a convivência do silvestre com práticas agrícolas, pecuárias, florestais, etc., embora com a intenção de que ocupe um lugar central. Cientes das dificuldades atuais, queremos caminhar com firmeza nessa direção, sem julgamentos nem purismos, aproveitando as brechas e assumindo o caráter exploratório da tarefa.


Nessa mesma busca, gostaríamos de colocar no centro a recuperação de culturas e formas de organização comunitárias, que estiveram presentes na Península Ibérica desde tempos pré-históricos, nas quais a vizinhança cuida e usufrui do entorno que habita de maneira comum. Defender e promover os bens comuns, a autogestão, a democracia direta da assembleia aberta e os trabalhos coletivos, o pensar-se em comum entre vizinhos e vizinhas e com o território. Também nos referimos aos comuns mais modernos e aos diferentes movimentos e estruturas associativas nascidas em torno do comum. Há diversas maneiras de materializar tudo isso; em qualquer caso, nos parece que implica trabalhar tanto internamente no coletivo como com diferentes atores locais, vizinhos e vizinhas, bem como organizar-se com outros grupos afins.


Por fim, nessa visão cabem múltiplas formas de concretizar um coletivo de convivência, desde a vizinhança até uma economia comum, assim como diferentes abordagens de coletivizar os cuidados. Seja qual for, nos parece imprescindível atender ao processo interno do grupo de maneira consciente e ativa, cuidando do desenvolvimento pessoal e ocupando-se da estrutura e das dinâmicas grupais do coletivo.


Para nós, situar-se em uma vida mais silvestre e comunal é uma das maneiras de responder à crise ecossocial. Reconhecemos que há muitas maneiras, muitos lugares a partir dos quais repensar, agir e viver esse sistema. Neste momento e circunstâncias, tentamos contribuir a partir desta proposta, partindo de um legado que perdura desde as sociedades pré-estatais, e que hoje muitos movimentos estão recuperando e atualizando.


Em que ponto estamos


Esta proposta encontra-se em uma fase inicial. Nós, duas pessoas, a promovemos, desenvolvendo essa visão no meio rural e com a inquietação de gerar encontro e comunidade:


Gostaríamos de reunir pessoas interessadas em fazer parte da criação de um coletivo de convivência que coloque os eixos silvestre e comunal no centro. Por enquanto, não foi concretizado além da visão aqui descrita. A ideia é que o próprio grupo construa sua forma de vida, organização e localização, de acordo com suas necessidades, capacidades e desejos.


Também queremos conectar com pessoas que, embora não estejam pensando agora em fazer parte de uma comunidade de convivência, ressoem com essa visão e queiram explorar como impulsionar uma cultura mais silvestre e comunal em seus territórios.


Se isso te motiva, te interessa, gostaríamos de nos encontrar, convidar você a se aproximar e fazer parte do processo. A ideia é se conhecer, reunir-se em diferentes espaços de exploração, sondar o que se move e em quais direções.


Você pode nos escrever ou ligar contando quem é, de onde escreve, qual seu interesse e sua disponibilidade para participar de encontros.


Até breve!


Raquel e Gonzalo

author: anred
title: Desde el territorio-cuerpo: por qué la liberación palestina es una cuestión feminista
content:
Tras el 7 de octubre de 2023, el proceso de colonización y el intento de exterminio del pueblo palestino por parte de Israel han entrado en una nueva fase de intensificación. Si bien dos semanas antes Benjamin Netanyahu exhibió, en la sede de la ONU, un mapa titulado “El Nuevo Oriente Medio”, del que Gaza y Cisjordania habían sido borradas, el 30 de octubre de 2023 apeló, como acostumbra el sionismo, a textos bíblicos y, citando a Yahvé, afirmó: “darás muerte a hombres y mujeres, niños y recién nacidos, bueyes y ovejas, camellos y asnos; no dejarás con vida nada que respire” . Por Maite Arraiza* |

Vientos del Sur.


Ante el actual genocidio, que no hace sino dar continuidad a la colonización sionista iniciada a finales del s. XIX con el apoyo del Imperio británico primero y del estadounidense después, al servicio de los intereses del capital occidental, Rita Segato (2025) se declara “ex-humana”, pues ya no quiere “pertenecer a esta especie siniestra, genocida”. El genocidio palestino nos interpela de manera directa a todas aquellas que nos consideramos feministas y luchamos por la profunda transformación de las condiciones materiales, de los regímenes de poder y de los afectos, vínculos y cuidados que sostienen la vida. En palabras del Movimiento de Mujeres Palestinas Alkarama (2025a), quien nos insta a asumir nuestra responsabilidad moral, política e histórica: “No hay feminismo revolucionario sin una postura clara a favor de la liberación de Palestina. Toda Palestina. Desde el río hasta el mar”.


Desde las tradiciones históricas de los feminismos anticoloniales, antiimperialistas y marxistas, en las que se inscribe también una parte significativa del movimiento feminista de Euskal Herria, junto a numerosas voces y colectivos feministas palestinos y aliados, este texto expone por qué la lucha por la liberación del pueblo palestino es una cuestión feminista central. Se erige, así, como denuncia del silencio, de la complicidad y del apoyo del feminismo blanco hegemónico al proyecto colonial sionista y al imperialismo occidental. Subraya que, junto a la vital tarea de denunciar y luchar contra el genocidio palestino, una postura feminista conocedora del carácter histórico milenario del pueblo palestino implica la denuncia de la colonización y el apoyo a la liberación de Palestina, de toda Palestina, desde el río hasta el mar. Hoy más que nunca, sostener una posición feminista exige afirmar alto y claro que no hay emancipación posible sin la liberación de Palestina.


¿De qué liberación habla el feminismo blanco hegemónico?


Ante la historia milenaria de Palestina 

1

 y los procesos de colonización, despojo y genocidio que la atraviesan, no debería ser necesario explicar por qué la liberación palestina es una cuestión feminista. Sin embargo, junto al apoyo sostenido por amplios sectores de los feminismos anticoloniales y populares en Abya Yala, Irak, Irán, Sudáfrica, el mundo árabe, Estados Unidos y múltiples naciones y territorios europeos, la falta de apoyo y solidaridad de determinados posicionamientos feministas con la lucha palestina remite a profundos y nada nuevos 

problemas

 en el terreno de los feminismos. Desde nuestras diversas configuraciones y posicionamientos en las redes y sistemas de poder y de dominación, ciertos privilegios se traducen de forma obscena en la defensa del 

derecho de Israel a defenderse

. A esta obscenidad se suman las posturas equidistantes de quienes comparan la violencia de 

ambos lados

, como si el terrorismo de Estado, la colonización y la limpieza étnica fueran lo mismo que el derecho de un pueblo a resistir y defenderse. Como señala Alkarama, el silencio de numerosas voces feministas globales no solo produce dolor, sino que reproduce desigualdades coloniales: “Cuando el sufrimiento de una mujer palestina se vuelve 

complicado

, c

ontrovertido

 o 

no prioritario

, lo que se está diciendo –sin decirlo– es que su vida vale menos” (Alkarama, 2025b).


El feminismo se ha caracterizado históricamente como un movimiento de liberación de las mujeres. El debate en torno a quién cuenta como 

mujeres

 y qué significa 

liberación

queer

author: CMI Argentina
title: Protesta en el Congreso: la resistencia popular enfrentó más de tres horas de represión que dejó 1500 heridos y 29 detenidos
content:
El jueves 6 de agosto, una masiva movilización contra la ley de extranjerización de tierras no solo desafió el mal tiempo y la estrategia comunicacional del Gobierno, sino que enfrentó el operativo represivo más extenso de la gestión de Javier Milei. Durante más de tres horas, un despliegue conjunto de fuerzas federales y de la Policía de la Ciudad avanzó en múltiples frentes. En esta nota repasamos los puntos donde se concentró la represión: el inicio en Bartolomé Mitre y Callao con gases lacrimógenos; el avance sobre la protesta en plaza Congreso; el caótico operativo por Avenida de Mayo y sus intersecciones hasta llegar a la 9 de Julio y luego, a la Plaza de Mayo, con efectivos embistiendo desde los costados para acorralar a los manifestantes. El saldo oficial arroja 29 detenidos – ya liberados – y organismos como la CPM registraron al menos 1500 heridos, con casos de traumatismos de cráneo y lesiones oculares por balas de goma.

Una convocatoria masiva pese a todo


La masividad de la protesta es un hecho inapelable.

La concurrencia colmó la plaza del Congreso pese a las tormentas que asomaron desde temprano

 (ver nuestra cobertura de la marcha)

. A esto se suma que el Gobierno había bajado el día anterior la parte de la ley que más resonancia tuvo en los medios de comunicación, los cuales, una vez conocida esta noticia, levantaron el dato como un triunfo para los sectores populares sin resaltar que aún quedaban artículos sustanciales, como el articulado de quema de tierras y desalojos, temas que son muy caros para las comunidades que sostienen recursos naturales, los territorios de pueblos originarios, campesinos y de quienes pagan un alquiler. Pese a todos esos factores, la plaza del jueves se colmó, incluso con la siempre latente amenaza de represión y la fuerte tormenta mediante.


El operativo represivo


El operativo de seguridad fue el habitual para este tipo de movilizaciones en el Congreso: participaron las cuatro fuerzas federales (PSA, PFA, Gendarmería y Prefectura), con la Policía de la Ciudad desplegada por fuera del perímetro de la plaza. Hacia las 17 horas, en la esquina de Bartolomé Mitre y Callao, Gendarmería inició la represión con gases lacrimógenos contra los manifestantes que se encontraban junto a las vallas. La respuesta de los presentes, que no cedieron terreno, derivó en una rápida escalada del operativo: se sumaron balas de goma y el agua a presión de los camiones hidrantes.

title: MP George Aslan: A lasting peace would encourage more Syriacs to return home
content:
The public debate over the Framework Law, which is widely seen as the first step the state is expected to take under the Peace and Democratic Society Process launched by Abdullah Öcalan on February 27, 2025, continues.


George Aslan, a member of parliament for the DEM Party, shared his views with ANF on how the Syriac community views both the process and the proposed legislation.


“Syriacs are among the peoples most affected by the conflict”


Aslan said that the Syriac community has been among the peoples most severely affected by the nearly four decades of conflict.


“When the conflict began, the Syriacs were left with two choices: either take up arms on behalf of the state and become village guards, or leave their homes.


They refused to arm themselves or become a party to the conflict. As a result, they were forced to abandon the homeland where they had lived for thousands of years. During the years of conflict, around 50 Syriacs fell victim to unsolved political killings.


During the first and second peace processes, part of the community once again turned its attention toward their homeland. Although those processes did not generate widespread enthusiasm, some people did return to the country. In the 2000s, this return process accelerated further. At that time, first the Ecevit government and later the AKP government called on our people to return. Some responded to those appeals. Especially over the past three years, many previously abandoned villages have come back to life as more people have returned.”


“Some statements raised concerns among Syriacs”


Aslan continued: “To be honest, some of the statements made at the outset of this process raised concerns within the Syriac community. In particular, the emphasis by Mr. Öcalan and some politicians on religious brotherhood and on ‘a thousand years of Turkish-Kurdish brotherhood’ caused unease among Syriacs. Likewise, when President Erdoğan spoke of Turkish-Kurdish-Arab brotherhood, those concerns grew even stronger. Many people began asking themselves:

‘

As in the past, will this Islamic-based unity once again come at our expense?’ We subsequently conveyed these concerns of the Syriac community to the relevant parties.”


“If the process succeeds, Syriacs will return to their ancestral lands”


George Aslan said that the Syriac community is closely following the process and believes that, if it succeeds and results in a lasting peace, more Syriacs living in exile will return home.


“The Syriac community is following this process very closely. At every public meeting I attended in various European countries, this issue came up. They shared the same concerns expressed by many Kurds. What they told me was:

‘

They will deceive you. We do not believe they are genuinely committed to peace.’


If the process is successfully completed and leads to a lasting peace, then I believe that, just as people once left their homeland in large groups, Syriacs will increasingly return to their ancestral lands in large numbers as well.”

title: Serok Barzanî pêşwaziyê li Parlamenterekî Almanyayê kir
content:
Roja Yekşemê 9ê Tebaxa 2026an li Pîrmamê Serok Mesûd Barzanî pêşwaziyê li birêz Serdar Yuksel endamê Parlementoya Almanyayê kir. Di hevdîtinê de Serok Barzanî bi germî bixêrhatina birêz Serdar Yuksel kir û kêfxweşiya xwe anî ziman ku ciwanekî Kurd kariye di navendên siyasî û parlementoyî yên Almanyayê de rolek hebe û destxweşî li hewl û keda wî ya di warên curbecur de û di parastina doza Kurd û penaberan li Almanyayê de kir. Her wiha digel balkişandina li ser bingeh û prensîbên xebata rizgarîxwaziya gelê Kurdistanê, tekez li ser aştîxwazbûna doza gelê Kurdistanê kir ku divê pirsgirêka gelê Kurdistanê li Rojhilata Navîn bi rêya aştî û diyalogê û bi awayekî serdemiyane bê çareserkirin. Her di wê hevdîtinê de birêz Serdar Yuksel rûmeta xwe ji bo rola dîrokî ya Serok Barzanî di azadîxwazî û xebata gelê Kurdistanê de û her wiha di şerê terorê û piştgirîkirina doza Kurd li Rojava de hebû, wê yekê jî xiste holê ku li Almanyayê û gelek cihên din ên cîhanê de xelk hene ku dost û piştgîr û hevxemê maf û daxwaziyên gelê Kurdistanê ne. Birêz Serdar Yuksel ezmûna Herêma Kurdistanê bilind û bi bihadar nirxand ku pêwîste piştgirî lê bê kirin. Her wiha rûmeta xwe ji bo rola Dezgeha Xêrxwaziya Barzanî jî hebû di alîkarî û hevkariya lêqewimiyan û koçber û penaberan de. Rewşa siyasî û dawî guhertinên li ser asta navçeyê û gefa terorê mijarên din ên wê hevdîtinê bûn.

title: The cost of visibility Nathalie Chi
content:
Protests against the Chinese mega-embassy in London. Credit: Monkey Butler Images F ace covered, recognisable features hidden. A back-up phone in hand, location services disabled. No recent travel plans. No recent contact with family members in Tibet. Avoid cameras. Avoid interviews. At political protests against the Chinese government, including recent demonstrations against the planned Chinese mega-embassy in London, some Tibetan participants arrive with these calculations already made. Not everyone takes the same precautions, but everyone understands the necessity. Visibility travels, particularly for Tibetans. A single photograph, name, or online post can instantly cross borders, reaching far beyond the crowd standing on a London street. This landscape of fear has recently gained a physical anchor. In January 2026, the UK government approved China’s plan to redevelop the Royal Mint Court in central London into its largest diplomatic mission in Europe. The plan has faced sustained opposition from local residents, campaign groups, and politicians, who have raised concerns over national security, surveillance, protest safety, and the impact on surrounding areas. author: groundxero
title: উচ্ছেদের মুখে দাঁড়িয়ে প্রতিরোধের প্রাচীর তুলছেন ঢাকুরিয়ার বস্তির বাসিন্দারা
content:
দক্ষিণ কলকাতার ঢাকুরিয়া ব্রিজের নীচের বস্তির বাসিন্দাদের। গত ১২ দিন ধরে তারা উচ্ছেদ নোটিসের বিরূদ্ধে আইনি ও সামাজিক প্রতিরোধ গড়ে তুলেছেন। মাথার ওপর ছাদ হারানোর আশঙ্কা নিয়ে তাঁরা এক অনিশ্চিত ভবিষ্যতের সামনে এসে দাঁড়িয়েছেন।


 


সুদর্শনা চক্রবর্তীর

প্রতিবেদন


 


“বিজেপি-কে ভোট দিয়েছিলাম তো আমরা সবাই। কিন্তু তারাই বুলডোজার চালাবে আমাদের ঘরে বুঝতে পারিনি।”


 


“আমাদের দেশের বাড়ি তো অনেক দূর, সেই পাথরপ্রতিমা। ওখান থেকে কাজে আসব কী করে! তাই তো এখানে ঘর করে থাকি।”


 


“আমরাই তো খেটে খাই। বেশির ভাগ বাড়ির ছেলেরা তো তেমন কাজ করে না। না খাটলে খাব কি? এখন তো টেনশনে রাতের ঘুম চলে গেছে।”


 


“বাবুর বাড়িতে বলছে, তোমরা গরীব মানুষ, কী করবে! তোমরা চলে গেলে আমাদের অসুবিধা হবে। তোমরা আসো বলে আমাদের ঘর পরিষ্কার হয়, রান্না হয় তোমাদের জন্যই তো চলে আমাদের। সরকারকে বলো তোমাদের এখানে একটা জায়গা দিতে, যাতে আমাদের বাড়িতে কাজে আসতে পারো।”


  


প্রায় ৩০০ জন মানুষ গৃহহীন হওয়ার আশঙ্কায় রাত কাটাচ্ছেন। ৪৩টি পরিবার। কারোওর জন্ম বেড়ে ওঠা এখানেই, কারোর পাশের জেলাতেই বাড়ি থাকলেও কাজের জন্য এখানেই রয়ে গেছেন বছরের পর বছর। দূর থেকে কোলকাতা এসে কাজ করা সম্ভব নয় এই শ্রমজীবী মানুষদের। আর তাঁদের মধ্যে অধিকাংশ শ্রমজীবীই মহিলা। দুশ্চিন্তা তাঁদেরই সবচেয়ে বেশি। তাই প্রতিবাদে, প্রতিরোধে পথে নেমেছেন, অবস্থাবন করছেন তাঁরাই।


 


রত্না পড়ুয়া বলছিলেন,


“এত টেনশন, চাপের মধ্যে আছি যে কিছুই মনে থাকছে না। আমরা মেয়েরা বাবুদের বাড়ি কাজ করে এসে এখানে বসছি। আমরা আশা রাখছি ১০ তারিখ একটা সুখবর পাব। প্রশাসন তো আমাদের সঙ্গে থাকছে না। এত দিদিরা, সংগঠন আমাদের পাশে এসে দাঁড়াচ্ছেন, ভালো কিছু হবে না, বলুন?”


এই চিত্র দক্ষিণ কলকাতার ঢাকুরিয়া ব্রিজের নীচের ৩২ নম্বর পঞ্চানন তলা বস্তির বাসিন্দাদের। গত ১২ দিন ধরে তারা রাজ্য সরকারের কাছ থেকে প্রাপ্ত উচ্ছেদ নোটিসের বিরূদ্ধে প্রতিরোধে আইনি ও সামাজিক প্রতিরোধ গড়ে তুলেছেন। বহু অনুরোধ ও চেষ্টা সত্ত্বেও দেখা হয়নি নগর উন্নয়ন দপ্তরের ভারপ্রাপ্ত মন্ত্রী অগ্নিমিত্রা পাল, এলাকার বিধায়ক স্বপন দাশগুপ্ত কারোর সঙ্গেই। কলকাতা কর্পোরেশন-এর মেয়র পদত্যাগ করায় এই মুহূর্তে সরকারিভাবে সেখান থেকেও কোনোও সহায়তা মেলেনি। এই পরিস্থিতিতে জোটবদ্ধ আন্দোলন ও বিভিন্ন শ্রমজীবী সংগঠনের মঞ্চ যোগদানের ফলেই উচ্ছেদ রোখার চেষ্টা করছেন এই বস্তির বাসিন্দারা। এর পাশাপাশি হাইকোর্টে মামলাও দায়ের করেছেন। যার রায় বেরোনো ১০ অগাস্ট।


 


 


৩৫ বছর এই বস্তিতে রয়েছেন হীরা কয়াল। আচমকা এই নোটিস পেয়ে বিপর্যস্ত হয়ে পড়েছেন,


“আমরা তো ভয় পাচ্ছি, আমরা কোথায় চলে গিয়ে কী করব! আমাদের কোনোও জায়গা নেই, ঠাঁই নেই। কোনোও সামর্থ্য নেই যে কোথাও গিয়ে ভাড়া বাড়িতে থাকব। সেখানে ৫০০০ টাকা ভাড়া, ১০০০০ টাকা ডিপজিট। কোথা থেকে দেব? আমাদের স্বামীরা সেভাবে খাটতে পারে না। আমরা খাটতে পারলে, লোকের বাড়ি কাজ করতে পারলে খায়। আমরা ১০০০০ টাকা মাইনেই পাই হয়তো কোনো রকমে। আমাদের তুলে দিয়ে কোথায় গিয়ে থাকব? ১০ তারিখ কী রায় দেবে তাই নিয়ে খুব টেনশন হচ্ছে মাথার ভেতর। যবে থেকে নোটিস এসেছে আমাদের ঘুম নেই, খাওয়া নেই, বাড়িতে সবাই ভয়ে শুকিয়ে যাচ্ছে। নতুন সরকারের কাছে এমন আশা করিনি। সবাই ভেবেছিলাম দেখা যাক এই সরকার এসে আমাদের কী হেল্প করে। কিন্তু আসামাত্রই যে এভাবে ঝাঁটা মারবে বুঝতে পারিনি।”


এই বস্তির বাসিন্দাদের সকলেই বলছেন, কেউই বুঝতে পারেননি, আচমকা এভাবে তুলে দেওয়ার খবর আসতে পারে। পাশের দক্ষিণ ২৪ পরগণা জেলার প্রত্যন্ত গ্রামে, সুন্দরবনে বসত থাকলেও, সেখান থেকে প্রতিদিন কাজে আসা তাঁদের পক্ষে সম্ভবই নয়।


 


এই বস্তিতে যাঁরা থাকেন তাঁদের মধ্যে বেশিরভাগ মহিলাই সংলগ্ন এলাকায় গৃহ পরিচারিকার কাজ করেন এবং সেই সূত্রে পশ্চিমবঙ্গ গৃহ পরিচারিকা সমিতির সদস্য। তাঁরা যোগাযোগ করায় এই সমিতি উচ্ছেদ বিরোধী আন্দোলনে সক্রিয় ভূমিকা নিয়েছে। এই উচ্ছেদের বিরোধীতায় আন্দোলনের সঙ্গে রয়েছেন সমিতির নেত্রী স্বপ্না ত্রিপাঠি।


 


যেভাবে এই উচ্ছেদ প্রক্রিয়া শুরু হয়, আন্দোলন শুরু হয়ে এগোচ্ছে তা অনেকটা এইরকম –


 


গত ২৭ জুন প্রথম ৩২ নম্বর পঞ্চানন তলা বস্তিতে উচ্ছেদের নোটিস পাঠানো হয়। তার আগে ঢাকুরিয়া ব্রিজের তলার দুই দিকে ৯০ ও ৯২ নম্বর ওয়ার্ডে কর্পোরেশন থেকে এনকোয়ারি, ছবি তোলা, তালিকা তৈরি করা হয়। নোটিস পাওয়র পর সদস্যরা সমিতির সঙ্গে যোগাযোগ করেন। আলোচনার পর সর্বসম্মতিক্রমে সিদ্ধান্ত নেওয়া হয় যে আন্দোলনের পথেই হাঁটা হবে। ইতিমিধ্যে ২৭ জুনের নোটিস বস্তিতে সার্ভ করা হয় ২৯ জুন। বলা হয় ৩ জুলাইয়ের মধ্যে তাঁদের উঠে যেতে হবে।


 


এরপরেই তাঁরা দেখা করেন বোরো ৮-এর এক্সিকিউটিভ ইঞ্চিনিয়ার-এর সঙ্গে। তিনি সরাসরি জানান কলকাতা কমিশনার-এর কাছ থেকে নির্দেশ আসায় কিছুই করার নেই। কমিশনারের সঙ্গে তাঁরা দেখা করতে পারেননি। এলাকার চেয়ারম্যান ও কাউন্সিলার-এর সঙ্গেও তাঁদের দেখা হয়নি যেহেতু মেয়র-এর পদত্যাগের পর এই পদ্গুলি নিষ্ক্রিয় হয়ে পড়েছে। পদাধিকারী কারোওর সঙ্গে দেখা না হওয়ায় এরপরেই তাঁরা সিদ্ধান্ত নেন কোর্টে যাওয়ার ও ১ তারিখ কোর্টে যান।


 


তাঁদের উদ্দেশ্য ছিল যাতে ৩ তারিখের উচ্ছেদ আটকানো যায়। যদিও তাঁরা ১ তারিখ ডেট পাননি, ২ তারিখ লিস্টেড হলেও সেদিন তাঁদের শুনানি হয়নি। এরপরেই তাঁদের তরফে আইনজীবী পুলিস কমিশনার, কলকাতা কর্পোরেশন-এর কমিশনার, বোরো ৮-এর এক্সিকিউটিভ …

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Balik-Tanaw | Manatili sa katuruan ni Hesus
content:
1 Kings 19:9a, 11-13a Psalm 85:9, 10, 11-12, 13-14 Romans 9:1-5 Matthew 14:22-33

Noong State of the Nation Address (SONA), nagkaroon ako ng pagkakataong makinig kasama ang isang pamilyang naging kaibigan ko sa Payatas. Nasa gitna ng kanilang munting tahanan ang telebisyon—isang espasyong nagsisilbing sala, silid-tulugan, at lugar ng kanilang maliit na kabuhayan. Habang nagsasalita ang Pangulo, hindi lamang ang kanyang mga salita ang aking pinakikinggan; higit kong pinagmamasdan ang katahimikan at mga reaksyon ng pamilyang iyon. Gusto kong maramdaman kung paano tumatagos sa kanilang buhay ang mga ipinapangakong pagbabago.

Habang tumatagal ang SONA, tila maraming multo ang lumilitaw. Mga multo ng katiwalian, korapsyon, kahirapan, kawalang-katarungan, at pagkakahati-hati. Marahil nakakatakot ang mga multong ito sapagkat marami sa mga ipinagmamalaking hakbang ay hindi pa rin tunay na nararamdaman ng mga mahihirap. Ang ating bansa ay tila nasa gitna ng mga multong ito. Ngunit bilang mga Kristiyano, ang paanyaya ay hindi lamang ang manatiling nananalig kay Kristo kundi ang maging mukha ni Kristo sa gitna ng mga ito—ang patuloy na makita ang Diyos sa gitna ng nagbabanggaang kapangyarihan at manatiling umaasa kahit sa gitna ng matinding pagkadismaya.

Pagkatapos ng SONA, napatahimik kaming lahat. Walang nagsalita. Ang katahimikang iyon ang nagpaalala sa akin ng unang pagbasa. Hindi natagpuan ni Propeta Elias ang Diyos sa malakas na hangin, sa lindol, o sa apoy. Natagpuan niya ang Diyos sa banayad na tinig ng katahimikan.

Marahil ganoon din ngayon. Hindi natin laging matatagpuan ang Diyos sa malalakas na talumpati, sa ingay ng politika, o sa sigawan ng mga makapangyarihan. Naroroon Siya sa katahimikan ng mga dukhang naghahanap ng sagot sa kanilang mga tanong. Naroroon Siya sa buntong-hininga ng mga magulang na nag-iisip kung saan kukuha ng pagkain kinabukasan. Naroroon Siya sa mga pusong marunong huminto, magnilay, at makaramdam ng sakit ng lipunan habang patuloy na naghahangad ng tunay na pagbabago.

Ito rin ang dahilan kung bakit dinudumog si Hesus sa Ebanghelyo. Nauunawaan Niya ang hikbi ng mga dukha at ang kanilang pananabik sa isang makatarungang bukas. Hindi lamang Niya sila binigyan ng pahinga at kapayapaan; ginising din Niya ang kanilang kamalayan. Tinuruan Niya silang mangarap at makibahagi sa pagtatayo ng isang lipunang mas makatarungan at mas makatao.

Matapos ang katahimikan ng SONA, isa-isang lumabas ang aming mga saloobin. Marami ang nadismaya. Mahirap ngang hindi madismaya, lalo na’t ang ating bansa ay nahaharap sa iba’t ibang krisis—ang mga epekto ng digmaan sa Gitnang Silangan, mga usaping pampulitika tulad ng impeachment, patuloy na korapsyon, at lumalalim na pagkakahati-hati ng lipunan. Sa gitna ng lahat ng ito, ang higit na naaapektuhan ay ang mga mahihirap.

Sa ikalawang pagbasa, ipinakita ni San Pablo ang kanyang matinding dalamhati para sa kanyang mga kababayan. Nadismaya siya, ngunit hindi siya nagpadaig sa pagkadismaya. Nanatili siyang nakaugat kay Kristo. Iyan ang paalala sa atin: ang pagkadismaya ay hindi dapat maging dahilan upang tayo’y manahimik o mawalan ng pag-asa. Sa halip, dapat itong maging hamon upang lalo nating samahan ang mga pamayanan, gisingin ang kanilang kamalayan, at tulungan silang huwag malinlang ng mga huwad na pangako. Sa panahong laganap ang kahirapan at kawalang-katarungan, napakadaling piliin ang pananahimik at kawalang-kibo.

Kung ayaw nating habang-buhay na mabuhay sa takot sa mga multo ng ating lipunan, kailangan nating manatili kay Hesus. Siya ang nagtagumpay laban sa kasamaan, sa kawalang-katarungan, at maging sa kamatayan. Siya ang ating lakas upang huwag magpalamon sa takot at pagkadismaya, kundi maging mga saksi ng pag-asa, katarungan, at kapayapaan sa gitna ng mundong puno pa rin ng mga multo.

Balik-Tanaw is a group blog of Promotion of Church People’s Response. The Lectionary Gospel reflection is an invitation for meditation, contemplation, and action. As we nurture our faith by committing ourselves to journey with the people, we also wish to nourish the perspective coming from the point of view of hope and struggle of the people. It is our constant longing that even as crisis intensifies, the faithful will continue to strengthen their commitment to love God and our neighbor by being one with the people in their dreams and aspirations. author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Free but out of reach? The long wait for public mental health services
content:
Jem Curtny Narboneta, a BS psychology student, participates in the poster-making contest during Psychology Week celebration. Photo courtesy of Jem Curtny Narboneta.

“The biological aspect includes medicines and genetics,” Del Valle said. “But psychosocial factors—the social determinants of health—also affect us. If we improve education, if people have jobs, and communities can support them, these all contribute to mental health.”

Trigger warning: Mentions of suicide

By Kasheena Camacho Bulatlat.com

MANILA —  For Filipinos experiencing mental health crises, long waiting periods for free mental health consultations continue to hinder their access to care, forcing some of them to seek costly private treatment.

For March Lavela, 24, deciding to seek professional help came after months of grief, mounting family responsibilities, and worsening panic attacks. “The turning point for me was when the pressure built up so much that my body couldn’t handle it anymore,” Lavela said.

He said the panic attacks began during online thesis classes, where repeated confrontations with a professor became overwhelming. The anxiety persisted even outside the classroom, with merely hearing the professor’s name triggering panic.

“I knew it was time to ask for help when I started thinking about death and killing myself,” he said. “…[R]ealizing my mind was going to that dark place made me see that I couldn’t fight this on my own anymore.”

Unable to afford private psychiatric consultations, Lavela sought free mental health services. He booked consultations with both the Philippine General Hospital (PGH) and the National Center for Mental Health (NCMH). The available schedules, however, were months away.

“I decided to just walk in at NCMH because I knew I couldn’t wait for a far-off online appointment date,” he said. “I felt like if I waited that long, I might already be gone.”

At the NCMH, he disclosed to hospital personnel that he had been experiencing suicidal thoughts. “They assisted me through the whole process once I walked into the hospital,” he said.

Lavela’s experience mirrors a broader challenge confronting the country’s mental healthcare system.

Jem Curtny B. Narboneta, 21, also agonized over the waiting period to access care.

Narboneta, a psychology student, said she initially spent around P11,000 ($181) on several online psychological consultation platforms in search of answers.

She also contacted around 15 to 20 emergency hotlines she found online but said none responded.

Her mother later accompanied her to NCMH for free consultation. Instead of receiving immediate care, they were advised to secure an online appointment. Narboneta said the earliest available schedule was nearly a year away.

“Obviously I couldn’t wait that long because I’d be long gone if I were to wait a year,” she said.

Unable to wait, she then sought consultation with a private psychiatric facility despite the additional cost.

“It greatly affected my well-being because I needed mental health consultation that time,” she said. “To find out I had to wait a year made me think of all the people who finally mustered the courage to seek help only to discover mental health services weren’t as accessible as they thought.”

Lavela and Narboneta are among the thousands of Filipinos seeking professional mental health services in the past years.

In an online interview with Bulatlat , Dr. Teresa Rosalie D. del Valle, a medical specialist IV at the NCMH, said that consultations have increased significantly in recent years.

“The pandemic heightened public awareness of mental health,” Del Valle said.

The increase in demand, however, has outpaced the country’s available mental health workforce, according to both Del Valle and international data.

According to the World Health Organization’s Mental Health Atlas 2024 , the Philippines has only 3.9 mental health workers for every 100,000 population, including 0.2 psychiatrists, 0.3 psychologists, 0.7 mental health nurses, 1.1 social workers, and 1.6 other mental health workers per 100,000 population.

The report also recorded one specialized mental hospital, 22 psychiatric units in general hospitals, and 1,362 community-based outpatient mental health facilities nationwide.

Del Valle said the current number of psychiatrists remains insufficient to keep up with the growing number of patients seeking care.

author: Brian Hioe
title: 科爾比的推文發飆事件，顯示出川普政府既想建立帝國，又想坐享其成
content:
川普政府戰爭部次長埃爾布里奇·科爾比（Elbridge Colby）近期在推特上發表了一系列 推文 ，猛烈抨擊「中等強權」將取代美國主導地位的說法。科爾比聲稱：「我們（戰爭部）並不擔心這會成為一種嚴重的可能性。相反地，我們更擔心少數盟友和夥伴會『認為這是可能的』，並因此將寶貴的時間、金錢和政治資本浪費在這種分散注意力的事情上。」

事實上，科爾比竟認為有必要耗費如此多篇幅試圖反駁此觀點，似乎證明了相反的情況，即科爾比確實認為此觀點具有威脅性或令人惱火。科爾比聲稱，「中等強權」缺乏形成聯盟的連貫基礎，且認為其盟友與美國的互動正日益加深，而非減弱。

科爾比接著大肆宣揚美國的卓越能力。他表示： 「說白了，實際情況就是，無論在數量或品質上，都沒有任何其他國家或國家集團能與美國的國防工業基礎抗衡。正如總統所言，美國製造的裝備最為精良，且我們的生產規模是任何可信的競爭對手都無法匹敵的。若說有什麼不同，那就是能夠對接美國國防工業基礎（DIB）是一種特權，而非權利 […] 在自由世界中，沒有任何可信的替代方案能取代美國技術及其對國防的深遠影響。」

科爾比的推文被各界解讀為美國在發脾氣。畢竟，科爾比一直試圖透過威脅撤回美國的支持，來敦促歐洲盟友挺身而出，為自身的防禦多盡一份力。既然事情已發展至此，美國或許正因盟友逐漸疏遠而感到不滿。

從這個角度來看，科爾比此舉無異於強烈抨擊「美國主導的全球秩序仍站得住腳」這一觀念。自加拿大總理馬克・卡尼在達沃斯世界經濟論壇發表 演說 後，「中等強國」應擔起更多責任的觀念已在國際社會獲得高度重視。

當然，對抗兩大超級大國主導的全球秩序而另結成聯盟的想法，在歷史上早有先例，例如「不結盟運動」或「南南 合作 」等概念。當美中兩極對峙時，世界日益呈現出多極格局之際，這種想法再度浮現，或許並不令人意外。如果科爾比認為，在某些人稱為「新冷戰」的時代，這種理念的再度浮現缺乏連貫的依據，那他似乎對歷史相當無知——儘管當然，卡尼所提出的「中等強國」結盟，仍是一種對西方主導的全球秩序的重新配置，這點與不結盟運動有所不同。

與此同時，科爾比或許正試圖兼得魚與熊掌，既要保有自己的帝國，又不願承擔責任。鑑於美國不願履行維繫其帝國的承諾，科爾比的推文正反映出美國如今正抱怨其帝國正逐漸瓦解。

然而，人們也注意到，美國已拋棄了任何以「軟實力」作為文化與政治霸權基礎的做法。取而代之的是，美國轉而對其盟友施加直接的脅迫。但或許，一個帝國若缺乏某種軟實力元素——無論是以基於規則的國際秩序、共同的民主價值觀、對資本主義自由市場的遵循，或其他形式呈現——便根本無法維繫其統一。事實上，軟實力能向從屬於霸權大國的勢力提供保證，該霸權不會施加超出隱含範圍之外的強制手段。正如西奧多・羅斯福所言，關鍵在於「說話溫和，手握大棒」，藉此促使在自身主導下形成的政治秩序得以凝聚為一體。

相較之下，科爾比似乎一心只想揮舞「大棒」，高聲威脅要懲罰任何反抗行為。對於那些覺得此舉構成威脅的大國來說，試圖尋求替代方案，而非屈從於一個對自身全球秩序根基幾乎一無所知、且反覆多變的霸權國家，這難道令人意外嗎？

看來科爾比似乎一心想要削弱美國的實力，或許他從一開始就根本不明白其中的運作機制。同樣地，人們不難發現，這系列推文無非是為中國等競爭對手提供了攻擊美國的彈藥。畢竟，若沒有任何「中等強權」聯盟崛起以同時制衡美國與中國，便會有國家直接轉向中國，將其視為美國的替代選項。又或者，正如不結盟運動當年所發生的一樣，中國將自行宣稱領導中等國。不過，對於川普政府成員而言，這種無知倒也不足為奇。

author: rti_admin
title: Does Ambedkar Posthumously Have a ‘Homeland’?
content:
In August 1931, during his first formal meeting with Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi at Mani Bhavan in Bombay, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar made a declaration that fundamentally shattered the nationalist illusion of a unified anti-colonial front: “Gandhiji, I have no homeland.” To grasp the profound weight of this statement, one must first interrogate what it truly means to call a place a “homeland.” A homeland is not merely a geographic expanse bounded by political borders, nor is it defined simply by possessing a passport or a constitutional territory. A homeland is a space of radical belonging—a site where an individual can exist freely, with uncompromised dignity and fundamental liberty. In his autobiography, Nelson Mandela captured this primal essence of freedom when he wrote: “I was not born with a hunger to be free. I was born free—free in every way that I could know. Free to run in the fields near my mother’s hut, free to swim in the clear stream that ran through my village, free to roast mealies under the stars and ride the broad backs of slow-moving bulls.” For Mandela, as for any human being, a true homeland is a place where freedom is the natural baseline of existence.

At a time when anti-colonial dissent was at its peak, Ambedkar’s blunt denial of the undisputed leader of the independence struggle was an act of extreme political honesty. It laid bare his genuine sense of alienation on behalf of his people. How could a man claim a homeland in a nation that systematically denied his basic human dignity? For the Untouchables, the daily tyranny of caste Hindu society—expressed through forced segregation, denial of public water, physical violence, and systemic humiliation—was far more immediate, brutal, and historically entrenched than British colonial rule. Ambedkar recognized that while Gandhi fought against British colonialism, the upper-caste leadership was eager to preserve its internal feudal empire. To declare to Gandhi that a country built on social injustice is a prison for its most oppressed people, not a homeland, was an act of profound refusal.

Today, as youth-led demonstrations at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar—organized by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over widespread NEET paper leaks and national examination irregularities—draw thousands of marchers, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and his companions carry “a photo of Dr. Bhim Rao Ambedkar, M.K. Gandhi, and a copy of the Indian Constitution” to ensure their protests remain peaceful. As mainstream civil society, student unions, and GenZ youth movements routinely frame Gandhi and Ambedkar side-by-side as twin patrons of democratic dissent, an urgent Ambedkarite critique demands to be posed: Has post-colonial India posthumously constructed a “home” for Ambedkar by diluting his radical anti-caste framework into a sanitized, state-sanctioned icon, paired with the very ideology he spent his life dismantling?

It is widely assumed today that Ambedkar eventually found his “home” in the post-colonial Indian Republic. The dominant narrative holds that the drafting of the Constitution, the formal abolition of untouchability under Article 17, and his elevation to national icon status granted him and his people the homeland he was denied in 1931. However, we must critically interrogate the difference between the “home” Ambedkar spoke of then and the “home” offered to his people now. The homeland Ambedkar envisioned was not merely a territorial entity with a flag and a legal code. It was a true social democracy anchored in pratitya-samutpada (interconnectedness), liberty, equality, and fraternity. It was a home where the annihilation of caste restored moral community, dignity, and real political agency to the depressed classes. What the post-colonial Indian state offers instead is a structural illusion: a constitutional home on paper, accompanied by an unchanged Brahminical social order in practice. The state eagerly claims Ambedkar as the “Father of the Constitution” to validate its democratic credentials globally, yet actively strips his memory of its radical, anti-caste methodology.

To claim that Ambedkar or Dalits have found a home in modern India is to ignore their daily lived reality deliberately. Are Dalits no longer facing discrimination? The empirical reality tells a devastating story. The “home” constructed by the modern nation-state remains a site of ongoing, systemic violence for Dalits. Untouchability has not vanished; it has merely adapted to modernity. When a Dalit …

author: Benjamin Cordero
title: Ang Paglalayag sa Kawalan: Isang Pagsusuri sa The Odyssey (2026)
content:
Isang dambuhalang tagumpay sa sining ng pelikula ang The Odyssey (2026) ni Christopher Nolan. Bagaman napakamahal na ng halaga ng sine sa kasalukuyang panahon, isa itong biswal na hiyas na nararapat panoorin sa pinakamalaking telon hangga’t maaari. Ngunit sa ilalim ng nagngangalit na alon ng Dagat Mediteranyo o sa sindak na dulot ng Cyclops o sa bigat ng modernong pagganap na dala ni Matt Damon, may kuwentong pumipintig sa isang napakapamilyar na paraan.

Ang panonood ng The Odyssey sa pamamagitan ng matang Pilipino ay parang nakararanas ng matinding déjà vu . Para sa isang kulturang hinubog ng pangingibang-bansa, walang-katapusang pagtitiis, at pagkakawatak-watak ng pamilya, ang sampung taong pakikipagsapalaran ni Odysseus para lang makauwi ay hindi lang kuwento ng mitolohiyang Griyego—ito mismo ang buhay at kalagayan ng modernong Pilipino.

Ang pinakamabilis at pinakamatinding koneksyon ng pelikula ni Nolan sa buhay-Pilipino ay ang karakter mismo ni Odysseus. Siya ay isang lalaking nakakulong sa isang walang-awa at nakapapagod na pagpapatapon sa sarili. Sa pelikula, mariing ipinakita ni Nolan ang sikolohikal na epekto ng pagkakahiwalay ni Odysseus sa kanyang bayan; hindi lang siya lumalaban sa mga halimaw, kundi lumalaban din siya sa oras, sa distansya, at sa unti-unting paglaho ng alaala ng tahanang kanyang iniwan.

Ito ang salamin ng totoong buhay ng milyun-milyong Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs), ang ating mga bagong bayani. Katulad ni Odysseus na umalis ng Ithaca para lumaban sa digmaan sa Troy para sa kanyang bayan, ang OFW ay umaalis din sa Pilipinas para lumaban sa isang digmaang pang-ekonomiko sa dayuhang lupain. Pareho silang ginagabayan ng iisang layunin: ang buhayin, protektahan, at sa huli ay balikan ang pamilyang kanilang minamahal.

Kapag nakatulala si Odysseus (Matt Damon) sa karagatan habang nakakulong sa isla ng Ogygia, sinumang Pilipinong nanonood ay makikita ang mukha ng ating mga tita, tito, ina, at ama na nagpupuyat habang nakatingin sa bintana ng mga matataas na gusali sa Hong Kong, Dubai, o Singapore. Ang mga halimaw na hinarap ni Odysseus—ang mapanlinlang na akit ni Circe o ang nakaparalisang pagkalimot na dala ng mga Lotus-Eater—ay madaling maitumbas sa mga panganib ng pangingibang-bansa ngayon: (1) Ang tuksong makiangkop nang tuluyan sa dayuhang kultura at limutin ang sariling pinagmulan. (2) Ang mabigat at mapag-isang depresyon ng pagiging dayuhan sa ibang bansa at; (3) Ang mga burukrasya, kahirapan sa bayang babalikan at pisikal na hadlang na nagpapatagal sa pag-uwi nang maraming taon, o dekada.

Habang nakikipaglaban si Odysseus sa malalaking alon, ang bigat ng emosyon ng pelikula ay pasan naman nina Penelope (Anne Hathaway) at Telemachus (Tom Holland) sa Ithaca. Mahusay na ipinakita ni Nolan na ang Ithaca ay hindi isang marangyang kaharian na naghihintay sa kanilang hari, kundi isang gumuguhong bahay na kinatatawanan ng mga mapagsamantalang manliligaw/dayuhan na unti-unting nagpapasasa sa kanilang yaman.

Ang bahaging ito ng kuwento ay napakasakit tanggapin para sa mga pamilyang Pilipino. Kapag ang isang magulang ay umalis ng Pilipinas para magtrabaho sa abroad, ang pamilyang naiwan ay parang nakabinbin sa hangin. Si Penelope ang sumasalamin sa nakatutunaw at mapag-isang dusa ng asawang naiwan—na kadalasan ay ang ina na mag-isang nagtataguyod sa bahay, nagpoprotekta sa mga anak laban sa mga mapagsamantalang tao sa lipunan, at nagkukunwaring matatag kahit na nadudurog ang puso sa tindi ng pangungulila.

Si Telemachus naman ang kumakatawan sa “anak ng OFW.” Ipinakita ni Tom Holland ang isang binatang puno ng kumplikadong emosyon—may galit, may pangungulila, at may matinding pressure. Lumaki siya sa ilalim ng anino ng isang tanyag na ama na halos hindi niya matandaan, at napilitang ipagtanggol ang kanilang tahanan bago pa siya maging handa. Sa pang-araw-araw na buhay ng Pilipino, ito ang realidad ng milyun-milyong bata na lumalaki sa pamamagitan lamang ng video calls at remittance slips. Lumalaki silang walang ama o ina sa tabi, napipilitang magmatured nang maaga, nakalantad sa nauusong karahasan (maging sa sariling paaralan) at pasan ang bigat ng sakripisyo ng magulang habang nahihirapan ding kilalanin ang sarili.

Sa kaibuturan nito, ang The Odyssey ay isang paggalugad sa konsepto ng nostos—ang sinaunang salitang Griyego para sa pagbabalik-bayan. Sa kulturang Pilipino, ito ang ating pinakamalalim na mithiin: ang konsepto ng pagbabalik o pag-uwi.

author: Kevin Lin
title: The Seven Deadly Sins of Conferencing
content:
Many of us know from experience that the most memorable and enjoyable parts of participating in a conference are the tea and coffee breaks, the conversations lunches and dinners, the informal chats outside of the conference room while the meeting is still happening, and the late-night hangouts with other participants. Genuinely good conversations take place and relationships are formed or renewed in those moments. So why don’t we recognise what is obvious, and create structures that bring out these experiences?


Social movements rely on purposeful gatherings to connect, share experiences, and strategise. We do this so often we should be really good at it. But more often than not, things do not seem to quite work. This has prompted me to reflect, and then test my impressions with other conference-goers who turn out to be feeling much the same ways. I need to first acknowledge how much unseen labour goes into any event planning; the event organisers are the most invisible if everything goes well. But it is necessary to recognise and name things that do not seem to work.


Here are the seven deadly sins of conference organising. I want to speak to my fellow conference organisers: of course, not all of us committed all of the sins, and some of you have done much better. But many of the sins would sound familiar to us, and we often let our guards down. By naming them, we may do a better job at avoiding them, and get to organise and experience more effective, creative and joyful gatherings.


 


Greed


 


The first sin is greed. We are often greedy about what can be accomplished with a gathering, especially with sizable conferences. We want to invite many people to be there to meet and connect, while also want them to have substantial discussions.


A medium to large conference of dozens to a few hundred people is amazing. But it is not primarily a place for deep learning or for substantial conversations despite our best efforts and most sincere wishes. There are simply too many sessions, too many speakers and too many people to learn and engage deeply. We listen to one panel after another and hardly remember anything from each speaker, while facilitators apologise for running out of time and no more time for questions. We then try to have conversations during breaks that on average last for 5 to 10 minutes before rushing back to the next session or talking or introducing ourselves to someone else. You should not feel alone in experiencing this.


We know deep learning and substantial conversation are most likely to take place in much smaller meetings. You may really have to keep it to a very small number of participants, arguably no more than 10 or 15 but maybe even fewer, to have sustained conversations that give everyone time to think, allow ideas to develop, and for them to build on each other’s ideas.


The medium and large conferences serve other important goals: it is good for building new relationships or renewing old ones, for feeling part of a larger movement with many others with shared values and goals, and for experiencing the optimism and joy of movement-building. It is good enough to take away with you the connections you have made, a sense of the movement’s diversity and creativity, and the fact that people are doing the best they can under enormous pressure and risk.


If these are the realistic goals, then our task is to structure the events in ways that let people and ideas to breath, to have both structured discussions and unstructured time for spontaneous conversations, and to make these events into festivals.


 


Busyness


 


The second sin is busyness. Far too often, I have been in conference planning where the logistics – the venue search and booking, the travel arrangement, the drinks, snacks and meals, and the interpretation – take up most of the planning time. We end up spending very little time discussing and experimenting with the actual program. In fact, the program design at times feels like an afterthought.


The logistics discussions and preparations are often not completely done until the very last minute. Time for a program discussion tends to be squeezed in between logistics discussions. When we are tight on time, we tend to revert to the familiar and the safest: let us get these speakers speakers for these panels, and each speaks for 15 minutes. It is the least that can go wrong. No one can claim they love this, but we keep doing it anyway.


It may be worth aiming to reserve a …

author: Rojava IC
title: Sleeper-Cell Report June 2026 – Justice Palace Department’s Head Killed
content:
The head of the Palace of Justice was seriously injured after being targeted in an attack on June 16. 


 


Key Points 


Five sleeper cell attacks were recorded in June; a slight increase from only three in May


A total of four military personnel were killed, and at least two injured 


Fatalities of two suspected ISIS affiliates were also recorded


Paper leaflets containing Pro-ISIS propaganda were distributed in several provinces throughout Syria


 


In Depth


This month, RIC recorded a total five attacks, two of which have been directly claimed by ISIS at the time of writing, the remaining three are believed to have been carried out by ISIS members.


On June 15, unidentified gunmen believed to be of an ISIS cell attacked the headquarters of general security forces, two of its members were killed and several others injured, west of Raqqa city, before one of the attackers self-detonated.  


On June 16, Salah Ahmad al-Saleh, head of the Palace of Justice in the town of Babila in rural Damascus was seriously injured by an explosive device attached to his vehicle. And on the same day, ISIS members targeted an oil tanker with machine-gun fire near the northern city of Manbij. Material damage to the tanker was reported.


On June 20, unidentified gunmen believed to be part of an ISIS cell, attacked members of the 76th Armored Division, causing the death of two Division’s members. The attack occurred near Tahnah junction in the western countryside of Manbij.


On June 24, two gunmen believed to be ISIS members, on a motorcycle opened fire on two members of the Engineering Regiment of the 72nd Division, on Ain Issa Road in Raqqa countryside, injuring both of them. 


On June 19, U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) forces conducted an airstrike in northwest Syria. CENTCOM confirmed the killing of Ali Husayn al-‘Ulaywi, a senior ISIS leader. 


Paper leaflets were distributed in several mosques across different areas in Daraa, Idlib and Aleppo provinces. The leaflets contain extremist content and rhetoric linked to ISIS.


Save the Children, an Australian children’s advocacy organization, called for the return of an ISIS-linked Australian woman and her disabled child from Syria after a failed repatriation attempt. Following the failed departure, Syrian authorities reportedly transferred them to a detention facility in northwestern Syria’s Idlib Governorate, since then, her family lost contact with her.


Another Australian woman was accused of supporting ISIS and appeared before a court in Melbourne, where prosecutors alleged she lived in a household that held a teenage girl in slavery while the victim was subjected to repeated abuse.  Her request for bail was rejected, as prosecutors argued she poses a risk to public safety. 


Tammy Bruce, U.S. Deputy Permanent Representative to the United Nations Ambassador said that it would continue working with Syria to combat ISIS, and support efforts to preserve stability and safety in the country.

author: Yasmine Johnson
title: Royal Commission puts pro-Palestine protesters on trial
content:
The Royal Commission into Antisemitism and Social Cohesion held a one-day hearing block on protests and policing on 4 August. Like the rest of the commission, it was more a prosecution than an inquiry: the Palestine solidarity movement was on trial, and its opponents were invited to act as judge, jury and witness. 

The commission has already been filled with unsubstantiated and unchallenged testimony from so-called lived experience witnesses, often from pro-Israel lobby organisations. It is a platform for those wishing to slander the Palestine movement as antisemitic. In this hearing block, the fix was in from the beginning. Despite nearly three years of protests involving many thousands of people, the commission declared that just two protests would be discussed: a Sydney protest on 9 October 2023 that marched to the Opera House and a Nazi rally held by the National Socialist Network outside NSW Parliament on 8 November 2025. 

The latter barely warranted a mention in the commission. It was fitting, given that one of the key, and outrageous, arguments pursued by pro-Israel organisations is that the left, rather than the far right, are the antisemites. This is in keeping with Israel’s alignment to extreme right-wing governments and parties around the world. Australia’s Special Envoy to Combat Antisemitism Jillian Segal, whose family has bankrolled far-right organisation Advance Australia, failed to put out a single statement of condemnation of the Nazi rally. The Nazis weren’t the subject of the hearing: they were props in an argument about the left. The point of including this rally was not to confront the far right, but to attempt to tarnish the Palestine movement by association. 

The main purpose of this block was to re-air the lies told about the 9 October Opera House protest, and to rake the police over the coals for “transferring control of the CBD to protesters”. The main two witnesses called were not people who had actually witnessed anything that night. One was David Ossip, president of the NSW Jewish Board of Deputies, a pro-Israel organisation. The other was the assistant commissioner of NSW Police, Peter McKenna. Not a single protester or protest organiser was invited to give evidence. Despite all this, proceedings did not go exactly as planned.

Ossip argued that the protest was “appalling” because it took place while Israeli civilians were being killed following the Hamas attack on 7 October. He apparently couldn’t understand why anyone might want to protest, given that Israel had not even begun any military operations by that time. This claim has been made several times at the commission, supposedly showing that people were not really protesting against occupation and a coming genocide, but celebrating the gruesome deaths of Israelis. The problem is that it is not true, and this was pointed out to Ossip in cross-examination by lawyers for the Palestine Action Group (PAG) and the Australian Palestine Advocacy Network (APAN). 

Prior to the attack in October, 2023 was already the deadliest year for Palestinians living in the West Bank since records began, with more than 200 killed in racist pogroms by extremist settlers and Israeli soldiers. For this reason, PAG had already organised five demonstrations by this point in 2023. 

By the evening of 7 October, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had already declared war, promising “mighty vengeance for this black day ... We will target all of Hamas's positions. We will turn Gaza into a deserted island. To the citizens of Gaza, I say. You must leave now. We will target each and every corner of the strip”. Two hundred and thirty Palestinians were killed by Israeli airstrikes on Gaza on that day alone. By 9 October, more than 400 had been killed in Gaza, a total blockade of food, water, fuel and medical supplies had been imposed, and Israel was openly preparing a ground invasion. Incredibly, when confronted with these facts, Ossip doubled down on his false claim that Israel had not commenced military operations.

The right has responded to Ossip's evidence with outrage. Not outrage that he would double down on false claims, under oath, in order to demonise a mass movement against genocide, but outrage that he could be challenged on his false claims at all. author: AWSM
title: A Community in the Cracks of Capitalism
content:
A piece of Christchurch that the property market abandoned after the earthquakes has become home to people abandoned by the property market. The old Bexley neighbourhood was largely cleared after liquefaction made conventional residential development impossible. Houses disappeared, streets remained and the land sat waiting for whatever official purpose would eventually be found for it. Into that gap came people who needed somewhere to live. They arrived in cars, vans, buses and tents. Some were working. Some were retired. Some had children. They did what people have always done when the institutions around them fail, they improvised. A community grew. Earlier this year about 40 people were living around Wetlands Grove; reports now put the number at more than 100. Christchurch City Council has told them they must leave by 28 February 2027 because the area is intended for wetland development. There is an obvious temptation to treat this as a story about homelessness, council planning or the difficulties of finding somewhere suitable for a group of people living in vehicles. It is all of those things, but underneath them sits a much simpler question. What is land for? The answer given by our economic system is that land belongs to whoever has legal title to it, and its legitimate use is determined by owners, planners and institutions. The people actually living on it remain secondary. They may sleep there, look after one another there and make the place usable through their own effort, but none of that gives them any meaningful claim to it. Their relationship to the place exists only for as long as the legal owner tolerates it. That distinction between ownership and use lies close to the heart of the anarchist criticism of private property.

The people living at Wetlands Grove have already demonstrated something that governments spend enormous amounts of money trying unsuccessfully to manufacture through policy documents – people can organise social life themselves. Earlier reporting described an informal community growing around buses, vans and cars, with neighbours helping one another through winter and a communal tent being established as shared space. One man who had been sleeping in a small tent was helped into an old car when the cold became severe. Council rubbish collection and portable toilets made conditions more bearable, but the social organisation of the place came largely from the people living there. Moko, one of the informal figures in the community, was working full-time on an on-call road crew. Others were pensioners. Ngawai Timu described abandoning a $470-a-week rental because she felt she was spending her life paying somebody else’s mortgage. Polly Stewart was surviving on the pension in a bus. Families were living there too, including a woman with several children living from a bus. These details matter because homelessness is constantly spoken about as though it were primarily a pathology of homeless people. Addiction, mental illness, poor budgeting, antisocial behaviour and bad choices are summoned as explanations because those explanations leave the social order intact. They allow us to imagine that housed people possess some quality that homeless people lack. Wetlands Grove makes that story harder to sustain. When people with jobs cannot obtain housing, when pensioners decide rent leaves too little for ordinary life, and when families find themselves competing with dozens of others for a private rental, the problem is no longer plausibly located inside the individual. There are certainly people living rough who struggle with addiction or serious psychological distress. There are also people who get up and go to work from a tent. A housing system that cannot reliably house either has failed at the most elementary level.

New Zealand has become remarkably skilled at describing this failure without challenging the institution producing it. We talk about housing supply, affordability pressures and housing need. We devise eligibility categories and waiting lists. We construct administrative pathways through emergency housing, transitional housing, community housing and social housing. Every stage acquires its own assessments and rules. The language becomes more sophisticated while people remain without homes. At the 2023 Census, Statistics New Zealand estimated that at least 112,496 people were experiencing severe housing deprivation, around 2.3 percent of the usually resident population. The …

author: Susan Price
title: Peru: Far-right Fujimori sworn in as president, amid protests
content:
Keiko Fujimori, leader of the far-right Popular Force party, was sworn in as Peru’s president on July 28, after narrowly defeating leftist candidate Roberto Sánchez in the run-off election in June.

Fujimori is the daughter of former dictator Alberto Fujimori, who imposed a United States-sponsored “shock therapy” in the 1990s, privatising public enterprises, eliminating state subsidies, further deregulating the economy and attacking labour laws.

Fujimori represents the continuation of her father’s policies and has maintained the neoliberal status quo through her party’s control of Congress since 2016 and other state institutions, such as the judiciary.

In her first address, Fujimori pledged to combat “insecurity” and has previously promised to fight crime with an “iron fist”. She said the military will take control during “states of emergency”, which have been used by successive right-wing governments to suspend freedom of assembly, movement and privacy.

The falsity of Fujimori’s supposed “anti-crime” agenda is laid bare by her and her party’s record of brazen corruption and facilitating organised crime. She was imprisoned in pre-trial detention for her role in the Odebrecht bribery scandal and for using illicit money to fund presidential campaigns. As president, she is now immune from prosecution.

Moreover, 15 of Fujimori’s 19 cabinet members have faced criminal investigations or been imprisoned for corruption, theft, fraud, embezzlement and assault. Vice President Luis Galarreta is currently under investigation for money laundering, abuse of authority and links to organised crime, while environment minister Vladimiro Huaroc has 51 investigations against him.

Fujimori’s supposed “tough-on-crime” approach also does not extend to the heinous crimes committed by the police and military when inflicting violence against Peru’s working class.

The Fujimorista-controlled Congress approved Law 32735 on July 21, which allows crimes committed by the police and military to be investigated and tried by police and military courts. Ongoing investigations and trials can now be transferred from civilian courts or stopped, including cases where police and military have already been convicted.

This adds to the widespread impunity already enjoyed by police and soldiers, who have killed at least 50 people in anti-government protests since 2022. Recently, a police officer shot and killed an eight-year-old boy in Huacho, a town about 150 kilometres north of Lima.

During her address, Fujimori lamented that Peru’s economic inequality is the highest in Latin America and pledged, in a populist move, to raise the minimum wage by 15%, to 1300 soles (A$545) a month. She knows this will have a negligible impact on big business bottom lines and workers’ living standards, in a country where more than 70% work in the informal economy, with no guaranteed minimum wage and basic work entitlements.

In many ways, Fujimori and her father are responsible for entrenching the neoliberal model that makes Peru one of the most unequal countries in the world. The top 1% control almost half (44.7%) of the country’s wealth, while the bottom 50% control just 0.1%.

Under this model, domestic and transnational corporations are granted almost free reign to pillage the country’s vast mineral deposits to make obscene profits.

Meanwhile, the concentration of the economy into monopolies and oligopolies — particularly in the agribusiness industry — results in price fixing and rising living costs. The basic family basket — the cost of basic goods and services for a family of four for a month — is more than 1860 soles ($779.29), which Fujimori’s promised wage raise covers less than 70% of.

Joining the far-right shift in governments in the region, Fujimori seeks to deepen ties with the United States and other far-right leaders in the region. Her inauguration was attended by far-right leaders, such as Chilean President José Antonio Kast and Argentine President Javier Milei.

She pledged to join US President Donald Trump’s Shield of the Americas, which aims to reassert US economic and military dominance in Latin America.

Thousands protested in the country’s capital, Lima, against Fujimori’s inauguration, rightly pointing out her role in introducing laws that facilitate crime and grant impunity to the military and police. Among the protesters were relatives of some of the thousands of people tortured, killed and disappeared under her father’s regime.
