author: Sheree Lowe
title: Our Children are the Treaty generation
content:
This

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Children’s Day

, we have an opportunity to reflect on something remarkable. 


Across Victoria, our Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children are growing up in one of the most significant political moments since colonisation. They are the first generation of children to grow up in

Victoria’s Treaty era

. Treaty is about far more than legal agreements or institutional reform. At its heart, Treaty is about people, and most importantly, our children, and our future generations. 


The true measure of any Treaty will not be found in the number of agreements reached or milestones achieved. It will be measured by whether it truly improves the lives of future generations. 


Will Aboriginal children grow up healthier? Will their identity and Connection to their Culture be strong? Will they have every opportunity to learn, thrive and lead? Will they inherit systems that recognise their strengths rather than focus on their disadvantage? 


These are the questions that really matter. 


Aboriginal children already possess extraordinary strengths. They inherit the oldest continuing culture on Earth. They are surrounded by families, Elders and Communities who pass on knowledge, stories and traditions – keeping them strong and keeping them connected to who they are. 


But despite their strengths, many Aboriginal children continue to experience inequitable outcomes across

health

, education,

incarceration

, and wellbeing. Too often, systems have been designed to exclude Aboriginal people and their families, rather than include them.  


Treaty is our chance to change this.  


Treaty allows us to shift decision-making closer to Aboriginal communities, strengthening self-determination and creating services that better reflect the aspirations, cultures and needs of Aboriginal children and families. 


This is not simply about changing policies. It is about changing possibilities. 


Imagine growing up as an Aboriginal child.

Imagine instead of growing up in a State that perpetuates stigma, stereotypes and wants to dismiss your culture in dark history books – you grow up knowing who you are, where you belong and actually understanding your Country and Culture.  


Children have the potential to grow up in a state where their Culture is not only respected but embedded throughout education, healthcare and public life.  Our collective history recognised, our languages celebrated and Community empowered to shape the services that support our families. 


Imagine knowing that decisions about your future are increasingly made by your own people, your Community.

That is the promise that Treaty represents. 


For today’s Aboriginal children, this is not some distant vision. It is unfolding right now, during their own childhood. 


They are the first generation who will remember Victoria before Treaty, and who will one day tell their own children what it was like to witness this historic transformation. 


That is both exciting and humbling, but it also places an extraordinary responsibility on all of us. 


Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Children’s Day reminds us that children are not just our future leaders – they are citizens of today. Their experiences matter. Their ideas matter. Their voices matter. 


If Treaty is truly about creating a better future, then Aboriginal children must remain at the centre of every conversation. 


Because when today’s children become tomorrow’s Elders, they will not judge this generation by the complexity of negotiations or the wording of agreements. 


They will judge us by outcomes. 


Did we create a Victoria where Aboriginal children could grow up proud of who they are? Did we ensure they remained connected to Culture, Country and Community?  Did we reduce the inequities they inherited? Did we create opportunities for every Aboriginal child and their family to flourish and thrive? 


The answers to those questions will be the enduring measure of success. 


So, this Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Children’s Day, let us recognise that our children are growing up during a defining chapter in our state’s history, and work together to ensure it’s done right.


We all must take pride in being the first Australian state to take this historic step and ensure that Treaty is not repealed after the state election. 


Because Treaty is a promise to our future generations.  


A promise that they are not simply growing up in the era of Treaty …

author: James Plested
title: ‘Ready to fight for a socialist future’: eight hundred attend Victorian Socialists’ campaign launch
content:
It was the biggest event the Victorian Socialists (VS) have put on since we formed in 2018. On Saturday, 1 August, 800 people turned out to the Aborigines Advancement League in the northern Melbourne suburb of Thornbury to help us launch our campaign for the 2026 state election. Tickets were selling so fast in the week leading up to it that we had to scramble to ensure the bigger-than-expected crowd could be properly accommodated.

It’s a long time since the socialist movement in Australia has had to deal with an issue like this, and it was hard not to feel, on the night, that something significant has changed. The evening’s compere, VS candidate for Northcote Kath Larkin, expressed the feeling in her opening remarks. “We know that this election will not be easily won”, she said, “but if tonight is anything to go by, we’ve got masses of people who are ready to fight for a socialist future”.

For decades now the numbers of people concluding that the major problems in society are caused by capitalism, and that it’s socialist politics and organising that provide the answers, have never really gone beyond a slow drip. But watching the movement of hundreds of people up and down the steps leading into the central part of the launch venue evoked—in this hopeful mind at least—something like a waterfall. I’d have settled for a steady stream, but this felt like something more than that.

Despite the multiplying and deepening crises of capitalism afflicting society today, we know the fortunes of our movement won’t change just overnight. “The tradition of all dead generations weighs like a nightmare on the brains of the living”, as Marx put it in

The Eighteenth Brumaire of Louis Bonaparte

. Part of that nightmare, for us, is the widespread sense of hopelessness and passivity in the face of the many obvious problems of society—a product of decades of one-sided class war being waged by the capitalist class and their political servants against working-class people, the poor and the oppressed.

There’s no shortage of people who feel, on some level, that something is very wrong with society. The problem is, very few think there’s anything much we can do about it. So, a big part of what we were trying to do at the launch was rekindle a sense of hope for the future and a belief that if working-class people stand up, get organised and fight back, then we can achieve the kind of radical change our society so desperately needs.

This was a dominant theme of all the speeches. Public school teacher and VS candidate for Niddrie Brendan Laws, who is running against the former Labor education minister and now Premier Ben Carroll, talked about it in connection with his work as a leader of the Socialists in Schools rank-and-file union group. “We organised Socialists in Schools”, he said, “to be the dogged fighters, to raise expectations, to assuage the fears about striking, [and] to let people know what power we have ... This year we’ve had this huge segment of workers get a bit more confidence, and it is now the most urgent task to translate that into the fight for the whole new society that we deserve”.

VS candidate for Footscray Jasmine Duff, who as a convener of Students for Palestine has played a central role in the Palestine solidarity movement, spoke similarly. “Socialism is about saying we deserve better”, she said. “We deserve a world of dignity, and we deserve a world where our lives aren’t measured by what we produce for the capitalists.”

The path to re-establishing socialism as a genuine fighting force in Australian political life is a long one. It will require the collective intellect and energy of thousands of committed socialist activists devoting themselves to our cause, not just for this election campaign, but for years and decades into the future. 

As we move along that path, however, it’s important to mark the moments that feel like genuine milestones. The VS launch was one such moment—providing exactly the spark of inspiration needed as we embark on what we hope will be a historic, breakthrough campaign.

James Plested is the Victorian Socialists communications director.

author: AWSM
title: A Kiwi Dies in Ukraine: The War Between Empires and the People Sent to Fight It
content:
Aotearoa Workers Solidarity Movement

The death of a New Zealand man, Samuel Haines,  fighting in Ukraine was reported in the familiar language used whenever ordinary people are consumed by war. He was described through his personal history, his motivations, his family and his decision to travel across the world to take part in a conflict that had nothing to do with the daily lives of most people in Aotearoa. What was not highlighted was the fact that the tragedy of war is that those who suffer most are usually not the people who create wars. Politicians, generals and corporate interests make decisions from offices far away from the front lines, while working-class people are asked to sacrifice their bodies in the name of nations they did not create and systems they do not control.

The death of a Kiwi volunteer in Ukraine raises questions that go beyond one individual. Why are people from countries on the other side of the world being drawn into a conflict between major powers? Why has a war involving Russia, Ukraine, NATO and competing geopolitical interests been presented to millions of people as a simple battle between good and evil? And what does the presence of far-right nationalist forces within Ukraine’s military tell us about the way states use ideology and violence when they prepare societies for war?

For anarchists, the answers do not begin with choosing which flag deserves our loyalty. The history of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries shows that nationalism has repeatedly been used to convince ordinary people that the interests of their rulers are their own. Workers who have more in common with each other than with their own governments are encouraged to see each other as enemies because states require obedience, sacrifice and the willingness to kill. The war in Ukraine is no exception. It is a conflict shaped by Russian imperial ambitions, Ukrainian nationalism, NATO expansion, Western strategic interests and the wider competition between global powers. The people trapped inside this struggle are paying the price for decisions made by governments that claim to represent them.

Sam Haines ended up fighting and dying as a volunteer militia as part of the Azov battalion that emerged in 2014 during the conflict in eastern Ukraine. Its early period was associated with individuals and organisations connected to far-right nationalist politics. Some of its founders had histories linked to ultranationalist movements, and the organisation used symbols and imagery that attracted criticism because of their associations with European fascist traditions. Scholars, journalists and human rights organisations have documented these connections. When Azov was incorporated into Ukraine’s National Guard, it became an official military unit rather than an independent militia. Some argue that integration changed the organisation and that its fighters have since played a significant role in defending Ukrainian territory. Critics sttae that formal incorporation does not erase its ideological origins or the influence that nationalist movements gained through wartime conditions. Denying or minimising the reality of these movements serves the interests of those who want war narratives to remain simple and unquestionable.

The uncomfortable truth is that states have often relied on extremist movements when those movements are useful. Governments that present themselves as defenders of civilisation have repeatedly made alliances with forces they would condemn under different circumstances. During wartime, groups willing to use violence are often granted influence because military effectiveness becomes more important than political principles. This pattern is not unique to Ukraine. It has appeared throughout history wherever states have faced crises and sought to mobilise society around national struggle. The machinery of war creates conditions where authoritarian ideas can grow because war rewards hierarchy, obedience and the belief that violence can solve political problems.

The debate around NATO’s role in Ukraine is another area where discussion is often reduced to slogans. One side argues that NATO is a defensive alliance whose support for Ukraine is a necessary response to Russian aggression. The other argues that NATO expansion after the collapse of the Soviet Union created a security crisis that helped produce the conditions for war. An anarchist analysis should be sceptical of both state narratives because both begin …

author: Susan Price
title: Abby Martin: Speaking truth to power
content:
Jordan Shukri AK Armaou-Massoud

Activist journalist and filmmaker Abby Martin’s recent documentary, Earth’s Greatest Enemy, reveals the role of the United States military as the world’s largest institutional polluter, tracing the link between war, empire and ecological destruction.

Green Left ’s Jordan Shukri AK Armaou-Massoud spoke with Martin, who recently visited Australia from the US to promote her film. Her tour coincided with a protest by Traditional Owners and anti-war activists at the joint US-Australian Pine Gap spy base, located on the traditional lands of the Arrernte people.

Under the Australian-British-US war pact, AUKUS, Australia has allocated $400 billion towards US imperialism’s agenda.

More recently, Australia has joined other nations in the rush to build hyperscale artificial intelligence data centres, some of which will have military applications.

Australia is enmeshed with US imperialism through the Pine Gap spy base, where companies such as Raytheon, Northrop Grumman, General Dynamics, IBM and HP have a presence.

Given all this, Martin told GL that Australia plays a crucial role in the US war machine, “even though it’s more invisible”, by “housing the main intelligence hub for US targeting in the Middle East”.

“Pine Gap is a central component in these atrocities,” Martin said.

Its role also extends to the Asia-Pacific region.

“Australia plays such a key staging ground for the US expansion and the Asia-Pacific encroachment, and we’re seeing that buildup today and the consequences of that buildup,” Martin said.

“Every [US] base is a dumping ground. I’ve seen it in Okinawa. I’ve seen it in Guam. I’ve seen it surrounding Australia.

“You guys are the second in line once these islands are destroyed. The US Navy calls those islands an unsinkable aircraft carrier.

“Australia is totally expendable to the US ruling class … and … even though the Australian ruling class probably feels like they have a gun to their head … [they] are basically putting a nuclear target on the back of Australia because you are folded into the crimes and atrocities of my government.”

Despite the role of US imperialism today, Martin told GL that the resistance to Israel’s genocidal war in Palestine and invasion of Lebanon, and the resistance to the US-Israeli war on Iran and blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, has been “incredibly powerful to see” and shows that the US “can only do so much with a military arsenal”, especially when it doesn’t “actually wield control economically like [it] used to”.

“[T]he smarter aspects of the [US] ruling class didn’t want to overextend and possibly impede US hegemony in the long run, but they couldn’t help themselves because Trump is a fucking madman and his is the chaos presidency … [E]very fringe element of the ruling class in the US [is] attaching their agenda and trying to ram it through, including the Iran war hawks.”

Martin said this overextension means the US empire could be brought to its knees “without firing a single shot”, and why the power of organised working people “is so integral to this equation”.

The US capitalist class and its governments have tried to co-opt the union movement for so long, Martin said, “because they know the power of us withholding our labour”.

“I think it shows you that they are losing ground. That’s why they’re so violent and so desperate, and that’s why the propaganda is so violent and so desperate because they know they’ve lost the public conscience.”

This is an age marked by intense crises of capitalism: wars, economic, societal and ecological crises. Yet capitalists rush headlong into destructive resource extraction; there is rising militarisation at home and genocidal wars abroad. All the while, the world’s poor, rural and indigenous peoples pay the heaviest price, especially in exploited countries.

Speaking to the interconnections between these crises of capital, and why internationalists should take up the fight for ecology and against imperialism, Martin said it has been “so frustrating for decades” to see “these struggles being isolated and siloed from each other”.

“[I]t was so obvious all along that the anti-war movement is integral to the environmental justice movement; that this is also a labour issue; that this is a human rights issue; that this is about the militarisation of the police.

author: James McVicar
title: Europe boils and burns: capitalism’s climate hellscape
content:
If you want to know how many lives our rulers are willing to sacrifice to defend the fossil fuel industry, you could start by looking at Europe. A heatwave that swept over huge swathes of the continent in June may have killed as many as

25,000 people

, according to one estimate from Indiana University. More than 3,000 in Spain and more still in Germany. The French national health agency has recorded

more than 5,700 excess deaths

. In many cities and towns, temperatures reached above 40 degrees Celsius.

Extreme heat is a major cause of weather-related death, if not

the

 major cause. It is a brutal way to die.

As the body desperately tries to offload heat by redirecting blood flow to the skin, the heart comes under increasing strain. Internal organs can start to disintegrate and leach toxins into the bloodstream. You can lose more than a litre of fluid every hour through sweat, which can cause a drop in blood pressure and lead to kidney failure.

Extreme heat also aggravates existing health conditions, which is why older people are particularly vulnerable. In France, about two-thirds of the excess deaths in June’s heatwave were people aged 75 and older.

The effects of extreme heat also intersect with the inequalities entrenched by capitalism. Women spend 30-50 percent more of their working day above heat stress thresholds, according to University of London researcher Laurie Parsons in an interview with DW, and they are

over-represented in heatwave deaths

. A 2021 study found that extreme urban heat exposure has

increased drastically since the 1980s

—mostly in sub-Saharan Africa and southern Asia.

Europe has been trapped under a heat dome: a mass of high-pressure air that traps heat like a lid and prevents clouds from forming. This in turn led to diabolical wildfires across France and Spain in July that forced hundreds of thousands of people to flee for safety. In such extreme weather conditions, wildfires can generate their own thunderstorms. The technical term is pyrocumulonimbus, but NASA calls them “fire-breathing dragon” clouds.

This is the hellish world capitalism is creating for more and more of us every day. It’s not just happening in Europe but all over the world. As a result of climate change, formerly extreme and rare weather events are becoming more frequent and more intense under the impacts of climate change. More heat domes, more mass deaths and raging infernos.

Analysis by a consortium of climate scientists from World Weather Attribution found that the June heatwave in Europe

would not have been possible

 without climate change. The pyrocumulonimbus cloud produced by the fires in France was the first one ever to be recorded in the country.

We know what’s behind all this: the continued extraction and burning of fossil fuels, driven by capitalism. The CSIRO states that about

90 percent

 of the world’s fossil fuel carbon emissions—the main cause of global temperature rises—comes from the burning of coal, oil and gas. In 2024, it was estimated that half of all planet-warming carbon dioxide emissions could be traced back to just

32 companies

, according to figures from the

CarbonMajors database

.

And cooking the globe is extremely good business. According to research by Oxfam, the six biggest fossil fuel companies doubled their profits for the second quarter of 2026, raking in

$46 billion

 compared to a measly $23 billion in the first three months of the year. They’re planning to increase their oil and gas production by 14 percent by 2030.

And this is not just a question of a handful of unregulated cowboy companies holding the rest of the world to ransom. CarbonMajors notes that in 1924,

17 of the top 20 carbon-emitting companies

 were state-owned, rather than private corporations. More to the point, fossil fuels are profitable only because of capitalism’s insatiable demand for them. Energy grids are built around them. Global shipping networks depend upon them. They’re a key ingredient in the production of plastics, fertilisers and construction materials. Militaries could not function without them.

The whole system of capitalism is defined by the competitive drive for profit. Capitalists control the world’s productive resources and will put those resources into motion only if they can turn a profit and secure a competitive advantage over their rivals. As long as this remains society’s motive force, the rich and powerful will go on burning fossil fuels to the very last drop …

author: Isaac Nellist
title: Green Left Show #89: How India's ‘Cockroaches’ struck a blow against Modi
content:
The youth-led Cockroach Janata Party movement forced education minister Dhamendra Pradhan to resign over exam and admission paper leaks and corruption in the education system.

On this episode of the Green Left Show, Isaac Nellist speaks to Manish Kumar, Uttar Pradesh State President of the All India Students’ Association (AISA) and PhD student at Allahabad University, about this powerful expression of dissent against the Narendra Modi Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government.

Kumar was one of three students and AISA members who participated in a 23-day hunger strike at the Jantar Mantar protest site in Delhi, alongside well-known activist Sonam Wangchuk.

They also discussed the police brutality against youth protesters in Delhi on July 20 and the next steps for the youth movement.

author: Unknown
title: ABD: "Sosyalistler halka kulak verdikleri için kazanıyor"
content:
2026 ara seçimlerine bir kaç ay kala, ABD siyasetinde bir sosyalist heyula kol geziyor. İki partili Trump ve MAGA Cumhuriyetçilerin popülist sağcılığı karşısında bir dönem bocalayan Demokrat Parti'nin 2024 yenilgisi sonrasında muhalefette yeniden başını kaldırmasında sosyalistlerin rolü giderek belirginleşiyor. New York Belediye Başkanlığını Trump'ın desteklediği Demokrat Partili rakibini yenilgiye uğratarak kazanan Mamdani'nin zaferinden sonra sosyalistlerin başını çektiği, tabanın söz ve kararına dayalı çalışma tarzı gitgide partinin yönünü daha derinden belirlemeye başlıyor. 


Toplumsal sorunlar üzerine çarpıcı denemeleriyle tanınan New York Times köşe yazarı, sosyolog ve kültür eleştirmeni Profesör Tressie McMillan Cottom, bu süreci çevirisini sunduğumuz "Sosyalistler halka kulak verdikleri için kazanıyor" başlıklı makalesiyle değerlendiriyor.


Amerikan siyasetinde sosyalist bir canlanmaya mı tanık oluyoruz?


Zohran Mamdani'nin New York Belediye Başkanı seçilmesinden bu yana yapılan siyasi tahlilleri toparladığınızda solculuğun altın çağında yaşadığınıza ya da komünistlerin gelmekte olduğuna inanasınız gelebilir.


Solcu adayların önseçim başarıları


Bu tablo, gün gelip seçim sonuçlarına da yansıyabilir; ama o gün bugün değil. Evet, bu hafta pek çok solcu aday başarılı oldu; Michigan ve Kansas'ta dikkat çekici ön seçim zaferleri kazanıldı, ama yarışı kazananların arasında pek çok ılımlı Demokrat da vardı. Kazanan adaylardan bazılarının kampanya bütçesi oldukça yüksekti. Diğerleri ise son derece büyük bir mali sıkıntıyla başa çıkmak zorundaydı. Ancak içlerindeki en iyiler, Demokratların kazanmak için yalnızca seçmenlerden bağış toplamakla kalmayıp onları örgütlemeleri gerektiğinin idrakinde kampanya yürütenlerdi.


Demokrat Partinin yapısal sorunları


Demokrat Parti derin bir yapısal sorunla karşı karşıya. Bir yanda özlemini duyduğu geçmiş, öte yanda ise henüz kuramadığı bir gelecek var. Şimdilik bunun farkında olan yalnızca partinin ilerici kanadı gibi görünüyor.


Düzen içi Demokrat Partililer, solcu adayların seçilebilirliği konusunda istedikleri kadar gürültü koparsalar da, partinin halletmesi gereken daha büyük meseleleri var. Demokratların seçim gücünün iki kaynağından biri olan işçi hareketi, New Deal'den sonraki on yıllar boyunca işçi sınıfından erkeklerin oylarını güvence altına almış ve kırsal bölgelerde, ABD'nin kuzeydoğusu ile Büyük Göller çevresinde yer alan, 20. Yüzyılın büyük bölümünde ülkenin ağır sanayi merkezi olan, ancak 1970'lerden itibaren hızlı sanayisizleşme yaşayan bölgelere verilen adla Rust Belt'te (Pas Kuşağı) Demokratların ana damarı olarak iş görmüştü. Sivil haklar örgütleri ise, Kennedy’nin öldürülmesinden sonra başa geçen Demokrat Başkan Lyndon B. Johnson’ın Sivil Haklar Yasası'nı imzaladığı günden beri bekleceği şekilde Siyahların oylarını güvence altına alarak Demokratların Güney'de rekabeti sürdürebilmesini sağlamıştı. Uzun yıllar boyunca sıradan Demokrat adaylar, karmaşık siyasal mesajlarını seçmene ulaştırma işini büyük ölçüde bu iki örgütlü toplumsal güce bıraktı.


Demokrat Parti'nin kendi sınırlarına varması


Anlaşılması gereken en önemli şey, peş peşe  60 yıl boyunca biriken ekonomik, hukuksal, siyasal ve kültürel zorlukların sendikalar ve sivil hak gruplarının bu görevi yerine getirmesini artık imkânsız değilse de çok güç kılmış olması.


Özellikle siyah sivil haklar örgütleri uzun zamandır Demokrat Parti'nin örgütlenmesi  için büyük çaba gösteriyor. Sadece sandığa gitmekle kalmıyor, seçmen yetiştiriyor, ulusal platformları yerel mesajlarla dönüştürüyor ve adaylarla çalışanları eğitiyor. Demokrat Parti'nin seçim makinesini ayakta tutanlar, kiliselerde ışıkları söndürmeyenler, minibüsleri kullanan, mahalle mahalle dolaşan, mitinglere katılan ve seçim günü seçmeni güvenle sandığa taşıyanlar siyah kadınlardı. Güney'deki siyah örgütçüler, Yüksek Mahkeme tarafından Oy Hakkı Yasası’nın budanmasından sonra Demokratların bir süvari kıtası gibi yardıma koşmasını bekliyordu. Oysa şimdi kendilerini terk edilmiş hissediyorlar. Muhafazakârların savunuculuk ve lobi örgütü Heritage Action ile kampüslerde ve seçim kampanyalarında faaliyet gösteren gençlik ve siyasi aktivizm örgütü Turning Point USA gibi gruplara bakıp, bakıp, "Bizim de böyle kurumlarımız olsaydı" diye hayıflanıyorlar.


Sendikalı işçilerin oranı da rekor düzeyde düşük. Demokratlar işçi sınıfı seçmenlerini geri kazanacak ve Güney'i harekete geçirecek, seçim kazandıracak merkezci bir mesaj bulsalar bile, seçmeni …

title: Solidaridad con periodistas del Líbano
content:
A la luz de la actual invasión israelí del Líbano, 

Industrial Workers of the World Printing and Publishing Workers Union and Freelance Journalists Union

 expresa su solidaridad con 

Union of Journalists in Lebanon

, miembro de 

la Federación Internacional de Periodistas

.


La invasión israelí ya se ha cobrado la vida de al menos 1.268 personas en el Líbano, según 

el

Ministerio

 de Sanidad

 de ese país en el momento de redactar este comunicado. Entre los fallecidos hay al menos cuatro periodistas, de acuerdo con 

la FIP

. Además de las muertes, la invasión israelí también ha provocado el desplazamiento de más de un millón de personas, entre ellas al menos 65 periodistas afiliados y afiliadas al UJL.


Para apoyar a los y las periodistas del Líbano, UJL ofrece servicios profesionales (por ejemplo, el acceso a un lugar desde el que trabajar) y sociales, como alojamiento. Aunque la crisis humanitaria es inmensa y crece cada día que persiste la invasión israelí, UJL solicita una contribución inicial de 10.000 dólares estadounidenses para atender las necesidades más urgentes.


Por ello, IWW PPWU-FJU está recaudando fondos para proporcionar a UJL esta contribución inicial. Las donaciones pueden enviarse aquí (enlace en inglés, para enviar dinero basta con hacer uso del botón violeta a la derecha en el que pone “donate now”): 

https://chuffed.org/project/175670-solidarity-with-union-of-journalists-in-lebanon


Animamos a toda persona dedicada al periodismo, a la afiliación de los sindicatos y a cualquiera que lea estas líneas a apoyar al UJL contribuyendo a esta recaudación de fondos y difundiéndola ampliamente.

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: SC issues protection for Negros lawyer, dev’t workers
content:
Photo by Supreme Court of the Philippines

“This is an important step toward protecting human rights defenders from red-tagging, surveillance, harassment, and threats.”

MANILA — After six months, the Supreme Court (SC) issued protective writs of amparo and habeas data for Negros-based lawyer Rey Gorgonio and development workers Joselito Macapobre, Analyn Mirano, and Ma. Anabelle Ilustrisimo.

After they filed a petition on March 5, the writs were granted at an SC en banc session on August 5. The high court directed Lt. Gen. Antonio Nafarrete and others not to go within one kilometer of the petitioners and their immediate family members.

“This is an important step toward protecting human rights defenders from red-tagging, surveillance, harassment, and threats,” said the National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers (NUPL) who represented the petitioners.

The SC further instructed the Court of Appeals (CA) to conduct a summary hearing to determine whether the four petitioners are entitled to the privileges of the writs of amparo and habeas data, particularly permanent protection, identification of accountability, and granting of other reliefs like deletion or surrender of government data on them.

A human rights lawyer, Gorgonio represents the poor in Negros. Macapobre, Mirano, and Ilustrisimo work for Paghida-et sa Kauswagan Development Group (PDG), a local grassroots organization working for agrarian reform, sustainable agriculture, and the rights of small farmers and fisherfolk.

“This Resolution is significant not only for the petitioners but also for development workers, human rights defenders, lawyers, journalists, church workers, indigenous peoples, farmers, and civil society organizations who continue to carry out legitimate work in communities despite increasing risks and restrictions on civic space,” said PDG in a statement sent to Bulatlat .

Read: Negros-based NGO helping farmers exposes lies, inaccuracies in terror financing complaint

The case stems from a buildup of harassment and surveillance against the Negros-based human rights workers.

On January 17, Mirano received a message from an unidentified individual claiming to be from National Intelligence Coordinating Agency (NICA), demanding her to become a paid informant for the military. A week later (January 25), Gorgonio received a death threat while at a public forum on the writ of kalikasan and the campaign to stop the palm oil plantation in Candoni.

Macapobre, on the other hand, survived an abduction attempt on January 18 after delivering seed relief assistance to farmers. He was seized by three armed men and was forced to a waiting van. He managed to break free and escape with the help of nearby farmer leaders. Despite this, the harassment against him continued.

Urong, Kabankalan City, that soldiers from the 94th Infantry Battalion were asking about her. The surveillance persisted until 2022 when she witnessed soldiers monitoring her movements at least three times.

They were subjected to red-tagging by the military and law enforcement agencies for their affiliation and the work they do.

PDG stressed that development workers and civil society organizations have consistently documented harmful effects of red-tagging like fear, weakened democratic participation, and undermined trust between communities and public institutions.

Human rights group Karapatan also welcomed the SC resolution, stressing that the four petitioners’ situation mirrors the plight of human rights defenders, development workers, lawyers, church people, journalists, and community organizers who have been targeted under the government’s counterinsurgency program.

author: Omar Hassan
title: By ditching Jacinta Allan, Labor has bent the knee to the bosses again
content:
After over a year of relentless campaigning by the capitalist press, Victorian Premier Jacinta Allan is history. Few on the left will mourn her passing. She implemented $2.4 billion in cuts to school funding and oversaw the degradation of schools and hospitals. She introduced harsh new sentencing laws, copied from the right-wing Queensland government, which meant children as young as 14 can now be sentenced to life in prison. She spent millions hosting an international arms fair during a genocide, and unleashed riot police and stun grenades on those who dissented. She continued the demolition of public housing and sell-offs of public land started by former premier Daniel Andrews, and when under pressure over budget deficits, continued the privatisation of VicRoads and planned to do the same to Melbourne Water.

Despite all this, the capitalist establishment wanted her brought down, and are gleefully celebrating her demise. The Murdoch press is known for its rabid hatred of Victorian Labor, and have made its predictable contribution. But it has been the

Age

 newspaper, historically considered a liberal outlet, which led the ruthless campaign to destroy Allan. It ran more than 100 pieces on what they came to call “corruption” in the Big Build (a collection of infrastructure projects announced in 2015), a small proportion of which was real and much of which was simply an attack on effective trade unionism. This campaign continued despite it being clear that the narrative being spun was helping the far-right One Nation rise in the polls.

When the news broke that Allan was resigning, the editors celebrated with a front page spread and major feature on their website. The paper’s editorial rightly took credit, referencing the

Age

’s endless and highly partisan reporting on the Big Build. Not satisfied with bringing down an elected premier, they demanded that Allan’s replacement, Ben Carroll, express “contrition” for his predecessor’s sins.

The nature of those sins was made clear when Paul Sakkal, the

Age

’s chief political correspondent, defined “

Victoria-style governance

” (cue thunderous minor chords) as a  government which “scorned business leaders, economists and the media” and cast them as “ideological enemies”. This is a reference to more than a decade of Labor governments in Victoria that, while far from left wing, have not fully embraced the interests and desires of big business. Key to the widespread capitalist hostility was Andrews’ close ties to the unions, particularly the CFMEU, and his stance in relation to the pandemic. The anti-vaxxer, death-desiring mobs that protested the lockdowns were backed by capitalists big and small, and have now congealed around Pauline Hanson’s One Nation.

Of course, Sakkal’s piece is not merely of historical interest. Rather, it presents Allan’s downfall as a fable whose lesson is that federal Labor must not implement the slightest measure that could cause the rich any discomfort. His focus here is on the minor tax tweaks proposed in the federal budget, which would ask investors to pay the same rates as wage earners (the horror!). This moderate half step back towards a fair tax system “showed signs that habits from Victoria might have spread north”, according to Sakkal. His proof? “Business groups protested for months”.

The irony, of course, is that the Andrews-Allan Labor government has been, until recently, the most popular state administration for decades. The fact that Andrews won ever greater support among working-class people for his public health measures, despite the backlash from businesses, stuck in the craw of the capitalist establishment. So too the mass support for Labor’s investment in public infrastructure, including the much-maligned Suburban Rail Loop. It is incredible that in the face of the campaign against it, only 37 percent of Victorians oppose the plan. The bosses and their media shills simply cannot understand why the majority of people value human life and social amenities more than profits. Nor can they accept that Victoria has in effect been a one-party state for nearly 28 years.

Carrol, Allan’s replacement, is a robotic right-wing ALP apparatchik from central casting, who has immediately set himself the task of winning back the support of the capitalists. His first announcement was to assuage them that his name was neither Jacinta Allan nor Daniel Andrews, a move which was applauded by the commentariat: “[Unlike Andrews and Allan] Carroll …

title: ‘Not Fair NEET, But Ban NEET’: Hunger Strike Against NEET Enters Seventh Day in Chennai
content:
The indefinite hunger strike against the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) in Chennai entered its seventh day on Saturday, August 8. The agitation, led by the Anti-NEET Federation and the Joint Movement Against NEET, is demanding not merely reforms to the examination but its complete abolition, along with greater state control over education.


 


Chennai, August 8, 2026:

 An indefinite hunger strike demanding the abolition of the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) entered its seventh day in Chennai on Saturday, with four anti-NEET activists continuing their fast at Koyambedu.


 


The four hunger strikers —

Dhanasekar, Jeeva, Puliyanthope Mohan and Ravi

 — are associated with the Ban NEET Movement of the Anti-NEET Federation in Tamil Nadu. The Joint Movement Against NEET is demanding the abolition of NEET, greater state autonomy over education and a designated public space in Chennai where the protesters can continue their agitation peacefully. One of the four hunger-strikers, Ravi was hospitalised on Thursday after coughing up blood. His condition is now reported to be stable.


 


The protesters are demanding that the TVK-led Tamil Nadu government pass a fresh Assembly resolution or Bill seeking exemption from NEET and pursue the pending legal challenge concerning the state’s earlier attempt to secure an exemption. They have also called for the government to provide a permanent public venue for peaceful protests in Chennai.


 


“We will call off the hunger strike if a resolution is passed. That’s the first step. Then, we need an alternative location to carry on with our protest against the exam,” said

S Manirathinam

, brother of S Anitha, whose death in 2017 became a defining moment in Tamil Nadu’s opposition to NEET.


 


Manirathinam urged the Tamil Nadu government to reaffirm its opposition to NEET through a fresh Assembly resolution or Bill. He said previous AIADMK and DMK governments had passed resolutions and a Bill seeking an exemption and argued that a renewed initiative would demonstrate that opposition to NEET cuts across party lines.


 


He also called for the state government to expedite its legal challenge to the President’s decision to withhold assent to the earlier exemption Bill passed in the state assembly.


 


‘Not fair NEET, but ban NEET’


 


The Anti-NEET Federation, a collective of students’ and youth organisations and social workers, says its demand goes beyond seeking reforms that will make NEET more transparent or prevent examination malpractice.


 


Its position is unequivocal:

NEET itself should be abolished

.


 


The federation argues that NEET favours students who can afford expensive private coaching and additional years of preparation, placing students from rural, government-school and marginalised communities at a great disadvantage. The Joint Movement Against NEET has similarly argued that the examination has deepened inequalities in access to medical education and contributed to the expansion of the private coaching industry. Its press statement also cited nearly 40 student deaths in Tamil Nadu, including those of Anitha, Pratheeba and Anukreethika, which it linked to examination pressure, systemic inequalities and unequal access to opportunities.


 


The federation is also demanding that states be allowed greater freedom to determine medical admissions, including the use of Plus Two examination marks, and that education be moved from the Concurrent List back to the State List.


 


Dhanasekar said the hunger strike began after the protesters were denied permission to hold a peaceful public demonstration, despite an assurance reportedly given during earlier anti-NEET protests.


 


School Education Minister A Rajmohan visited the protest site on Wednesday, reiterated the government’s opposition to NEET and appealed to the protesters to withdraw their fast, Dhanasekar said. “We will end the hunger strike only if the government allots us a public place to continue our agitation peacefully,” he said.


 


Anitha’s name remains at the heart of the anti-NEET struggle


 


Do you remember S Anitha?


 


During the month-long protests against NEET at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, her name was repeatedly invoked by protesters from Tamil Nadu. For the anti-NEET movement, her memory is not merely commemorative. It is political.


 


Anitha was a

Dalit student

from Ariyalur district and the daughter of an

 agricultural daily-wage labourer …

title: Mehr Proletariat und weniger Todesanzeigen: Vom Ende der Arbeiterklasse bis zu ihrem Wiederaufbau
content:
Gefunden auf portal oaca, die Übersetzung ist von uns. Dieser Text von Agustín Guillamón öffnet viele interessante und wichtige Fragen die in der Debatte und in der Praxis überprüft werden müssen. Dort wo das Proletariat als tot, oder nicht-existent erklärt wurde, gibt Guillamón antworten auf diese falsche Position und unterstreicht wieder, sowie andere weltweit auch, die Gründe warum die Klassenfrage enormer Bedeutung ist und für die Abschaffung des Kapitalismus und aller Staaten-Nationen zentral ist.


Wir sind an dem Punkt wo Guillamón Gewerkschaften/Syndikate eine kämpfende Rolle zuspielt – Punkt Nr. 5 – anderer Meinung. Der Syndikalismus/Gewerkschaftswesen, auch mit dem Adjektiv ‚revolutionär‘ ist nur ein Organ für die Verhandlung zwischen Arbeit und Kapital und nicht ein Instrument der Selbstbefreiung des Proletariats, ergo eine Organisationsform für die Zerstörung kapitalistischer Verhältnisse. Mehr dazu in der Textreihe Kritik am Syndikalismus/Gewerkschaftswesen/Gewerkschaften/Syndikate. Dass die Befreiung der Arbeiterklasse nur das Werk der Arbeiterklasse selbst sein kann und nicht irgendeiner Partei/Avantgarde/Gewerkschaft/Syndikat, dass diese Ausdruck der Organen sein wird, die nur dem Zweck der Zerstörung der Klassengesellschaft dienen, die das Proletariat aus ihrer Autonomie heraus erschafft. Nicht eine neue oder alternative Verwaltung des Kapitals ist das Ziel, sondern seine Endgültige Abschaffung.


„Die gewerkschaftlichen/syndikalistischen Organisationen sind keineswegs eine Waffe im Kampf gegen das Kapital, sondern ein perfekt in das System integriertes Instrument, das als Vermittler und Schlichter zwischen der herrschenden Klasse und den Ausgebeuteten dient, um den Preis der Arbeitskraft zu regulieren und zu verhindern, dass sich die Arbeiterklasse zu einer revolutionären Kraft formiert. Ein weiteres widerwärtiges Merkmal ist, dass sie die Aufgabe erfüllen, die massive Kraft der Klasse in sektorale Interessen einzugrenzen, was zur Spaltung und Zersplitterung des Kampfes beiträgt und die Illusion nährt, dass jeder Beschäftigungssektor, jede Rasse und jede ethnische Gruppe eigene Interessen habe, die vom Rest losgelöst seien.“ Materiales x la emancipación.


Auch überrascht uns am Ende des Textes ein Zwinkern das Guillamón an drei „anarchistischen“ Organisationen im spanischen Staat macht, die unserer Meinung, trotz der jetzigen pathetischen Lage anarchistischer Kreise dort, die ranzigste Variante dieser sind.


Nicht desto trotz sind die Thesen und die Fragen die hier im Text aufgeworfen aktuell und auch für uns sehr interessant um sie zu diskutieren.


Lang lebe die Anarchie


_________________


Mehr Proletariat und weniger Totenanzeigen: Vom Ende der Arbeiterklasse bis zu ihrem Wiederaufbau


2026


Einleitung


Seit Jahrzehnten vertritt ein Teil des kritischen Denkens die Ansicht, dass das Proletariat nicht mehr die historische Rolle einnimmt, die es während des langen Zyklus der Arbeiterbewegung – etwa von der Mitte des 19. Jahrhunderts bis zur Krise des fordistischen Kapitalismus in den 1970er Jahren – gespielt hat. Die Deindustrialisierung der westlichen Ökonomien, die Fragmentierung der Arbeit, die Ausweitung des Dienstleistungssektors, die Prekarisierung der Beschäftigung, die Individualisierung der Arbeitsbeziehungen und die zunehmende Integration des sozialen Lebens in die Logik des Konsums haben dazu geführt, dass die Gültigkeit der Klassenpolitik als strategischer Horizont der Emanzipation in Frage gestellt wird.


Im libertären Milieu ist die Diskussion besonders intensiv. Autoren wie Tomás Ibáñez und Miquel Amorós argumentieren, dass die tiefgreifenden Veränderungen des Kapitalismus die historischen Bedingungen untergraben haben, die die klassische Arbeiterbewegung erst möglich gemacht haben. Das Verschwinden der Arbeiterkultur, die institutionelle Integration der Gewerkschaften/Syndikate, die Auflösung der alten Arbeits- und Nachbarschaftsgemeinschaften sowie die zunehmende kommerzielle Kolonisierung des Lebens hätten dem Proletariat die politische Zentralität genommen, die es über mehr als ein Jahrhundert hinweg innehatte. Es ginge nicht mehr nur um die Niederlage bestimmter Organisationen, sondern um das Ende eines historischen Zyklus, in dem sich die Arbeiterklasse als revolutionäres Subjekt konstituieren konnte.


Diese Einschätzung enthält Elemente, die schwer zu bestreiten sind. Es ist offensichtlich, dass der heutige Kapitalismus die Produktionsbedingungen, die Zusammensetzung …

title: Stand and fight Calum Stuart
content:
Credit: Ivan Weiss


T

he day I interviewed Daniel York Loh, there was news of anti-immigration protests—some of which turned violent—erupting across Belfast, Northern Ireland. The BBC reported that people had been targeted simply for having “a different skin colour”.


In recent years, xenophobic and racist rhetoric has been on the rise in the UK. This has manifested alongside right-wing politicians and political parties (such as Nigel Farage, leader of Reform UK, and Tommy Robinson, a far-right activist) moving from fringe entities into mainstream influence. For Loh—an actor, writer, and filmmaker of Singaporean and British heritage who has been a vocal supporter of left-wing causes—these developments have been equal parts alarming and maddening.


Based in London, Loh has been working in the performing arts in both the UK and Asia for more than forty years. In that time, he’s become increasingly invested in working to improve Asian representation on stage and on screen. He was a founding member of BEATS (British East and Southeast Asian in Theatre and on Screen), a not-for-profit, volunteer-based advocacy group for British East and Southeast Asians working in theatre, film, or television. He’s also a member of the Race Equality Committee of Equity, the trade union for performers and creatives in the entertainment and performing arts industry. In 2016, he was one of twenty-one contributors to the anthology

The Good Immigrant

, reflecting on issues of race, immigration, identity, and Othering in the UK. A tenth anniversary issue of the book was launched this year.


More recently, Loh appeared in the true crime drama

I Fought The Law

, a four-part series following the determined struggle of Ann Ming—played by the award-winning British actor Sheridan Smith—a former nurse who campaigned for seventeen years to overturn the UK’s double jeopardy law after the murder of her daughter in 1989. Loh stars as Ming’s mixed-race husband, Charlie, in a story that examines grief and trauma, while not shying away from the racial politics of Britain in the 1980s and 1990s.


I’d like to start with

I Fought The Law

, which was based on a true story. It received rave reviews and you were nominated for an award at the 2026 Royal Television Society North East and the Borders Awards. What was it like taking on this role and playing a character based on a real person?


Daniel York Loh with Sheridan Smith in I Fought The Law. Credit: Anastasia A Arsentyeva


Charlie Ming, he was like me. He was mixed race but, essentially, very, very British. Very, very Middlesbrough [a town in North Yorkshire, England]. Ann Ming was kind of an advisor on the series, but [Charlie’s] not around anymore.


I Fought The Law

 was based on Ann Ming’s book [

For the Love of Julie

, published in 2009]. It was a real privilege to do it. It was such a good script and an amazing story. Sheridan Smith is an amazing actor and we had a great director [Erik Richter Strand]. I can’t speak highly enough of the whole thing, really.


I got the impression that it resonated with people because, right now, there’s a widespread sense of cynicism in many places. But in the series you have an ordinary person who’s taking on a massive system and prevailing.


I’m told the viewing figures were very high for the modern era. I think people were very taken with [the story]; it was a genuinely huge achievement. Ann Ming kept on going, she was very dogged, which I think people really admire… when you win in the end. If you’re very dogged and you don’t win, they kind of think you’re mad.


How do you feel the series dealt with the issue of racism?


There was a scene that flashed back to when Ann and Charlie were younger, and the racist neighbour comes around and there’s graffiti with racist slurs on the wall outside. And there were a few people online going, “Oh, typical ‘woke’ ITV.” But that’s in her book! It’s in Ann Ming’s book, and it was actually much worse. They suffered terrible racism when they first got together. I wanted that stuff in there. It’s important in social history and it resonates with what’s going on now.


There’s always people who want to blame migrants for anything and everything. If you put one foot out of line, your entire ‘community’—in inverted commas, because people don’t know each other a lot of the time—suffers. It reminds me of my own childhood. My childhood was basically [full of] racist abuse and my dad coming up to the school; the teachers …

author: Mag
title: Am autoritären Kipppunkt: „Law and Order“-Politik hat Konjunktur
content:
Dossier


„… In der Klimaforschung ist ein Kipppunkt ein Moment, an dem – laut Weltklimarat – „eine kritische Grenze“ erreicht wird, „jenseits derer sich ein System umorganisiert“, neue Prozesse sich verfestigen und negative Dynamiken sich beschleunigen. Dies lässt sich auch auf gesellschaftliche Kipppunkte übertragen. Kipppunkte entstehen nicht zufällig, sie sind das Ergebnis länger zurückliegender destruktiver Prozesse. Doch im Gegensatz zum Klima sind gesellschaftliche Prozesse nie unumkehrbar. Allerdings sind etablierte Diskurse, Strukturen und Normen oft nicht rückgängig zu machen. Sind autoritäre Kipppunkte überschritten, wird der Boden brüchig, auf dem plurale und demokratische Gesellschaften stehen…“

Kommentar von Daniel Mullis, Maximilian Pichl und Vanessa E. Thompson vom 16. Juni 2023 in der taz online


, siehe mehr daraus und dazu:


[Buch: »Erziehung zur Grausamkeit. Die Massenpsychologie des Neuen Faschismus«] Lehrjahre der Unmenschlichkeit: Faschismus als Prozess der Verrohung


„

Seit dreißig Jahren, in manchen Nationen sogar schon länger, erleben wir einen Aufstieg des rechten Populismus. Ultrarechte Parteien werden nicht nur stärker, viele radikalisieren sich auch nach und nach – oder sogar rasend schnell. Und eine entscheidende Rolle spielt dabei ein Kult der Härte, der die schräge Allianz aus Neuem Faschismus und Ultraliberalen fest zusammenhält.


Konnte man vor einigen Jahren noch vom aufkommenden »Rechtspopulismus« sprechen, wäre das heute in vielen Fällen eine Verharmlosung. Rechtsextremismus oder Neuer Faschismus trifft es da schon weit besser, bedenkt man, dass sich faschistische Bewegungen durch eine Reihe von Eigenschaften auszeichnen: Führerkult, paranoide Weltbilder, die permanent geschürt werden, ein Schwarz-Weiß-Denken, antagonistische Feindbilder, vor allem von Minderheiten, aber auch gegen vermeintliche innere Feinde. (…)


Faschismus ist, so gesehen, eher eine Stimmung, die einen nach und nach erfasst und überwältigt. Die Affekte von Gekränktheit, Angst, Neid, das Ressentiment und die Erlösungssehnsucht, sie alle sind ansteckend – und diese Ansteckung läuft nicht bloß von den Agitatoren zu den Anhängern, sondern wirkt kreuz und quer. Wie bei Synapsenverschaltungen werden die Verbindungen gestärkt, je intensiver sie benutzt werden. Emotionen, Tonfall und Phrasen werden übernommen, steigern sich zu Fanatismus.

Der Faschismus ist demnach weniger eine Ideologie als ein sozialer Prozess. Ansteckung ist kein Zufall, sie gedeiht in Milieus, in denen Gefühle zirkulieren wie ein Echo, das lauter zurückkehrt, als es ausgesendet wurde. Bis der Fanatiker am Ende als normal erscheint und der Normale als verdächtig.


Das trifft alles auf Parteien wie die MAGA-Bewegung der US-Republikaner zu, genauso auf die Alternative für Deutschland oder die Freiheitliche Partei in Österreich. Sie alle haben sich in den vergangenen Jahren in einem Prozess der Selbstradikalisierung markant verwandelt. Gewiss, Rechtspopulismus ist nicht dasselbe wie Faschismus, aber die Übergänge sind fließend. Wer als Rechtspopulist begann, kann als Faschist enden.


Und es geschah und geschieht dabei auch etwas Eigentümliches, das bis heute erst in Ansätzen verstanden wird: Die Radikalisierung der einen Partei wirkte als Aufschaukelung und Vorbildeffekt auf die anderen zurück. Das Resultat ist die Radikalisierung aller in einem längst globalen Resonanzraum. Simpel gesagt: Ohne Trump wäre die AfD wahrscheinlich gemäßigter, die FPÖ wäre ohne die AfD weniger radikal – und umgekehrt. (…)

title: Letter of solidarity By Francisco Solar and Joaquín García,Regarding the Health Situation of Our Comrade Juan Aliste Vega (Chile)
content:
ES: (Chile) Sobre la situación de salud del compañero Juan Aliste Vega por Francisco Solar y Joaquín García

It was around February of this year that our brother and comrade Juan Aliste Vega began to experience the first episodes of pain—mild at first—in his left hip. True to his character, he lived with this minor discomfort, but he never normalized it; he knew it was an abnormal pain.

As time passed and the pain intensified, the unusual situation transformed into a worrisome one, so naturally, he sought medical attention at the La Gonzalina prison hospital in Rancagua. Without much success in this initial visit, he was given and prescribed medications such as paracetamol and tramadol. Juan was not satisfied; the pain persisted, the root cause remained unclear, and his daily life was significantly disrupted because the pain naturally led to serious mobility issues. We witnessed his concern and persistence during this period. Juan has never been a complainer, and his unfortunately long time in prison has given him a deep understanding of his body, crucial for remaining resilient in a hostile and uncaring environment. The day came when Juan could no longer move and had to be rushed to the prison hospital. After a series of negligent acts, X-rays, and unhelpful doctors, he was sent back to his cellblock with painkillers and IV fluids. Something was wrong; we all knew it. A second emergency trip to the hospital that same afternoon was necessary, and a new X-ray analysis revealed possible septic osteoarthritis in his hip. Due to the urgency of his condition, he was transferred to the Rancagua Hospital, where he received strong antibiotics. That same night, he returned to his cellblock.

From that moment on, Juan could only move with crutches. His daily life was severely disrupted. The antibiotics only solved part of the problem; the pain persisted, something was still there. Despite how adverse the situation became in his daily life, we were fortunate enough to be able to support him and thus try to lessen, even if only a little, the burden on his shoulders. These were, and are, the kinds of care and concern we believe should always be shared among comrades, beyond any code of conduct imposed by the prison environment. Revolutionary affection must always prevail over individualistic apathy.

The culmination of this critical situation, which initially led to his hospitalization in the unit, was due to a pain that was more intense than “normal” and once again left him unable to move. Only then did the hospital administration decide to admit him for further evaluation.

We haven’t seen him since that day.

Despite the pain and the complexity of his situation, our comrade has always remained strong and determined to face everything that has been thrown at him. This attitude has always characterized him, ever since, as a teenager, he decided to confront the dictatorship as part of the Lautaro Youth Movement and later, as an independent subversive, relentlessly fighting predatory capitalism and those who uphold it. He has also demonstrated this strength during the nearly 30 years he has spent in prison for two different reasons and in different contexts. During these years, he has not hesitated to participate in various anti-prison movements, mobilizations, and strikes, writing solidarity texts, advocating for the freedom of another comrade, contributing to the groups fighting in the streets, fighting for the dignity of those who visit us, and battling in every corner of this space of confrontation, making it a symbol of the anti-prison struggle.

For more than two months, Juan has been hospitalized at the Penitentiary Hospital of the former Santiago Penitentiary, where he has access to better care, palliative treatments, and, above all, greater closeness and contact with fellow inmates and family.

His condition is extremely serious: multiple diagnoses have revealed a cancerous tumor in his left hip with metastases in various parts of his body.

Aware of the severity of his condition, Juan, as expected, is determined to fight. His messages are of resistance and strength, of struggle and dignity. And we hope that the outpouring of solidarity on the streets will reflect this same sentiment. Because it is essential to connect the world from the outside and from prison. Because it is necessary to live up to Juan Aliste’s legacy and act accordingly.

Francisco Solar Domínguez Joaquín García Chancks

author: James McVicar
title: Hanson’s middle-class army assembles for Victorian state election
content:
Imagine Christmas family lunch, but everyone there is your racist uncle. Or try this: Akira Kurosawa’s 1954 masterpiece

Seven Samurai

, but instead of skilled swordsmen, it’s people who have spent years honing the art of giving people the creeps—and there are eight of them. 

Last Monday, Pauline Hanson was in Melbourne to announce One Nation’s first eight candidates for the upcoming Victorian state election. Among them was Warren Pickering, the party’s state leader, who will be contesting the seat of Pakenham. 

Pickering spent time in the Middle East as a combat engineer with the Australian military, but it was only later that he paid the supreme sacrifice, when he lost his job at mining giant BHP for heroically refusing the COVID jab. His pet conspiracy theory is the “fifteen-minute city”, a fanciful notion that the government is planning to build suburbs where shops, schools, and hospitals are all within easy reach. Keep dreaming, Warren!

Then there’s Colleen Harkin, formerly of the Liberal Party, who is One Nation’s candidate for the South-Eastern Metropolitan region in the upper house. She works at a hard-right think tank, the Institute of Public Affairs, a natural home for someone who

likened climate change education to child abuse

. 

The IPA does valuable research such as polling public attitudes towards the

Australian national anthem

, polling public attitudes towards

Australia Day

 and polling public attitudes towards the

Australian flag

. Many questions still remain unanswered, however. What percentage of the Australian population know

all

 the words to pub rock anthem “Khe Sanh”? How many Australians regularly throw a shrimp on the barbie?

Harkin’s bio on the IPA website adds that she “enjoys a good steak tartare”. There’s something unsettling but totally plausible about a vision of Hanson’s foot soldiers sitting around a table devouring plate after plate of raw meat.

The most disconcerting of the eight candidates is probably former criminal lawyer Mark Nicholson. His claim to fame is being the “brains” behind Pauline Hanson’s animated TV series

Please Explain

 and feature film

A Super Progressive Movie

. A sort of third-rate, Third Reich Walt Disney. He shares with his cartoon creations a certain two-dimensional, dead-behind-the-eyes look that’s hard to unsee.

Hanson’s first announced Victorian candidates are like stock characters from the far-right universe. For all the talk of being a party of “battlers”—a label which sticks no matter how many private jets and D&G galas Hanson racks up—One Nation’s state election line-up is decidedly middle class. 

Colleen Harkin hails from the traditional party of business owners big and small. Two of them—Nicholson and Aaron Sandford—are lawyers. Fiona Lopez is an HR manager and Rikkie-Lee Tyrrell a dairy farmer. Natalie Adams is a small business owner, and rounding out the list is Chris Burson, a Geelong councillor and ex-cop. In a word, the sort of people who are the backbone of the capitalist status quo. Nationalism, racism, authoritarianism and exploitation are the air they breathe.

Russian revolutionary Leon Trotsky wrote incisively about fascism as he watched it come to power in Italy, then in Germany. He understood well the middle-class roots of fascist politics, writing that “a particle of Hitler is lodged in every exasperated petty bourgeois” (that’s French for small-business owner). His solution to the problem—a socialist society that sweeps away once and for all the rule of the many over the few—is needed now more than ever.

author: By Camilla Donzelli, Contributor
title: Locked Up and Criminalized: People on the Move Face a Broken System on Crete’s Shores
content:
Crete, Greece — People on the move arriving on Crete are held in makeshift facilities where they have no rights, as authorities freeze asylum registration while implementing the EU’s contested new Migration and Asylum Pact. 


The abandoned Kitrenosis industrial complex sits along the highway connecting the cities of Rethymno and Heraklion, on Crete’s northern coast. The warehouses, disused for years, look out over a cliff that drops straight into the sea. Scattered across the outdoor lot are piles of objects hinting at a transient human presence: faded clothing, broken chargers, crumpled cigarette packs.


Discarded belongings are scattered across the ground outside of the abandoned Kitrenosis industrial complex. Photo contributed by Romanos Lioutas.


Crete has no dedicated reception system, and Kitrenosis is one of the stopgap solutions authorities have turned to after transferring people from the island’s southern shores, where boats arrive, to temporary holding sites in the north.


According to local media reports, the site was last used in

December 2025

, when it held more than 500 people. It has sat empty since, but inside one of the warehouses, traces of makeshift shelter remain. The space has no windows — a beam of sunlight creeping in through the gap in a broken gate is the only light inside the facility. The floor is littered with the remains of packaged food, half-empty water bottles, gym mats and flattened cardboard boxes.


In November 2025, the Italian organization Operazione Colomba published a

report

 confirming the deplorable conditions at Kitrenosis and the island’s two other temporary facilities: the former exhibition center Agia, located about twenty minutes from downtown Chania, and the old refrigerated storage unit inside the port of Heraklion. The report found that all three sites lacked basic infrastructure and essentials, such as beds, showers, toilets, and clean clothing, and suffered from frequent overcrowding and a lack of privacy.


As of July 2026, all three facilities sit empty, a lull attributed to bad weather slowing arrivals. However, the

latest data

 published by the independent organization Refugee Support Aegean puts the number of people who reached Crete in the first half of the year at roughly 8,500 — a figure confirming that the route from Libya to the island is now well-established, regardless of seasonal fluctuations.


The inside of the abandoned Kitrenosis industrial complex. Photo contributed by Romanos Lioutas.


Manufacturing an Emergency


“Crete has been a landing point for a long time. This isn’t new in the past year. What has changed is the political narrative,” Maria, an activist with the Chania-based migrant solidarity collective Steki Metanaston, told Unicorn Riot. As early as 2023, Refugee Support Aegean was already noting a

rise in arrivals

 to Crete, flagging the complete absence of adequate reception infrastructure and procedures. By 2024, the same organization reported a

further jump in landings

, with more than 5,000 people reaching the island.


It was 2025, however, that saw the sharpest spike in absolute numbers. According to

data

 released by Refugee Support Aegean, more than 20,000 people landed on Crete’s shores that year. This is a significant figure that made the island Greece’s main point of entry, but it needs context. The latest

report

 published by the Asylum Information Database (AIDA), the Greek Council for Refugees and the European Council on Refugees and Exiles (ECRE) confirms that the route has become well-established, while also pointing to an overall drop in arrivals nationwide — down 21% from 2024 to 2025.


That figure has been almost entirely absent from political and media discourse. Instead, the raw number of arrivals hitting Crete’s coastline has been wielded as a propaganda tool by the conservative New Democracy government, first elected in 2019 and now serving its second term.


“The numbers are clear: arrivals are trending downward. What’s changing are the routes,” said Michalis Markodimitrakis, a researcher at the Hellenic Mediterranean University and a member of Thalassa of Solidarity, a Heraklion-based collective. “Greek authorities know this, as this redistribution has been happening for more than two years. But they’ve deliberately chosen to do nothing. Because if you do nothing, you can present the situation as a crisis, and in times of crisis, extreme measures are justified and meet little opposition.”

title: Drei Jahre Anti-CSD-Naziprotest in Berlin – drei Jahre Misserfolg
content:
Im Vordergrund der Berichterstattung über den Berliner CSD 2026 steht derzeit der schreckliche islamistische Anschlag, der einer Mutter aus Polen das Leben kostete und viele weitere Personen verletzt und traumatisiert zurück ließ.


Im Vorfeld gab es weitere queerfeindliche Angriffe. So wurde auf Teilnehmende mit einer Airsoftpistole geschossen und erneut gab es Störaktionen von Berliner Neonazis. Um diese einzuordnen, gibt es hier einen Rückblick auf die Neonazi-Aktionen der letzten Jahre.


Die

Vorgeschichte


Am 27. Juli 2023 versuchte eine zehnköpfige Gruppe von Neonazis am Alexanderplatz abströmende Teilnehmer*innen des Berliner CSDs gewalttätig anzugreifen. Sie waren vermummt und mit Glasflaschen bewaffnet. Zwei Späher sicherten die Aktion nach außen ab. Die Angreifer konnten als Mitglieder des „III. Weg Berlin“ identifiziert werden.


2024 –

der erste Versuch

 neuer Neonazi-Strukturen


Im Jahr 2024 gründete sich die „Deutsche Jugend voran“ (DJV) und führte zu einer neuen Dynamik in der Neonaziszene. Vorrangig über soziale Medien wurden junge rechtsorientierte Jugendliche mobilisiert und zu niedrigschwelligen Aktionen eingeladen. Ein zentrales Thema war von Anfang an die Agitation gegen CSDs und Prides. Die erste wahrnehmbare Aktion von DJV war eine versuchte Störaktion am 27. Juli 2024 beim Berliner CSD. 38 Neonazis trafen sich dafür im Umfeld des Potsdamer Platzes und wurden dort von der Polizei festgesetzt. Mit dabei waren neben dem DJV-Chef Julian Milz auch Christopher Wetzels und Luka Zechel. Die Aktion erregte Aufmerksamkeit in der Lokalpresse und bei interessierten Antifaschist*innen, den CSD mit seinen mehreren hunderttausend Teilnehmenden beeinträchtigte sie nicht.


2025 –

Festigung der Zusammenhänge


Im Folgejahr meldete die DJV eine Gegenkundgebung zum Berliner CSD am 26. Juli 2025 an. Mit dabei waren 49 Neonazis, die sich aus der DJV, der Berliner „Heimat“ sowie neu gegründeten Strukturen, wie „Berliner Jugend“ (BJ) und „Deutsche Patrioten voran“ (DPV), rekrutierten. Der DJV-Chef Julian Milz saß zu dieser Zeit wegen mehrerer Gewalttaten in Untersuchungshaft und die Aktion wirkte sichtlich unkoordiniert. Die Neonazis bildeten aus ihren Transparenten einen Kokon, um sich gegen die zahlreich vertretene Presse abzuschirmen. Am Rande kam es zu mehreren Verhaftungen von Teilnehmer*innen.


Auch von dieser Kundgebung ging keine Störung für den Berliner CSD mit seinen 500.000 Teilnehmenden aus.


2026 –

Öffentlicher Ausdruck eines Niedergangs


Die Mobilisierung gegen den diesjährigen Berliner CSD zeigte die aktuelle Schwäche der Berliner Neonaziszene. Nach den Razzien bei der DJV ist diese nicht mehr wahrnehmbar. Die DPV und „Jägertruppe“ (JT) versuchen, diese Lücke zu füllen, aber scheitern gleich mehrfach. Zum einen verfügen sie nicht über die Führungspersonen, um die mobilisierbaren Neonazis an sich zu binden, zum anderen sind sie nicht in der Lage, strategische Schlüsse aus früheren Niederlagen zu ziehen. Während zu dem Naziprotest gegen den Berliner CSD am 25. Juli 2026 mit KI-Bildchen von Deutschlandfahne-schwingenden Menschenmassen vor dem Brandenburger Tor mobilisiert wurde, fanden sich vor Ort lediglich 18 Neonazis der beiden Gruppen ein. Weder „Heimat“ oder „III. Weg“ noch die Brandenburger Neonazis, die DPV und JT bei ihren Protesten in den letzten Monaten unterstützt hatten, sahen sich genötigt, an der Versammlung teilzunehmen. Stattdessen liefen die Neonazis wieder in die politisch gewollte Repression, die wahrnehmbaren Naziprotest am Rande der Veranstaltung zu unterbinden hatte. Mehrere der anwesenden Neonazis bekamen Anzeigen wegen Bewaffnung und Beleidigung. Eine zweite, für Abends angekündigte, Kundgebung wurde kurzfristig abgesagt.


Berlin ist nicht Bautzen oder Chemnitz. Die aktiven Neonazis treffen hier auf eine politische Stadtgesellschaft und eine große queere Szene, die Bilder wie in der ostdeutschen Provinz mit bedrohlichen Neonazi-Gegenmobilisierungen nicht möglich machen.


Der Blick auf die Stimmung gegenüber Queers in den Randbezirken zeichnet schon ein anderes Bild. Von hier aus rekrutiert sich auch ein Großteil der Berliner Neonazis. Auch in Marzahn-Hellersdorf versuchten die Neonazis Störaktionen gegen lokale Pride-Veranstaltungen. Weiterhin bleibt anti-queere Agiation eines der Hauptrekrutierungsfelder der Neonazigruppen, doch der Protest gegen den Berliner CSD ist ein fortgesetztes Mahnmal des Scheiterns für die Neonazi-Strukturen.

title: EEUU crea ofensiva abierta contra anarquistas y antifascistas en diversos países
content:
Foto de portada por Andrew Lichtenstein / Corbis

El gobierno de Donald Trump da un giro estratégico redefiniendo su doctrina de Seguridad Nacional y su política exterior al catalogar a diversas expresiones políticas bajo el concepto de “terrorismo político de extrema izquierda”, una ruta que guía su agenda en materia de seguridad con los países que considera sus aliados. El objetivo es investigar, desarticular y perseguir a ciertos movimientos sociales.

Bajo el liderazgo del secretario de Estado Marco Rubio, el pasado 16 de julio, se llevó a cabo la Reunión Ministerial sobre el Resurgimiento del Terrorismo Político , a través de la cual logró reunir en el Salón de Conferencias Loy Henderson - el espacio de reuniones más grande del Departamento de Estado-, delegaciones de 66 países, bajo la narrativa de combatir a "terroristas de extrema izquierda". Entre los países participantes figuran España, Argentina, Canadá, Alemania, Italia, Chile, Uruguay e Israel.

Este foro no es un hecho aislado, sino que forma parte de una estrategia más amplia diseñada y ejecutada desde la Casa Blanca, equiparando "actos de terrorismo doméstico”, como “asuntos prioritarios para las fuerzas del orden federal" de Estados Unidos, así lo estipula el Memorándum Presidencial de Seguridad Nacional N.º 7 (NSPM-7).

El NSPM-7 es el sostén del evento presidido por Marco Rubio, pero, sobre todo, de los compromisos asumidos en esta ofensiva conjunta contra el denominado “terrorismo de izquierda”. El Memorándum ya había sido firmado por el presidente Trump desde septiembre del 2025, en el cual instruye a todas las agencias de inteligencia y organismos de seguridad para los EEUU, así como a los encargados de impartir justicia, a desmantelar, desfinanciar y procesar a las redes calificadas como "terroristas de extrema izquierda".

Según el NSPM-7, el objetivo es “investigar, procesar y desarticular entidades e individuos involucrados en actos de violencia política”.

Según Trump, el móvil de la determinación tomada en términos de catalogar a ciertos grupos de “extrema izquierda” fue el asesinado de Charlie Kirk -influyente comentarista conservador que fue abatido por un disparo en ese mismo mes de septiembre-, clasificada por el mandatario como “horripilante”.

Este ha sido también el catalizador principal por el cual se convocó el encuentro Ministerial, donde Marco Rubio arremetió contra lo que calificó como "punto ciego" histórico en la doctrina antiterrorista occidental, justificando que “la violencia de extrema izquierda ha sido catalogada erróneamente por la academia y los medios como un ‘exceso trágico de idealismo’".

Bajo la misma línea y, siguiendo la ruta de la nueva doctrina de seguridad de los EEUU, Stephen Miller, asesor de seguridad nacional de la Casa Blanca, no dudó en denostar al movimiento antifascista (antifa) y grupos afines, señalándolos como una "infección" que busca el derrocamiento de los sistemas de gobierno occidentales, instando a los aliados a no ceder ante las apelaciones de "libertades civiles" de estos actores.

El departamento de Estado de EEUU cataloga como “terroristas de izquierda” a diversos grupos anarquistas y antifascistas, quienes se han sumado a las protestas en contra del genocidio de Israel frente a Palestina. Los mismos que han salido a las calles en favor de los derechos de los migrantes. Son quienes se han manifestado por el asesinato de George Floyd, a manos de un oficial de policía, en 2020 en Minneapolis, Minnesota. Son los mismos quienes salieron a las calles tras el asesinato del migrante mexicano Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, en este mes de julio del 2026, luego de que falleciera, tras recibir disparos por parte de agentes del Servicio de Inmigración y Control de Aduanas (ICE).

En la izquierda al oficial que provocó la muerte George Floyd. A la derecha el migrante mexicano, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, asesinado por diversos disparos del ICE en julio del 2026.

El Departamento de Estado ha clasificado directamente a diversos grupos bajo los términos de “extrema izquierda” como Organizaciones Terroristas Extranjeras (FTO) y Terroristas Globales Especialmente Designados (SDGT). Entre los grupos señalados destacan:
