author: L214
title: Adoption définitive de la loi d’urgence agricole : décryptage d’un fiasco démocratique
content:
Annoncé à la suite des mobilisations des agriculteurs lors de l’hiver 2025, le gouvernement a présenté en avril un projet de loi censé répondre à la crise agricole. Cette loi d’urgence agricole a été adoptée par les parlementaires le 21 juillet, à 296 voix contre 224 à l’Assemblée nationale et 214 voix contre 111 au Sénat. Retour sur une séquence qui a cristallisé toutes les tensions autour du modèle agricole français.

La loi d’urgence agricole propose de répondre aux crises rencontrées par le secteur de l’élevage d’une seule manière : en facilitant l’implantation et l’agrandissement de bâtiments d’élevages intensifs. Ce texte autorise la création, par voie d’ordonnance, d’un régime spécifique à l’élevage, dont le contenu n’a pas été rendu public. Le ministère de l’Agriculture affiche néanmoins ses intentions sans détour, précisant que le texte entend  « débloquer un certain nombre de projets agricoles qui sont inutilement freinés ». Il vise en particulier la création de 2 200 poulaillers intensifs, comme demandé par le syndicat de la volaille de chair ANVOL. Une mesure contre-productive, puisque l’intensification ne résout aucune des crises de l’élevage, et ne fait même que les aggraver.

→ En savoir plus sur notre décryptage du projet de loi

Le texte a été aggravé au fil de la navette parlementaire. L’amendement n°489 de la députée Hélène Laporte (Rassemblement National), adopté malgré l’avis contraire du gouvernement, impose que le futur cadre juridique ne soit pas plus  « défavorables aux élevages » que les règles européennes. Cet ajout présente un risque direct d’exclure les élevages bovins pourtant émetteurs de gaz à effet de serre et pollutions. L’amendement n°1091 du député Stéphane Travert (Ensemble pour la République) restreint quant à lui la participation du public aux consultations sur les élevages intensifs aux seules personnes  « justifiant d’un intérêt à agir » géographique, visant à écarter les associations nationales de ces débats , quand bien même les pollutions peuvent s’étendre sur un large périmètre. Supprimée après le passage au Sénat, cette disposition a finalement été retenue en Commission mixte paritaire, malgré les inquiétudes du ministère de la Transition écologique.

Le texte a également introduit un arsenal juridique visant à criminaliser les lanceurs d’alerte qui documentent la réalité des élevages intensifs . Introduit par l’amendement n°1114 du député Jean-René Cazeneuve (EPR), l’article 18 bis crée une circonstance aggravante spécifique à l’intrusion dans les locaux agricoles. Au Sénat, l’amendement n°COM-151 des rapporteurs Laurent Duplomb, Franck Menonville et Pierre Cuypers précise que cet article s’applique aux « activités d’élevage, d’abattage ou de découpe et de préparation des viandes et des produits assimilés » . Aucune clause de sauvegarde pour les lanceurs d’alerte n’a été adoptée : alors que ce texte cherche à multiplier les élevages intensifs, il développe simultanément les moyens d’en empêcher la documentation .

→ En savoir plus sur les débats à l’Assemblée nationale

C’est dans ce climat de tension, y compris au sein du bloc central, que le projet de loi a été adopté : 296 voix pour, issues d’une majorité des députés d’Ensemble pour la République jusqu’à Horizons ainsi que de l’ensemble des députés de la Droite Républicaine au Rassemblement national, contre 224 voix, portées en majorité par les députés des groupes de gauche. Malgré les nombreuses controverses, le texte a reconduit une fracture politique gauche/droite. On peut néanmoins noter que la loi Duplomb de 2025 avait été adoptée avec 316 voix favorables, contre 296 seulement pour ce texte. Il existe donc une prise de conscience chez un nombre croissant de députés, encore insuffisante, mais réelle.

La canicule et ses millions d’animaux morts de chaleur ont occupé les débats, mais selon les groupes, les conclusions à tirer de cette hécatombe ont été radicalement opposées. Si les députés de tout groupe politique ont dénoncé les ravages de la canicule, seuls ceux situés à gauche de l’hémicycle ont fait le lien avec le modèle d’élevage intensif que ce même texte cherche à faciliter. Benoît Biteau (Écologistes) a notamment rappelé les chiffres des surmortalités :  « Face au dérèglement climatique qui apporte son lot de canicules, on voudrait continuer à agrandir les élevages industriels alors même qu’on enregistre 1 200 % de mortalité en plus chez les volailles, 55 % chez les porcs, 40 % chez les bovins. Mais bien …

author: Tobias Sennhauser
title: Rückblick auf die Sommersession 2026
content:
Mercosur-Freihandelsabkommen


Das Freihandelsabkommen zwischen den EFTA-Staaten und Mercosur (

26.033

) soll den Handel mit Brasilien, Argentinien, Paraguay und Uruguay öffnen. Der Nationalrat lehnt die Vorlage mit 96 zu 86 Stimmen bei 9 Enthaltungen knapp ab. Zuvor waren mehrere Begleitmassnahmen gescheitert: die Übernahme der EU-Entwaldungsverordnung (108 zu 83 Stimmen), ein Agrarkredit von 880 Millionen Franken über acht Jahre (94 zu 91 Stimmen) sowie Anträge zu einem Amazonienfonds und gegen Zwangsarbeit. Nun ist der Ständerat am Zug.


SP und Grüne stimmten gegen die Vorlage, dafür waren FDP und GLP. Den Ausschlag gaben einige Nein-Stimmen aus der SVP- und der Mitte-Fraktion. Der Schweizer Bauernverband warnte vor zusätzlichen Importen und Druck auf die einheimischen Märkte. Der Wirtschaftsdachverband economiesuisse spricht hingegen von einem «fatalen Zeichen für den Wirtschaftsstandort» und fordert eine Korrektur durch den Ständerat.


Einschätzung von Tier im Fokus (TIF):

 Dieses Abkommen hätte Importe von Fleisch aus Ländern mit tieferen Tierschutz- und Umweltstandards erleichtert. Dieses Fleisch käme aus Produktionssystemen, die mit Entwaldung und Massentierhaltung verbunden sind. Wir lehnen das Freihandelsabkommen mit den Mercosur-Staaten ab und appellieren an den Ständerat, der grossen Kammer zu folgen und die Vorlage zu versenken.


Stopfleber-Initiative


Die Volksinitiative «Ja zum Importverbot für Stopfleber» (

24.089

) will die Einfuhr von Stopfleber verbieten. Nachdem sich der Nationalrat in der Frühjahrssession als Erstrat für einen indirekten Gegenentwurf (25.404) aussprach, folgte ihm nun der Ständerat mit 24 zu 15 Stimmen bei 3 Enthaltungen. Der Gegenentwurf verzichtet auf ein Importverbot und setzt stattdessen auf die bereits eingeführte Deklarationspflicht: Ab 2027 müssen Produkte von gestopften Enten und Gänsen den Hinweis tragen, dass sie unter für Tiere schmerzhaften Bedingungen erzeugt wurden. Der Bund soll die Importe beobachten und dem Parlament alle fünf Jahre Bericht erstatten.


Die bürgerliche Mehrheit und der Bundesrat lehnen ein Importverbot ab und verweisen auf internationale Handelsverpflichtungen und die schwierige Kontrolle verarbeiteter Produkte.


Einschätzung von Tier im Fokus (TIF):

 Eine Deklarationspflicht ist ein Hohn angesichts des Leids der Tiere. Wir halten an der Initiative und damit auch am Importverbot fest.


Importverbot für tierquälerisch erzeugte Pelze


Der Bundesrat verlängert am 5. Juni 2026 die Übergangsbestimmungen des Pelz-Importverbots, das am 1. Juli 2025 in Kraft getreten ist. Neu dürfen tierquälerisch erzeugte Pelzerzeugnisse erst ab dem 1. Juli 2029 nicht mehr eingeführt und ab dem 1. Juli 2030 nicht mehr verkauft werden. Die Pelzbranche soll damit Zeit erhalten, ihre Produktionssysteme an ein geplantes Zertifizierungsprogramm für angeblich nicht-tierquälerisch erzeugte Pelze anzupassen.


Einschätzung von Tier im Fokus (TIF): Für uns ist unverständlich, wieso die Pelzindustrie mehr Zeit erhält. Die Produktion von Pelzen geschieht meist in tierquälerischer, in der Schweiz verbotenen Haltungsbedingungen. Für die sogenannten Pelztiere bedeutet jeder Tag, an dem wir warten, Leid und Tod.


Kultiviertes Fleisch


Eine Motion (

23.3941

) verlangt, die Zulassungs- und Bewilligungsverfahren für neuartige Lebensmittel, insbesondere kultiviertes Fleisch und Produkte aus Präzisionsfermentation, zu vereinfachen und zu beschleunigen. Der Nationalrat hatte den Vorstoss in der Sondersession vom Mai 2025 mit 94 zu 87 Stimmen bei 8 Enthaltungen angenommen. Der Ständerat lehnte ihn am 8. Juni 2026 auf Antrag seiner Kommission und des Bundesrates stillschweigend ab. Damit ist die Motion erledigt.


Einschätzung von Tier im Fokus (TIF):

 Kultiviertes Fleisch könnte dazu beitragen, die Tötung von Tieren mittelfristig stark zu reduzieren. Für uns ist es deshalb unverständlich, gewaltfreie Alternativen zu blockieren. Die Ablehnung dieser Motion zementiert den Status quo der Tiernutzung.


Tiertransporte


Ab dem 1. Juli 2026 dürfen Tiere neu auch nachts sowie an Sonn- und Feiertagen transportiert werden. Bisher waren nur Transporte von Schlachttieren und Sportpferden vom Nacht- und Sonntagsfahrverbot ausgenommen; alle anderen Lebendtiertransporte brauchten eine kostenpflichtige Sonderbewilligung mit 48 Stunden Vorlauf. title: Erfolg: Pläne für die weltweit erste Oktopusfarm eingestellt
content:
Update vom 27. Juli 2026 


Gute Nachrichten: Weltweit erste Oktopusfarm auf Gran Canaria wird nicht gebaut 


Die weltweit erste Oktopusfarm auf Gran Canaria wird nicht gebaut. Der spanische Konzern Nueva Pescanova hat das Projekt endgültig eingestellt und seinen Antrag auf eine Fabrik im Hafen von in Las Palmas zurückgezogen. Damit bleibt Hunderttausenden Oktopussen Gefangenschaft, Leid und eine grausame Tötung erspart.  


Zuvor hatten Wissenschaftler:innen, Tierschutzorganisationen und engagierte Menschen weltweit starken Widerstand gegen die Pläne geleistet. Allein PETA-Unterstützer:innen verschickten mehr als 200.000 E-Mails an die Verantwortlichen auf Gran Canararia, darunter 45.000 aus Deutschland. Wir wandten uns zudem an EU-Politiker:innen, demonstrierten mit einem Riesenkraken vor Spanischen Konsulaten, richteten Briefe und Petitionen an die zuständigen Behörden auf Gran Canaria und arbeiteten in der international Octooalition mit mehr als 30 NGOs zusammen.  


Wir freuen uns über diesen Erfolg für die Kraken und bedanken uns bei allen Unterstützer:innen.  


Kraken sind empfindsame Lebewesen und gehören nicht in Gefangenschaft.


Originaltext  


Auf Gran Canaria soll die erste 

Intensivtierhaltung

 für 

Kraken

 entstehen! Laut den Plänen des betreibenden Unternehmens würden in der kommerziellen Anlage jedes Jahr Hunderttausende der hochintelligenten Tiere in beengten Becken gezüchtet und getötet werden. Ihr 

Fleisch

 soll vermarktet werden. Doch die Wissenschaft warnt: Eine solche Haltung würde für die Tiere extremes und anhaltendes Leid bedeuten. Bitte helfen Sie uns, diese grausamen Pläne zu stoppen! 


Kraken sind intelligent, komplex und faszinierend 


Kraken sind empfindsame Lebewesen, die Freude, Neugierde, 

Schmerz

 und Angst fühlen können. Die ausgesprochen intelligenten Tiere nutzen beispielsweise Muscheln als Schutzschilde, stehlen Köder aus Fischfallen und befreien sich aus Aquarien. Es gibt sogar Kraken, die ihr Zuhause hübsch dekorieren. Die Tiere kommunizieren mittels Farbwechseln und Farbsignalen miteinander – bis heute ist der Mensch nicht in der Lage, ihre Sprache genau zu verstehen. 


Kraken in der 

Aquakultur

 einzusperren, würde zu unnatürlichen Verhaltensweisen wie Aggressionen, Kannibalismus, Verletzungen und zum Tod führen. Die auf engstem Raum gehaltenen Tiere würden miteinander kämpfen und versuchen, zu entkommen. 


Eine artgerechte Versorgung ist nicht möglich 


Derzeit gelten in Spanien keine gesetzlichen Vorgaben zum Schutz von Kraken. So sind die Tiere skrupellosen Firmen ausgeliefert, die sie unter allen denkbaren Bedingungen halten dürfen. Sie können ihnen Schmerzen und Leid zufügen, ohne je dafür belangt zu werden. Am Ende ihres qualvollen Lebens werden die Kraken getötet – vermutlich ohne Betäubung. Wenn man ihnen das Gehirn aufschneidet oder den Kopf einschlägt, werden sie bei vollem Bewusstsein in nackte Panik verfallen und quälende Schmerzen erleiden. 


Die Wissenschaft ist sich einig: Kraken sind empfindsame Lebewesen. Es ist schlichtweg unmöglich, sie in solchen Anlagen zu halten, ohne ihnen dabei Leid zuzufügen. Faszinierende Kraken oder andere Tiere in ein kahles Becken zu sperren, ist Tierquälerei. 


Kraken-Farm schädlich für die Umwelt 


Eine Kraken-Farm ist jedoch nicht nur grausam für die Tiere, sondern schadet auch der Umwelt. Um die Kraken zu ernähren, müssten wild lebende Meerestiere gefangen werden, was die 

Überfischung der Meere

 vorantreibt. Fischpopulationen werden weiter dezimiert und das Ökosystem des Meeres wird immer mehr gestört. 


Jetzt lesen


Fische


Lachszucht: Alle Informationen über Tierleid, Gesundheit und Co.


Die industrielle Lachszucht an Land ist genauso unethisch wie die im Meer. Darum leiden Lachse in der Aquakultur. Jetzt lesen!


Jetzt lesen


Helfen Sie uns, die Mega-Lachsfabrik in der Schweiz zu verhindern 


In der Schweiz ist der Bau einer großen Lachsfabrik geplant, in der jährlich bis zu 4.000 Tonnen Lachs- „Produkte“ produziert und bis zu 1,5 Millionen Lachse gemästet werden sollen. Unterstützen Sie jetzt unsere Petition und helfen Sie uns, dieses tierquälerische Vorhaben zu verhindern.  


 Jetzt helfen!

author: Unknown
title: Geothermal project temporarily halted after protests by villagers and environmental activists
content:
Resistance by villagers and environmental activists against the geothermal power plant (GPP) project of U.S.-based IGNIS H2 Energy Generation Inc. continues in the village of Lîcik, located on the border between the districts of Varto in Muş and Karlıova in Bingöl.


In the face of resolute protests by local residents, the construction equipment was withdrawn from the site the previous day. The village was surrounded by a large number of gendarmerie personnel this morning.


With entry and exit routes closed, company officials re-entered the village with construction machinery and resumed work.


In response, residents of Lîcik, people from neighboring villages, environmental activists from Varto, and representatives of political parties gathered in the area.


Following talks between company officials and the crowd that marched to the construction site, work was temporarily suspended, and the construction equipment was once again removed from the area.


In a press statement, representatives of the Peri Valley Environmental Protection Platform called for the promises made to be honored and demanded the complete cancellation of the project.


The platform said it had been given a three-to-four-day period, during which it would continue its legal, political, and public campaign against the project.


The Varto Ecology Platform also stressed that the struggle should not be left solely to bureaucratic negotiations and called for broader participation by local residents.


Environmental activists argue that the geothermal project would harm agriculture and livestock farming and poses a risk of water and soil contamination.


The platforms emphasized that the project is not only a concern for Lîcik, but also for the surrounding villages, and reiterated their demand that it be canceled entirely.


Following the temporary suspension of the project, the villagers announced that they would continue their round-the-clock vigil at the site as well as their legal efforts against the project.

author: David Swanson
title: Videos from the World Social Forum
content:
By World BEYOND War, August 9, 2026


For background, read:


Nonviolent Citizen Resistance Moves the World Social Forum Forward in Benin


Here are some video recordings from the World Social Forum:


Intercontinental Dialogues on the Environmental Crisis:


The session brings together activists and scholars from different traditions who exchange perspectives on the ecological crisis, peace, democracy, and social justice, while exploring the wisdom resources that inspire their movements. It examines whether today’s environmental, political, and social crises reflect a deeper civilizational crisis, and discusses pathways toward ecological justice, peace, and a more sustainable future.


Standing with Sudan: Humanitarian action and global advocacy:


The session explores how civil society, humanitarian organizations, grassroots movements, and international networks are responding to the ongoing crisis in Sudan, and how they can work further through coordinated action and solidarity. The panel highlights initiatives supporting affected communities, particularly women, children, and displaced populations, and also examines how global advocacy can influence international actors, strengthen humanitarian responses and promote a nonviolent path toward des-escalation.


Grand débat (in French):


Video here on Facebook

.


During the debate, I said this as introductory remarks:


Grand Débat sur la paix, le désarmement et l’autodétermination des peuples


Mot introductif de Guy Feugap, Organisateur Africain de World BEYOND


C’est en principe Tord Björk qui devrait être à cette place, afin de s’exprimer en personne au nom de Internatinoal Peace Bureau, une organisation fondée dès 1891, sur cet important débat sur la paix. Mais il n’a pu être là, car il a été refoulé avec plusieurs autres personnes dès son arrivée à Cotonou.


Moi je suis Guy Feugap, Organisateur Africain de World BEYOND War, partenaire de IPB. Je tiens à vous adresser un message, simple, que je partage avec Tord : la jeunesse africaine remportera la lutte pour la liberté pour nous tous !


Dans le cadre de cette préparation au Forum social mondial au Bénin, IPB, World BEYOND War et l’Assemblée sociale mondiale des luttes et des résistances ont coopéré avec le Réseau pour la paix et la justice climatique. Ce réseau, né en Suède, s’étend désormais à travers le continent africain, au Congo et en Afrique de l’Est, parmi les jeunes, en associant la revendication de la paix à celle d’une transition climatique juste.


Au cours de ce processus, nous avons pu organiser plusieurs réunions en ligne avec de nombreux jeunes militants venus de Turquie, du Portugal, de Via Campesina, des syndicats, des mouvements de défense des migrants, des mouvements pour la paix et pour le climat, et bien d’autres encore. Nous avons été particulièrement touchés par le témoignage de Burry Turkana, originaire de Gambie, qui nous a fait part directement depuis la caravane en route du Sénégal vers le Bénin, ainsi que par celui de Jackson Kisangani, originaire de l’est du Congo, l’un des principaux organisateurs du mouvement international pour la paix et la justice climatique, depuis le cœur des zones de guerre où les jeunes se mobilisent pour protéger l’environnement et construire un avenir meilleur sans guerre.


Notre message est désormais clair : nous devons nous unir dans une action commune pour la paix sur Terre et la paix avec la Terre, et pourquoi pas à travers une journée d’action commune internationale en faveur de cette vision qui consiste à rassembler les préoccupations sociales et écologiques au sein d’un appel unifié à la paix. Un appel à la résistance contre le modèle de développement actuel oppressif, qui exploite les êtres humains et la nature et qui est contrôlé par des puissances occidentales de plus en plus racistes. Nous, les peuples de tous les continents, devons nous unir contre ce modèle qui opprime les populations tant dans le Sud que dans le Nord.


Partons de ce moment inspirant à Cotonou pour lancer un mouvement rural et urbain inspiré par la nouvelle dynamique créée par ce Forum social mondial, par les caravanes pour la terre et l’eau, et par la nécessité de décoloniser le monde entier. Un mouvement uni par un appel à la paix sur Terre et à la paix avec la Terre !


Globalisons la lutte et que vive la jeunesse africaine !


Je vous remercie

Toby creeping up to take a photo of the spoonie. Credit: Hai-Dang Phan


M

ud envelopes my feet, dark and cool, slick with sea. It’s low tide, and the sea has receded to reveal a massive mudflat stretching as far as the eye can see. We are at Tân Thành beach, roughly two hours by car from Saigon, on the coast of Vietnam’s Mekong Delta. It is early January—the dry season in the tropical south—when huge numbers of migratory shorebirds can be found on this expanse.


Following the lead of our guide, Ba and I cautiously navigate the ankle-deep water of a tidal channel. From atop the sea wall a storm-grey heron watches our slow progress. To the north and east, fishing huts perch high on bamboo posts. To the south, giant steel transmission towers dominate the horizon as they march offshore towards rows of wind turbines. On the muddy backshore, fishing boats lie stranded with nowhere to go, outsized eyes painted on their fading prows. They are the same kind of boats that my family used when we fled the country over forty years ago.


We are sloshing across the mudflats this morning because somewhere out there might be a spoon-billed sandpiper, one of the world’s rarest shorebirds and a critically endangered species. A few regular, if elusive, birds are recorded every winter here at

Tân Thành

. Our guide is

Bùi Thành Trung

—or, as he prefers it, Toby. He’s one the best birders in Vietnam, a shorebird specialist with a knack for finding “spoonies”, as he affectionately calls them.


“Stay inside the channel!” Toby shouts, spotting scope balanced over a shoulder. We have about two hours before the tide makes it too dangerous to be wandering the mudflats. We aren’t the only ones making the most of low tide. Further out, dozens of local women are digging for clams.


The watery path leads to the first set of makeshift bamboo “monkey bridges” we’ll need to cross. My seventy-four-year-old father stops in his tracks, considers the 30-metre obstacle course, his old knees, his bad balance, and tells us “kids” to go ahead without him. But Toby has just the pep talk. “You’re still cứng” he says, clenching his fist and smiling—s

till hard

,

still tough

. That’s all it takes; Ba comes along.


There is something simultaneously exhilarating and comforting about being at Tân Thành. There’s no point bothering with footwear because they’ll only get stuck in the mud. Earlier, the act of taking off our shoes before setting foot on the mudflat called to mind the familiar Asian custom before entering a home. We are, after all, guests here in what Toby calls “Spoonyland”.


F

or the past few days, Ba and I have been on a meandering road trip through the Mekong Delta, from Saigon to the river town of

Châu Đốc

 near Cambodia. He wanted to show me some of the places where he was stationed and fought during the war, some fifty years ago, as an officer of a patrol boat unit in the South Vietnamese Navy.


Today, we return to our primary mission: to experience Vietnam through its birds. Whenever we returned to Vietnam in the past, we usually spent all our time visiting family. For once, I wanted to see the country itself. On this matter, Ba and I found common ground. While he’s no avid birdwatcher like me, Ba likes a good challenge and wants to see as much of Vietnam as he still can.


Given the country’s long, distinctive coastline, a trip focused on shorebirds seemed essential, and searching for the spoon-billed sandpiper offered us a chance to do something extraordinary: witness a bird brought back from the brink of extinction. The guide I initially contacted was unavailable, but put me in touch with his friend, Toby. I knew about Toby from eBird, an online platform that birdwatchers the world over use to record and share sightings. Toby was the top “lister” in Vietnam, with 750 species observed—a distinction that filled me with unexpected pride when I first saw his Vietnamese name on top of a leaderboard stacked with Anglo-sounding names.


Toby studied business administration and held a decent desk job for an industrial sales company. Then, one day, a brief encounter with a sunbird ignited his passion for birds. More than ten years later, Toby has explored nearly every province in Vietnam on a quest to photograph every bird species in the country.


R

eaching the sandbar peninsula, we catch our first glimpse of the shorebirds. I can’t make most of them out; they are only shapes flying back and forth. The birds are everywhere, in …

title: Ermenek maden katliamının baş şüphelisi 8 yıl sonra yakalandı
content:
Mersin İl Jandarma Komutanlığı ekipleri, Karaman’ın Ermenek ilçesinde 18 maden işçisinin hayatını kaybettiği maden katliamının baş şüphelisi olarak aranan ve hakkında 21 yıl kesinleşmiş hapis cezası bulunan Y.Ö.’yü (49), yaklaşık 8 yıl sonra Silifke’de yakaladı.

Mersin İl Jandarma Komutanlığı JASAT (Jandarma Suç Araştırma Timi) ekipleri, Ermenek ilçesinde 2014 yılında 18 maden işçisinin hayatını kaybettiği maden kazasının baş şüpheli olarak aranan Y.Ö.’nün yakalanması için çalışma başlattı.

Hakkında 21 yıl kesinleşmiş hapis cezası bulunan ve yaklaşık 8 yıldır firari olduğu belirlenen Y.Ö.’nün, yapılan kapsamlı araştırmalar sonucu Silifke ilçe merkezinde olduğu tespit edildi. JASAT ekiplerince düzenlenen operasyonla yakalanan Y.Ö., gözaltına alındı. Y.Ö., işlemlerinin ardından cezaevine teslim edildi.

author: Liza Gross
title: Wildfire Smoke Now Threatens Prenatal Health More Than Harmful Human Emissions
content:
Increasing wildfires are offsetting the gains from reducing vehicle and industry sources of air pollution.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation .

In 1965, a presidential advisory panel issued a report warning that pervasive chemical and carbon pollution was harming environmental health and changing the climate. Five years later, President Richard Nixon signed the Clean Air Act.

Since that 1970 law and its amendments were passed, combined emissions of a half dozen harmful air pollutants from vehicles and industrial sources have decreased by nearly 80 percent .

But mounting evidence shows that pollution from wildfire smoke is eclipsing those air-quality gains. The unchecked burning of fossil fuels is creating warmer, drier conditions that make wildfires more intense and destructive, and blanket communities in toxic smoke that is more harmful than pollution from other sources.

Now, a new study shows that smoke from wildfires is also reversing the health benefits of reducing air pollution for society’s most vulnerable population: babies in the womb.

Increasing wildfire activity is “systematically offsetting prenatal air quality gains” from reducing emissions from vehicles, refineries, factories and other human sources, researchers from the University of Maryland, College Park, report in the study, published Thursday in Frontiers in Environmental Health.

Low-income, rural and Indigenous populations bore the disproportionate burden of wildfire’s contribution to poor air quality, the authors found.

The major contribution of the study is its focus on a “very specific population that is quite at risk for adverse health outcomes,” said senior author Michel Boudreaux, associate professor of health policy and management. “We were looking at infants that were born and what their exposure was like during the prenatal period.”

Prenatal exposure to wildfire smoke significantly increases the likelihood that babies will be born too early or too small , raising their risk of dying early or developing chronic respiratory conditions and other diseases later in life.

The University of Maryland team studied how wildfire smoke and human sources of air pollution changed across the contiguous United States between 2003 and 2019, looking at air pollution data from the Environmental Protection Agency and live birth records. (The EPA datasets do not include years beyond 2019.)

To understand how much wildfire smoke contributed to unhealthy air exposures for unborn babies, the team used computer models to estimate exposures to fine particle pollution, or PM2.5, from both human sources, such as cars and industry, and natural sources, like wildfires. The team modeled air quality without emissions from fires to calculate how much of that total pollution came from wildfires.

The researchers obtained data for nearly 65 million babies born over 16 years and determined how many days they were exposed in the womb to the EPA threshold for unhealthy air.

Average daily prenatal exposure to air pollution from human sources dropped by 37 percent during that time, the analysis found, but contributions from wildfires doubled, offsetting those gains.

Although the study does not integrate data on preterm birth, birthweight or other outcomes, it is a very good exposure-characterization study, said Ilona Jaspers, an inhalation toxicologist and professor of pediatrics at the University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill, who was not involved in the study. “What this study does do well is confirm and expand the well-established finding that ambient PM2.5 in the United States is increasingly wildfire-dominated, offsetting Clean Air Act gains, but applies a birth-weighted lens to it,” she said.

Wildfire smoke exposures are likely to have vast public health consequences, Jaspers said. In previous studies , Jaspers and her colleagues used prescription insurance claim data to show that exposure during specific perinatal periods can lead to childhood respiratory diseases.

The research doesn’t look at how much time the mother was spending outside, if she wore an N95 mask or if she had an air-filtration system in her home, which Boudreaux acknowledges as a limitation of the study. But data sources like Purple Air that track wildfire smoke are detecting a large amount of pollution in the form of a PM2.5 inside people’s homes, he said.

author: Shan Kenshin Ecaldre
title: Experts challenge gov’t claims on Pax Silica
content:
The AI-assisted illustration of the proposed 1,600-hectare industrial hub to be located in New Clark City in Capas, Tarlac. Photo courtesy of the People’s Television Network

Pax Silica follows a pattern in which developing countries bear the environmental and social costs of technologies that largely benefit wealthier economies.

CABUYAO CITY, Laguna — Engineers and information technology professionals critical of the proposed Pax Silica data center and artificial intelligence (AI) hub said that the Marcos Jr. administration is making promises that fail to address the project’s social and environmental impact.

In a statement released on Aug. 4, Pro-people Engineers and Leaders (PROPEL) and the Computer Professionals’ Union (CPU) disputed recent remarks by Information and Communications Technology Secretary Henry Aguda defending the controversial project planned for New Clark City.

The groups said that government agencies have repeatedly introduced “technofixes” in response to concerns over water use, energy demand, and land conversion. They stressed that these measures only reveal the project’s weak planning and foreign-oriented character.

“It’s clear that in the face of the consistent opposition to the Pax Silica project, the different departments of the administration are throwing one technofix after another that will supposedly solve all the problems related to the project,” the groups said in a statement. “At best, it reveals how poorly conceived the project is from the beginning; at worst, it exposes the lengths at which the Marcos Jr. administration is willing to go just to cater to the economic agenda of another country.”

PROPEL challenged government assurances that advanced cooling technologies could minimize water use in the proposed AI facilities.

The group observed that some hyperscale data centers abroad have promoted closed-loop cooling systems that recycle water but stressed that such systems require large amounts of electricity. Desalination, another option reportedly being considered, would also consume substantial energy and require additional infrastructure along the Zambales coast or Manila Bay.

Engineers warned that cooling requirements in the Philippines could be significantly higher than in temperate countries because of tropical heat, with temperatures reaching 40°C in some areas.

“With all the lack of transparency behind the project, and all the sudden promises that they can address the water problem, we can only expect what communities in the US are already experiencing around data centers, unusable tap water, water shortages, and other disruptions,” the statement said.

The warning echoes growing international criticism of large AI facilities which have been linked to heavy water consumption and local resource conflicts in several parts of the United States.

The groups also questioned the projected electricity demand, citing BCDA estimates of three to five gigawatts.

According to PROPEL, meeting such demand through solar power could require thousands of additional hectares of land. The statement also raised concerns over the possible use of off-grid fossil fuel plants and generators, practices already documented in some overseas data center complexes.

The engineers said that government discussions of nuclear energy as a possible long-term power source introduce further technical, financial, and social issues that have not been publicly debated.

“The massive projected demand for electricity will only lead to even more land being ceded to the project,” the group said.

CPU said that government comparisons with existing local data centers are misleading because Pax Silica is designed primarily for AI development and training, requiring far greater computing power.

CPU chairperson Ian Aragoza said that newer Philippine hyperscale facilities consume less than 100 megawatts each, while the DICT itself has projected at least 400 megawatts of data center consumption in New Clark City.

“This means we can’t simply rely on old studies and past experiences,” the statement said. “Pax Silica is trying to introduce something new altogether.”

The group said AI-focused facilities differ substantially from conventional cloud and enterprise data centers, making previous impact assessments insufficient.

The groups said that Pax Silica follows a pattern in which developing countries bear the environmental and social costs of technologies that largely benefit wealthier economies.

author: winter oak
title: Paranoia or perceptivity?
content:
A book review by Paul Cudenec, who reads it

here


In July, I

mentioned

 in passing that the legendary counter-cultural artist Robert Crumb, now nearly 83 years old, had spoken out about possible industrial manipulation behind the Covid debacle. [1]


Further investigation led me to get hold of his new cartoon book (the first in 23 years), which in English is called

Tales of Paranoia

. [2]


Because I have the French version,

Chroniques de la Paranoia

, I cannot

quote

 Crumb by absurdly trying to translate his translated words back into English, but I can

describe

 what he says. [3]


As is apparent from the book’s title, the

framing

 he chooses for his illustrated reflections is that he is questioning whether the dark suspicions swirling around in his head have any basis in reality.


He starts off by admitting to his own tendency to “join the dots” in an imaginative manner and wondering whether he has not inherited a certain something from his mother, who apparently once opened up the family TV set to search for the bugging device she thought her husband had planted in it.


But Crumb quickly moves on to the heart of the matter by suggesting that the “pandemic” was a scam conducted by Big Pharma and the medical-industrial complex.


Like all good Covid sceptics, he has done his own research. For instance, he cites an article from

The New York Times

 in January 2018 warning of the threat of a global flu pandemic and calling for huge amounts of money to be invested in vaccine research.


Early in the book, we see Crumb facing the righteous wrath of a doctor friend in the USA, telling him that Covid was not a

political

 issue on which it was possible to express a personal opinion, but a

scientific

 one, in which his duty was to

trust the experts

.


This conversation keeps him awake half the night, tossing and turning, and he finds himself wondering whether he will be targeted in some way for challenging the official narrative.


While these fears and doubts do not completely disappear – especially the metaphysical doubts expressed in his one-to-ones with God – the series of cartoon strips shows an increasing certainty with regard to the Covid machinations.


The Rand Corporation appears to have helped in this process, with a

report

 it issued in 2021 entitled

Detecting Conspiracy Theories on Social Media

. [4]


Analysing the language it uses, Crumb asks who exactly decides what information is “factual”, or what sources “reliable” or “unreliable”, and on what exact basis such decisions are made – he notes that we are again being told to trust the so-called experts.


He also describes how the report identifies four kinds of “

conspiracy theory

” [5] – those involving visits from extra-terrestrials, those about the dangers of vaccines, those about the origins of Covid and those warning of a planned genocide of the white race.


And he points out how questioning the Covid agenda is thus neatly sandwiched between “crazy” UFO theories and “far right” racial theories in a pincer movement aiming to discredit by association.


To illustrate the scope of the shadowy networks running our world from behind the scenes, he focuses in on one individual whom he names only as “Deep State Woman”, explaining that he does not want her to be able to sue him!


Having shown us how he was accused by the “trust the Science” crowd of having crossed over to the “dark side” by trusting his own brain instead, Crumb concludes by devoting a whole page to listing some of the many bodies that he says put fear in his belly and spread paranoia.


These include the CIA, Mossad, AIPAC, the Federal Reserve, the World Bank, Blackrock, the oil industry, the pharmaceuticals industry, the 5G industry, Google, Facebook, Microsoft, GAVI, the Wellcome Trust, the WHO, the

WEF

, [6] the

Bill Gates Foundation

, [7] the

Carnegie Endowment

 [8] and the

Rockefeller Foundation

… [9]


Many years ago I was greatly struck by a cartoon that I came across in one of the American anarchist magazines that I used to devour at the time – I have no idea which one now.


This showed the gradual arrival of what is called “civilization” in a small corner of the USA: in 12 frames we see the transformation of an idyllic corner of countryside into an ugly mess of buildings, roads and overhead wires.


I always kept it in the back of my mind and it served as a visual underpinning of my personal understanding of the whole vile “

development

” …

author: The Canadian Press
title: Climate change made Ontario, N.W.T. fire conditions roughly twice as likely: report
content:
The conditions underlying intense July wildfires in Ontario and Northwest Territories were made roughly twice as likely due to human-induced climate change, said a new report published Thursday.


The report by an international team of scientists says what were once rare fire conditions are now increasingly likely today due to climate change, driven by the burning of fossil fuels.


“The geographic spread of these fires is scary and shows that despite preparedness from wildfire governance, adaptation alone is not enough,” said Theodore Keeping, a co-author and Imperial College London research associate.


“We need to rapidly move away from fossil fuels to avoid events like this becoming even more of a reality.”


The

World Weather Attribution

 report says early observations indicate the hot, dry and windy conditions fuelling fires in Northwest Territories could now be expected to occur every two to six years, and every six to 15 years in Ontario.


In a world without human-caused climate change, the report suggests those conditions would have been much rarer, or less than once in 40 years.


Early estimates suggest this is the worst wildfire season on record in Ontario and in Northwest Territories’ top 10, as measured by area burned.


The study garnered the attention of the United Nations climate chief, who said the science backed up “what the people on the front lines already know.”


“Humanity’s addiction to burning massive amounts of coal, oil and gas is heating our planet, turning more of Canada’s vast forests into tinderboxes, and spreading dangerous smoke far beyond the flames,” said Simon Stiell, the UN Climate Change Executive Secretary.


The vast majority of Ontario’s wildfires burned during a few intense days in July, on the back of a scorching heat wave and intense lightning activity along a roughly 500-kilometre storm front over the province’s northern boreal forest.


Thousands of evacuees from more than a dozen mostly First Nations communities fled their homes while noxious plumes of smoke deteriorated air quality for millions of people from Thunder Bay to the northeastern United States.


Extreme fire weather has been more sustained in the Northwest Territories, where fires have remained active and spread over a long period rather than being driven by a single week of explosive growth.


Thursday’s report, whose co-authors included several scientists across the federal public service, highlighted the disproportionate impact of the wildfire season on First Nations and the importance of including those communities in risk assessments and preparedness plans.


Chief Russell Wesley of the Cat Lake First Nation in northwestern Ontario, one of the evacuated communities, said this year’s fires were a “warning” that the province and Ottawa’s current approach is insufficient.


In a news release, Wesley called for action on 11 priorities, including the creation of a First Nations wildfire authority and the expansion of Indigenous fire stewardship programs. Indigenous burning practices, the setting of small, low-intensity fires guided by traditional knowledge, were excluded for decades by governments but have been shown to boost diverse, fire-resistant landscapes and clear the forest of dead debris that could otherwise help fuel more intense flames.


“Maintaining healthy forests is not only an environmental responsibility; it is essential to our survival as First Nations peoples,” said Wesley.


“Without healthy forests, our communities, cultures and future generations are at risk.”


To come up with the results in Thursday’s report, scientists used observations and climate models focusing on the seven-day and 30-day periods of most extreme fire weather in Ontario and Northwest Territories. They then compared those conditions against what would have been expected in a world without fossil fuel emissions.


For both periods in Ontario, those conditions were made about twice as likely due to climate change, the report found. In N.W.T., the likelihood of the most intense seven-day period was five-hold, while the 30-day period was double.

‘We measure it in memories lost’: Bradley Creek wildfire leaves Okanagan Indian Band facing long road to recovery


Adapting to a future with more intense wildfires could include supporting more fire-resistant tree species, strengthening early warning systems and steering new development away from high-risk areas, the report says.

author: Avispa
title: Peter Thiel en La Moneda: la reunión que el gobierno de Chile intentó mantener en las sombras
content:
La transparencia de un gobierno no se mide sólo por las leyes que promulga o los discursos que pronuncia. También se refleja en aquello que decide ocultar. La visita a Chile del multimillonario tecnológico estadounidense Peter Thiel y su reunión privada con el Presidente José Antonio Kast es un claro ejemplo de ello.

Durante semanas, el encuentro permaneció fuera de toda comunicación oficial. No apareció en la agenda presidencial, no hubo fotografías, no existieron comunicados de prensa y tampoco se informó quiénes participaron de la reunión y cuáles fueron los temas tratados. Solo después de una solicitud de información realizada por el diputado Gonzalo Winter, el gobierno se vio obligado a reconocer que efectivamente el encuentro se realizó en dependencias del Palacio de La Moneda. La confirmación, sin embargo, estuvo lejos de despejar las dudas.

Una respuesta que responde poco

La presidencia de Chile sostuvo que la reunión fue "breve" y "protocolar" y que durante ella se abordaron las oportunidades y desafíos que plantea la inteligencia artificial para el Estado. Al mismo tiempo, afirmó que no existían actas, registros de asistentes ni documentos relacionados con el encuentro y rechazó entregar mayores antecedentes, invocando las normas que protegen las comunicaciones presidenciales.

Posteriormente, frente a nuevas consultas hechas por Gonzalo Winter, la respuesta oficial insistió en que no existían antecedentes adicionales, lo que llevó al parlamentario a extender sus solicitudes de información a todos los ministerios y organismos públicos, argumentando que la explicación entregada por La Moneda dejaba abiertas demasiadas interrogantes.

La explicación oficial terminó siendo paradójica: si la reunión fue tan irrelevante como se sostiene, ¿por qué mantenerla fuera de la agenda pública? Y si realmente abordó materias relacionadas con inteligencia artificial y asuntos estratégicos del Estado, ¿por qué impedir conocer quiénes estuvieron presentes?

Peter Thiel no es un empresario cualquiera.

Fue cofundador de PayPal y uno de los primeros inversionistas de Facebook. Pero su influencia trasciende el mundo financiero.

Es también cofundador de Palantir Technologies , empresa especializada en análisis masivo de datos, inteligencia artificial y plataformas utilizadas por organismos militares, servicios de inteligencia y agencias de seguridad en diversos países. Su compañía mantiene contratos con el Departamento de Defensa de Estados Unidos, agencias de inteligencia y fuerzas armadas occidentales, convirtiéndose en uno de los actores más influyentes del complejo tecnológico-militar estadounidense.

Por ello, cualquier reunión privada entre un jefe de Estado y una figura de estas características difícilmente puede ser considerada un simple encuentro de cortesía.

La visita a Chile tampoco puede analizarse de manera aislada.

Peter Thiel mantiene una conocida cercanía política e ideológica con el presidente argentino Javier Milei. Ambos comparten una visión libertaria radical sobre el rol del Estado, la regulación económica y el desarrollo tecnológico.

En los últimos meses, Thiel ha fortalecido su presencia en Argentina, país donde ha desarrollado vínculos empresariales y políticos y desde el cual proyecta parte de sus inversiones regionales. Esa relación convierte al Cono Sur en un espacio cada vez más relevante para los intereses de uno de los empresarios tecnológicos más influyentes del mundo.

Su paso por Santiago coincidió precisamente con una etapa en la que Chile y Argentina buscan fortalecer sectores considerados estratégicos, como la minería de minerales críticos, los centros de datos, la inteligencia artificial y la infraestructura digital.

Las hipótesis que deja la reunión

Ante la ausencia de información oficial, inevitablemente surgen distintas hipótesis.

No existen antecedentes públicos suficientes para afirmar cuál fue el verdadero propósito del encuentro, pero sí es posible plantear preguntas legítimas.

¿Buscaba Thiel explorar oportunidades de inversión tecnológica en Chile?

¿Existieron conversaciones relacionadas con inteligencia artificial aplicada al Estado?

¿Se abordaron materias vinculadas a ciberseguridad o procesamiento de datos públicos?

¿Hubo interés en proyectos relacionados con, litio o infraestructura digital?

¿Se trató de una reunión política entre dirigentes que comparten una visión común sobre el desarrollo tecnológico y el rol del Estado?

Precisamente porque el Gobierno decidió …

author: Vivian La
title: A controversial plan to update Line 5 just suffered a major loss at the Michigan Supreme Court
content:
In a win for opponents of Enbridge Energy’s Line 5 pipeline, the Michigan Supreme Court vacated a key permit last week for a proposed project that would replace a segment of the pipeline running underneath an environmentally-sensitive area of the Great Lakes, finding that a state commission did not examine the full scope of possible harm to the environment.


Following the 6-1 decision, the justices remanded the permit back to the Michigan Public Service Commission for a more thorough review, which likely extends the timeline for a decision on a project that’s already been mired in legal and procedural hurdles for years. 


Enbridge Energy received the permit in 2023 for its proposal to replace a segment of the oil and natural gas liquids pipeline — which connects lakes Michigan and Huron via the Straits of Mackinac — with a new one encased in a tunnel buried in the lakebed. Environmental groups and tribal nations appealed the decision, landing the case before the state’s highest court this year.


Writing for a nearly unanimous court in a

58-page opinion

, Justice Elizabeth Welch said that the commission didn’t consider the full range of potential environmental harms, nor did it look at how the project would impact the public’s right to use the state’s natural resources, which includes the Great Lakes — protections granted under the state’s public trust doctrine.


“We cannot fault (the commission) for this failure, because there was little authority on this issue prior to our decision today. Even so, it was error,” the opinion stated.


Justices found that the commission incorrectly limited its scope of review under the Michigan Environmental Protection Act to just the tunnel, when it should have examined how the project would impact the broader pipeline. Line 5 transports crude oil and natural gas liquids 645 miles from Superior, Wisconsin, through Michigan to Sarnia, Ontario, with 4.5 miles of the pipeline crossing the straits. 


In its new review, the justices said that the public service commission must answer whether the tunnel project will extend the lifespan of the 73-year-old pipeline, and if it does, determine what impacts there are to the environment and to the public trust.


“It is impossible to prevent or mitigate an environmental risk without understanding the nature of that risk,” the justices wrote.


Lawyers for the plaintiffs — four tribal nations across Michigan and three environmental groups — argued that because the tunnel project would extend the pipeline’s lifespan, it causes harm by increasing the risk of

oil spills

 along Line 5’s entirety and increased greenhouse gas emissions from the fossil fuels it transports.


“The court has made clear that our understanding of environmental harm, it’s a practical understanding, but it’s also a broad one,” said Chad Hughes, senior attorney for the Environmental Law & Policy Center, which argued with the plaintiffs. “There’s no requirement to narrowly focus on the physical location of the project. You look at the environmental harms where they happen.”


By broadening the scope of reviews under the Michigan Environmental Protection Act, opponents said conversations about shutting down the entire pipeline are finally a possibility. The justices wrote that “a meaningful examination” of alternatives can’t happen until the commission determines the full impacts of the project.


“The door has been kicked open to an imaginable future where we can talk about alternatives other than Line 5,” said President Whitney Gravelle of the Bay Mills Indian Community, one of the plaintiffs in the case.


In a statement, Enbridge spokesperson Ryan Duffy wrote that the company disagrees and is disappointed by the ruling, calling it an additional delay to a project that has already been under review for nearly a decade. Enbridge is reviewing the opinion and assessing legal options, he said.


“What remains unchanged is our commitment to operating Line 5 safely and responsibly, incorporating enhanced safety measures in the Straits, and protecting Michigan’s natural resources for generations to come,” the statement said.


The lone dissenting opinion from Justice Brian Zahra said that the court’s directive to consider the full scope of potential harms was “a moral hazard,” because state regulators already decided Line 5 was in the public interest when it approved construction more than 70 years ago. 


But Zahra agreed with the majority on the requirement to consider …

author: Darío Aranda
title: Marchar por la tierra sin olvidar los despojos del pasado y del presente
content:
OPINIÓN


Por Adrián Moyano*


Sí, claro. ¿Cómo no vamos a marchar el jueves 6 de agosto por las tierras? Pero déjenme pasar un par de avisos: la primera extranjerización significativa de la historia que nos incumbe la llevó a cabo el Estado argentino a través de su brazo armado. Los corrimientos de la línea de fortines fueron paulatinos desde la década de 1820 en adelante, pero el ritmo de la usurpación se tornó vertiginoso y mortal a partir de 1878.


Me permito recordar que para 1810 la frontera entre el antiguo Virreinato del Río de la Plata y el territorio de los pueblos indígenas libres, entre ellos el mapuche, pasaba a dos o tres galopitos de Buenos Aires. Y fue junto con los rémingtons y los sables que llegó la propiedad privada.


El monumental despojo no benefició inicialmente en nada al pueblo argentino. Es más, en la época de "la manteca al techo" la clase trabajadora sufría condiciones de explotación espantosas, las que también comenzaron a padecer culturas que no eran perfectas, pero nunca habían puesto en el centro de su funcionamiento la plusvalía.


Cuando buena parte de los y las mapuche sobrevivientes todavía languidecía en campos de concentración, su antiguo territorio se fraccionó y quedó en manos de militares de alto nivel que se llenaban la boca con invocaciones a la patria, entre ellos, el propio Roca. Por dar un par de ejemplos, un año después de que muriera Inakayal, la Compañía de Tierras del Sud Argentino ya poseía una cantidad de hectáreas que incluso vulneraba la legislación vigente y en parte de los antiguos dominios del lonco Reuque Cura se instaló la Estancia Pulmarí, también de capitales británicos. De ese origen fue el Ferrocarril del Sud, que unió Bahía Blanca con el Alto Valle del río Negro y después con Zapala. ¿Se imaginan a cuánto trepó la cotización de las tierras que hasta 1879 recorrieron en libertad las caravanas mapuches y tehuelches?


Claro que vamos a marchar el jueves, pero desde que se reformó la Constitución Nacional (1994), ningún gobierno reconoció --como dicta la ley suprema del país-- “la posesión y propiedad comunitarias de las tierras que tradicionalmente ocupan” las comunidades indígenas y menos aún se dignó “regular la entrega de otras aptas y suficientes para el desarrollo humano”. Pasaron 32 años y no sé cuántas gestiones. Como la “tierra indígena” no es “enajenable, transmisible ni susceptible de gravámenes o embargos”, los títulos de propiedad comunitaria serían barricadas infranqueables ante la profundización del despojo que ahora requiere el funcionamiento capitalista.


Por último, déjenme sumar que la Ley 26.160 que ordenó el Relevamiento Territorial de Comunidades Indígenas estuvo en vigencia durante 18 años y no se terminó en ningún lado. ¿Inoperancia o decisión política? ¿Cómo puede ser que, superado el primer cuarto del siglo XXI, el Estado en sus diversas jurisdicciones no sepa cuáles son los territorios indígenas? Si hasta tiene herramientas para saber si ampliamos el galponcito del fondo.


Vamos a marchar, claro que sí. Pero después no me vengan con que “hay que aprovechar las ventajas que nos da el mercado internacional”. Con esa excusa llenaron de soja hasta los maceteros. O con que “hay que pensar a la cordillera como una torta”.


*

Periodista y escritor

. Autor de numerosos libros, entre ellos "Crónicas de la resistencia mapuche" y "A ruego de mi superior cacique, Inakayal".


La entrada

Marchar por la tierra sin olvidar los despojos del pasado y del presente

 se publicó primero en

Agencia de Noticias Tierra Viva

author: DisabilityARK
title: England V Disability
content:
Disabled people in the United Kingdom (UK) have endured relentless


attacks on their rights and opportunities on multiple fronts. Many


hard-won freedoms have been steadily rolled back in recent years.


This document summarises some of these policies that have either


been proposed or successfully enacted. Disabled people are often


used as the testing ground for future policies, so being aware of what


is happening to them has broader implications for the rights of other


groups. During the Holocaust, many of the procedures developed on


disabled people were later applied to wider populations. More recent


examples include bank account surveillance systems, which are laying


the groundwork for more extensive population-wide surveillance.


Following the 2008 financial crash, attacks on disabled people’s rights


intensified. In 2016, the United Nations (UN) found that the UK was


engaged in “grave and systematic” violations of disabled people’s


rights, and linked these actions to a significant number of excess


deaths. In 2024, the UN follow-up report to the inquiry declared that


the UK made “no significant progress” on implementing the inquiry’s


recommendations regarding independent living, social security, and


an adequate standard of living. Now, in 2026, things have only gotten


worse. This zine cannot adequately cover every front of attack or the


rapid changes currently taking place, but it aims to provide a broad


snapshot of the situation in England in the Summer of 2026.


Author


Disability Action Research Kollective

DisabilityARK
