author: Mekong Review 2
title: No one owes you a living Kirsten Han
content:
Singapore declares itself a “pro-family” country, but there’s a gap between ideal and reality. Credit: Singapore Stock Photos / Unsplash


Unease: Life in Singapore Families


Teo You Yenn


Ethos Books: 2026


.


O

n the surface, Singapore gleams. It’s wealthy, orderly, safe. The trains (generally) run on time, the amenities are plentiful, and the tiny city-state punches above its weight in international rankings to do with governance and education. Singapore is regularly brought up by policy wonks and politicians around the world—and across the political spectrum—as a model to learn from. The government enthusiastically proclaims itself to be “pro-family”, gearing policies towards supporting (heterosexual) Singaporeans with getting married and having children. What’s not to like?


Everything sounds great on paper. Yet, through years of research and lengthy interviews with close to a hundred parents, sociologist Teo You Yenn uncovers a different reality: “Everyday life is hectic and tense; life is stable but not quite secure; there is a pathway to follow but it does not always seem right; family is everything but family life feels off-kilter.” There is, she observes, a “sense of unease” that sits in the hearts of families in Singapore, regardless of their socioeconomic background.


Teo’s previous book,

This Is What Inequality Looks Like

—an ethnographic study of low-income households in Singapore—became a national bestseller when it hit the shelves in 2018. It pushed Singaporeans to look beyond rhetoric about “uplifting the poor” and instead consider inequality as a nationwide condition from which none of us can be extricated. With

Unease: Life in Singapore Families

, Teo directs attention to quotidian family life and once again prompts Singaporeans to reflect on the nature of the water we swim in.


Setting out to understand how parents navigate the much coveted but often elusive work–life balance, Teo finds that it isn’t basic childcare that occupies the most real estate in parents’ minds—it’s education. “Education systems or policies are rarely considered, by scholars or policymakers, as a source of work-life conflict; yet, my research shows that education has become a big component of ‘care labour’,” she writes. “Contemporary demands on parenting go well beyond baths and burps and fevers and sleeplessness, to supervision and nagging and strategising and conflicts of an entirely different, arguably more stress-inducing, level.”


E

veryone in Singapore knows of the “kiasu parent”. Translated from Hokkien, to be ‘kiasu’ means to be afraid to lose, or lose out. The kiasu parent is obsessed with ensuring their kid keeps up with, if not outstrips, the rest of their cohort. The kiasu parent studies school rankings as if they contain the meaning of life and plots to get their offspring into the best option. The kiasu parent harasses teachers for progress reports and even demands extra homework. The kiasu parent, keeping tabs on what other (kiasu) parents are doing, signs their sprog up for extra tuition in all subjects… and also for piano, swimming, and ballet.


This archetype of the kiasu parent is often the butt of jokes—a beast to be reckoned with, but one we roll our eyes at. Government officials evoke their spectre when speaking of the need for a “mindset shift”, implying that the problems of a pressure-cooker education system stem from individual attitudes. Things would surely change if only all these parents could just

stop being so kiasu

.


Teo has no interest in lecturing parents. She’s much more invested in the structures within which Singaporean parents operate. Kiasu parents do not simply emerge, fully-formed, from Singapore’s diminishing rainforests; if they’re terrified of losing out, something must be making them feel like competitors in the first place. And individual parents have neither the clout nor capacity to shape the arena and dictate the rules. That can only come from something bigger and more powerful: government policies, institutional processes and procedures, social conditions that everyone has to respond or adapt to.


E

ducation is a high-stakes game in Singapore. Although there have been shifts, over the years, away from a hyper-focus on academic results, the practices of scoring and sorting are still prevalent. It has to include us.” With long black hair, glasses, and a loose-fitting T-shirt, she seems far removed from the stereotypical image of a rebel medic working in a warzone. Ma Hnin lives in a camp, hidden along a dirt road, that serves as a coordination point for forces fighting Myanmar’s military junta, which seized power in an illegal coup on 1 February 2021. Earlier that morning, a Y-12 surveillance aircraft and a Myanmar military jet fighter had flown overhead and dropped at least two bombs near the frontline—a reminder that, even in moments of relative calm, the threat of attack is never far away. Since the earliest days of the return to military rule, Ma Hnin has been part of the resistance movement. After participating in the nationwide Civil Disobedience Movement and anti-coup protest, she joined the People’s Defense Force (PDF) as a medic. The PDF serves as the armed wing of Myanmar’s National Unity Government, the civilian administration established by elected lawmakers ousted by the military coup, ethnic representatives, and democracy activists. title: Sorunu konuşmakla yetinmedik çözümü birlikte ürettik
content:
Hepinize merhabalar. Ben Kayseri’de bir Anadolu Lisesinde okuyorum. Bugün sizlere 23. Gençlik Yaz Kampında gerçekleşen lise forumundan ve bu seneki deneyimlerimden bahsedeceğim. Bu benim katıldığım 5. kamptı; 5 senedir aksatmadan, büyük bir heyecanla lise forumunda yer alıyorum.

Bu sene, forumun formatında bir değişikliğe gidilmişti. Geçen senelerde her il kendi konuşmacısını seçer; o konuşmacı sahneye çıkar ve belirli bir sorun hakkında konuşurdu. Bu sene ise sadece dinleyen değil, tamamen sürecin bir parçası olunan dinamik bir model geliştirilmiş.

Forum öncesinde beşer kişilik ekiplere ayrıldık. Her bir ekibe fahiş kantin fiyatlarından okul güvenliğine ve akran zorbalığına kadar liselerimizde bizzat karşılaştığımız farklı bir sorunsenaryosu verildi. Bizden sadece sorunu anlatmamız değil, somut bir çözüm üretmemiz istendi. Ekipler olarak önce sorunları masaya yatırdık, ardından "Nasıl bir çözüm üretebiliriz?" diyerek tartışmaya başladık.

Bize verilen konu kantin fiyatlarıydı. Bu konu hakkında şu şekilde bir çözüm ürettik:Öncelikle konuyla ilgili bir "Genç Hayat" yazısı yazdık ve bütün arkadaşlarımızla tartıştık.Ardından bu süreci sosyal medya hesaplarıyla destekledik. Sosyal medya hesaplarımızın stickerlarını bastırıp okul çevresine yapıştırdık. Kantin önünde durarak sıra arkadaşlarımızı bilinçlendirdik. Her sınıf kendi temsilcisini seçti ve boykot kararları almaya başladık. Her sınıf kendine belirli bir gün seçerek hep beraber (evden getirdikleriyle) yemek yedi; o gün kantinden hiç alışveriş yapılmadı. Ayrıca okul dışındaki sağlıklı ve uygun fiyatlı bir mekanla anlaştık. Tüm bu adımlar sayesinde okulumuzda kantin fiyatlarının düşmesini sağladık. Ayrıca kurduğumuz sınıf temsilcilikleri, ileride karşılaşabileceğimiz diğer sorunlara karşı da mücadele etmeye devam edecek.

Açıkçası ilk başta formatı tam kavrayamamıştım ve bu kadar etkili, bu kadar eğlenceli geçeceğini tahmin etmemiştim ama ne yalan söyleyeyim, tamamen yanılmışım. Geçen senelere kıyasla liseli arkadaşlarımın katılımı ve enerjisi çok yüksekti. Kiminle sohbet etsem herkes yeni formattan son derece memnun kaldığını söylüyordu. Orada ekipler içinde her ne kadar güle oynaya, şakalaşarak tartışsak da ele aldığımız konular aslında geleceğimizi doğrudan ilgilendiren hayati meselelerdi. Çünkü başımızı çevirip baktığımızda, bu sorunların hepsini Türkiye’nin dört bir yanındaki liseliler olarak kendi okullarımızda canlı canlı yaşıyoruz. İşte tam da bu yüzden katıldığımız lise forumunun değerini bir kez daha anladım. Birebir aynı dertleri paylaştığımız için arkadaşların getirdiği çözüm önerileri ve aktardığı tecrübeler her birimiz için altın değerinde birer rehber oldu.

Ancak biz liseliler olarak şu gerçeği unutmamalıyız: Bu sorunların çözümünü sadece kamptaki lise forumu ile sınırlı tutamayız. Buradan aldığımız meşaleyi kendi okullarımıza, kendi şehirlerimize taşımak zorundayız. Kampa gelemeyen arkadaşlarımıza da burada olan biteni aktarmalı, onların da fikirlerini alarak mücadelemizi büyütmeliyiz. Çünkü bugün liselerimizdeki bu sorunlara hep birlikte "dur" demezsek, yarın çok daha büyük ve yıkıcı problemlerle yüzleşmek zorunda kalacağız. Gelecek biziz ve çözümü de yine biz üreteceğiz!

content:
The 12-article bill was approved by majority vote in the Justice Commission after around 18 hours of deliberations.


The “Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Integration,” prepared as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey, is scheduled to be taken up by the Turkish Grand National Assembly (TBMM) General Assembly tomorrow.


The 12-article bill was submitted to the Speaker’s Office of the TBMM on August 5, bearing the signatures of 367 members of parliament. It began to be debated in the Justice Commission on August 7.


After nearly 18 hours of deliberations, the commission approved the bill by majority vote.


The bill is expected to be debated in the General Assembly at 11:00 a.m. tomorrow. As was the case at the Justice Commission, it is widely expected to be approved by a majority vote in the General Assembly as well.

title: Movement Leadership: The law can only be implemented if it is led and directed by Leader Öcalan
content:
The Movement Leadership issued a written statement regarding the “Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Cohesion,” which was prepared as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey and approved by majority vote in the Justice Commission this week. The bill is scheduled to be taken up by the Turkish Grand National Assembly (TBMM) General Assembly tomorrow.


The statement released by the Movement Leadership on Sunday reads as follows:


“The long-awaited framework law has passed through the parliamentary commission and will now be submitted for approval by parliament. While some have strongly opposed the bill, others have criticized it on various grounds. The DEM Party also highlighted many of its shortcomings and deficiencies during the commission process and outlined what further steps should be taken after its adoption.


Following Devlet Bahçeli’s call, Leader Apo (Abdullah Öcalan) stated that he had the capacity to move the conflict stemming from the Kurdish question onto legal and political ground. With the ‘Call for Peace and Democratic Society’ issued on February 27, 2025, he clearly presented a roadmap for how this could be achieved.


Based on Leader Apo’s call, our Freedom Movement has fulfilled its responsibilities in order to advance the Peace and Democratic Society Process. On this basis, a state of non-conflict has been maintained for the past eighteen months.


During this process, the National Solidarity, Brotherhood and Democracy Commission was established in parliament to promote peace, democratization, and a resolution to the Kurdish question. As a result of the commission’s work, a report was prepared which, despite its significant shortcomings, can still be regarded as an important document.


The language of a foundational law should be the language of peace


Throughout this process, Leader Apo remained in contact and dialogue with state officials, the DEM Party, and our Freedom Movement in order to facilitate the adoption of a foundational law that would pave the way for democratization and a resolution to the Kurdish question.


We also closely followed the discussions and developments surrounding this foundational law. Based on the draft legislation that reached us through various channels, we presented our views and criticisms to the public through our statements.


First and foremost, we emphasized that the language of a foundational law aimed at achieving peace should not be the language of war, but the language of peace. As Leader Apo has stated, we stressed that it should not be simplistic, narrow in scope, or incapable of serving the future, and that the sensitivities of all sides should be taken into account.


It is essential that Öcalan be free and able to work without restrictions


We also pointed out that, for the steps envisioned by the law to be realized, it is essential that Leader Apo be free and able to work without restrictions.


Furthermore, we emphasized the importance of the law committing to the adoption of democratization and freedom-related legislation through a clearly defined series of steps.


Even before our statement, Leader Apo had already conveyed, through the DEM Party delegation, the objectives of the framework law and how it should be structured to the public.


Throughout this process, the DEM Party and democratic forces also presented their views and proposals regarding the framework law and held a number of discussions on the issue.


The bill, which has been debated for months and reflects the views expressed by our people, ourselves, and democratic forces, has now passed the Parliamentary Justice Commission with the approval of the other political parties, despite attempts by what we describe as an anti-Kurdish tendency to obstruct the process through provocations.


The law contains serious shortcomings and deficiencies


This law contains serious shortcomings and deficiencies. The recommendations contained in the parliamentary commission’s report regarding democratization and the resolution of the Kurdish question have not been reflected in the bill. In this respect, it does not fully meet its stated purpose.


By referring only to disarmament without mentioning the Kurdish question or even using the term ‘Kurd,’ the bill demonstrates that the issue has not been addressed in a comprehensive manner. author: Salma Abdelrahman
title: Open call for proposals and reporting practices on artificial intelligence
content:
Everything is about AI now. On a general discourse level, a prophecy is being shoved down our throats telling us it is the one thing that is going to fundamentally change life as we know it.


The prophecy comes at us wrapped in the language of utopia and a tech giant’s latest market offering. Today, the capabilities of the computational power behind AI models is unprecedented, so much so that it may very well rival the cognitive skills of the human mind. AI is going to solve the mysteries of disease and eradicate world poverty, we are told. Sam Altman, the CEO of OpenAI, has declared the arrival of “singularity,” the concept of machine intelligence surpassing human intelligence, two times now and still counting. Demis Hassabis, the CEO of Google’s DeepMind, is the more cautious one: he only promises we are “near” it.


Based on these claims, hundreds of billions of dollars of capital are being thrown into AI-related investments, roughly 1 percent of global GDP. That is not counting the overall compulsion of businesses from all over the world to switch to AI, mainly out of fear of missing out on something big.


The implications are profound. Fantasies of replacing human labor that have been the obsession of capitalism for the past two centuries are reaching new heights with AI’s support. Data centers are being erected everywhere, doubling the global demand for copper. Operating them requires massive amounts of energy, leaving a larger carbon footprint on an already strained planet. Cooling them requires massive amounts of water. A Bloomberg analysis concluded that “two-thirds of new data centers built or in development since 2022 are in places already gripped by high levels of water stress.”


All this for an industry that has not only failed to generate revenue so far but that doesn’t even have any idea how it could do so in the future.


Despite all this, very little critical engagement is given to AI — except maybe the environmental impact.


Egypt is no stranger to this. In 2024, Egypt saw US$278 million in data center investments. The figure is projected to grow to $694 million by 2030. Everyday in the press, you notice startups from different sectors and fields promising they will be providing AI-oriented solutions. “How exactly?” you might ask. No one actually knows.


This is an open call to invite those who are interested in this sort of critical engagement, both in the global context and with a focus on Egypt. While we do not want to restrict proposals, we are looking for approaches that open new ways of thinking about AI’s impact on the fundamentals of our lives. That means the proposals could be on fundamental subjects — labor, governance, health, environmental impact or entertainment — as much as on ways of approach — people’s history with AI, the political economy of AI or AI in the Global South. At the core, we are interested in trying to demystify the prophetic discourse surrounding AI and to look at the politics and power behind the claims that help themselves to grandeur. What really is behind this catchall that contains so much yet so little and that has thrust itself into every aspect of our lives?


As much as we are looking for concrete proposals, we also invite those who are interested in developing a practice of reporting on AI in Egypt to reach out — let’s have a conversation on how this could look like and what Mada Masr can provide to help.


Please reach out by email to submissions@madamasr.com, with a subject line of “Down with AI.”

The post

Open call for proposals and reporting practices on artificial intelligence

 first appeared on

Mada Masr

.

title: „Linke ausrotten“: Der neue ultrarechte Präsident Abelardo de la Espriella ist eine Gefahr (nicht nur) für Menschenrechte und Friedenspolitik in Kolumbien
content:
Dossier


„

Eine Gruppe von 21 internationalen Menschenrechtsorganisationen, darunter das Internationale Büro für Menschenrechte in Kolumbien (Oidahco), warnt vor der bevorstehenden Politik des ultrarechten gewählten Präsidenten Abelardo de la Espriella. Sie befürchten einen möglichen Abbau von Menschenrechten, Rückschritte bei der Umsetzung des Friedensabkommens von 2016 und der Friedenspolitik sowie eine Aushöhlung der Rechte von Frauen und LGBTIQ+-Personen. (…) Sein „Sofortplan“ sieht vor, den Einflussbereich bewaffneter Gruppen durch weitläufige Militäroperationen in den ersten 90 Tagen seiner Regierung zurückzudrängen. (…) Die unterzeichnenden Menschenrechtsnetzwerke fordern die Europäische Union und ihre Mitgliedstaaten sowie die Schweiz, Norwegen und das Vereinigte Königreich daher auf, die künftige Regierung De la Espriellas zur Einhaltung der Verpflichtungen des kolumbianischen Staates aus dem Friedensabkommen von 2016 zu bewegen

…“

Artikel von Pablo Schröder vom 26.06.2026 in amerika21

 und mehr zum Thema:


Kolumbien: Aufgeheizte Stimmung zum Amtsantritt von De la Espriella – Gegen-Demonstrationen in Bogotá, Cali und Barranquilla


„Entgegen der Tradition trat der neue Staatschef sein Amt diesmal nicht im Kongress in Bogotá, sondern in Cali an. (…) Bei der Veranstaltung in der drittgrößten Stadt Kolumbiens nach Bogotá und Medellín wurden zahlreiche Staatschefs aus Mittel- und Lateinamerika erwartet. Darunter befanden sich die beiden als rechtsextrem geltenden Präsidenten Javier Milei (Argentinien) und José Antonio Kast (Chile) sowie weitere dem rechten Lager zuzurechnende Staatschefs wie Rodrigo Paz (Bolivien), Daniel Noboa (Ecuador), Santiago Peña (Paraguay), José Raúl Mulino (Panama), Laura Fernández (Costa Rica), Luis Abinader (Dominikanische Republik) und Nasry Asfura (Honduras). Wie bei den Amtseinführungen der Präsidenten der Region üblich, wurde auch Spanien durch König Felipe VI. vertreten. Seitens der USA nahm Außenminister Marco Rubio, der wichtigste Ansprechpartner der Trump-Regierung für Lateinamerika, an der Veranstaltung in Cali teil. Laut der Zeitung „El Colombiano“ aus Medellín zählte zudem FIFA-Präsident Gianni Infantino zu den Gästen der Veranstaltung. (…)


Bei der Veranstaltung fehlten jedoch auch einige prominente Gesichter, darunter der noch amtierende Präsident Gustavo Petro. Ebenfalls nicht anwesend war der Präsidentschaftskandidat des „Pacto Histórico“, Iván Cepeda. Auch andere Mitglieder des linken politischen Blocks blieben der Veranstaltung fern und hatten für Freitag (7.8.) zu Demonstrationen in Bogotá, Cali und Barranquilla aufgerufen. Wie das Portal „La Silla Vacía“ berichtete, erklärte Cepeda, diese Mobilisierungen seien „ein friedlicher Ausdruck zivilen Ungehorsams und der Volkssouveränität“. Weniger versöhnlich hatte sich in den Tagen zuvor der noch amtierende Präsident Petro gezeigt. Bei einer Pressekonferenz am Montagabend vor lokalen und ausländischen Medienvertretern im Casa de Nariño in Bogotá hatte er an seiner Darstellung festgehalten, die Wahlen seien manipuliert worden. (…)


Anstatt die Wogen zu glätten, warnte Petro zudem vor einem möglichen „Bürgerkrieg“ im Land aufgrund der Ablehnung, die dieser und andere mutmaßliche Pläne der künftigen Regierung hervorrufen. „Es ist ganz klar, wie ein Bürgerkrieg in Kolumbien aussehen könnte“, erklärte der Präsident. (…) Auf diese Aussagen reagierte auch De la Espriella. In einer Live-Übertragung in seinen sozialen Netzwerken ging der künftige kolumbianische Präsident gegen Petro und auch gegen Cepeda vor und erklärte: „Zum ersten Mal haben sich ein scheidender Präsident und sein unterlegener Kandidat ohne jeden Grund dafür entschieden, den Sieg der Demokratie an den Wahlurnen nicht anzuerkennen und einen sogenannten zivilen Ungehorsam gegenüber der Regierung zu verkünden, die ich vertrete und die von fast 13 Millionen Kolumbianern gewählt wurde, die sich trotz aller Widerstände des Establishments – sowohl der legalen als auch der illegalen Machthaber – für mich entschieden haben.“ (…)


In diesem Zusammenhang bekräftigte De la Espriella, dass er der „Präsident aller Kolumbianer“ sei und dass er „mit der Kraft der Verfassung und des Gesetzes das durchsetzen werde, wofür sich die Kolumbianer entschieden haben, nämlich mich zu wählen“. Außerdem rief er dazu auf, „das Falsche, das Illegale und das Verzerrte nicht weiter zu normalisieren“. Nennen wir die Dinge beim Namen und stellen wir uns ihnen so, wie sie sind. Dieser …

title: Nach knapp 45 Jahren Haft: Eingabe von US-Bürgerechtsorganisationen für Mumia Abu-Jamal bei der UN Arbeitsgruppe gegen Willkürliche Inhaftierungen
content:
„

Im Juli 2026 brachten fünf Bürgerechtsorganisationen aus den USA, das Abolitionist Law Center, die American Civil Liberties Union, das Center for Constitutional Rights, das California Coalition for Women Prisoners und die Release Aging People in Prison Campaign

eine Petition


 an die

UN Arbeitsgruppe gegen Willkürliche Inhaftierungen


 ein.

Sie bitten um eine Stellungnahme des UN Gremiums über die anhaltende Haft von Mumia Abu-Jamal vor dem Hintergrund des juristischen Versagens der beteiligten US Gremien nach knapp 45 Jahren Haft

.“

Meldung vom Berliner Bündnis Freiheit für Mumia Abu-Jamal!


 und ein Artikel darüber:


USA: Mumia setzt auf UNO. Petition an UN-Gremium für willkürliche Inhaftierungen fordert Freilassung des Bürgerrechtlers und Langzeitgefangenen Abu-Jamal


„Zur Lage des weltweit bekannten US-Bürgerrechtlers und seit 1981 in Pennsylvania inhaftierten politischen Gefangenen Mumia Abu-Jamal (72) hat Samah Sisay, Menschenrechtsanwältin beim »Center for Constitutional Rights« (CCR), kürzlich erklärt: »Er ist betagt und krank und sollte nicht länger eingesperrt sein!« Die Juristin gehört einer in der US-Bürgerrechtsbewegung verankerten Gruppe von Rechtsbeiständen an, die gemeinsam mit Abu-Jamals Anwalt Bret Grote vom »Abolitionist Law Center« (Pittsburgh) am 28. Juli eine Petition bei der »Arbeitsgruppe gegen willkürliche Inhaftierungen« der Vereinten Nationen in Genf eingereicht haben. Neben dem CCR gehören dazu die »American Civil Liberties Union«, die »Release Aging People in Prison Campaign« (alle in New York City) sowie die »California Coalition for Women Prisoners« (Oakland). Sie ersuchen das UN-Gremium um humanitäre Unterstützung für die Durchsetzung der Forderung nach unverzüglicher Freilassung des zu Unrecht inhaftierten Menschenrechtsaktivisten und Autors. Die Petition bringt Abu-Jamals seit Jahrzehnten wiederholt vorgebrachte Beschwerde vor ein Völkerrechtsgremium außerhalb der Gerichtsbarkeit der USA: Er sei wegen eines Verbrechens, das er nicht begangen habe, willkürlich inhaftiert worden. Das Verteidigungsteam des seit 2015 mehrfach lebensbedrohlich erkrankten Gefangenen fasste den Beschluss, sich im Namen des Mandanten an die UNO zu wenden, nachdem nahezu alle in den USA möglichen Rechtsmittel ausgeschöpft waren. Das in der Petition beklagte Unrecht hat einen Namen: die »Mumia-Ausnahme«. Der US-Investigativjournalist Linn Washington prägte den Begriff, um aufzuzeigen, dass die US-Justiz Abu-Jamal routinemäßig dieselben Rechtsansprüche verweigert, die anderen Personen gewährt werden. (…)


Aktuell betrifft das vor allem Abu-Jamals Recht auf eine angemessene medizinische Versorgung. Bereits am 20. April 2021, also vor mehr als fünf Jahren, hatten UN-Menschenrechtsexperten in Genf gegenüber der US-Regierung ihre »ernsthafte Besorgnis über die Behandlung und das Wohlergehen von Mumia Abu-Jamal« geäußert. Der Veteran der »Black Panther Party« saß zu diesem Zeitpunkt bereits seit fast 40 Jahren in Haft. Der Hohe Kommissar für Menschenrechte intervenierte, als der politische Gefangene anlässlich einer Operation am offenen Herzen an sein Klinikbett gefesselt wurde. Gleiches war ihm zwei Monate zuvor während der Behandlung seiner akuten Herzinsuffizienz vier Tage lang widerfahren. »Diese fortgesetzte grausame, unmenschliche und erniedrigende Behandlung, einschließlich der vorsätzlichen Missachtung seiner Würde und der unmenschlichen Haftbedingungen, stellt eine klare Verletzung der fundamentalen Rechte von Mr. Abu-Jamal dar«, so das Urteil der UN-Experten. Die Fesselung sei »verwerflich«, da sie bei dem schwer erkrankten Häftling »zusätzliches und unnötiges Leid« verursache. An die US-Behörden erging die Aufforderung, sich umgehend mit den über Abu-Jamals Fall hinausreichenden Vorwürfen der »rassistischen Diskriminierung bei der medizinischen Behandlung von Gefangenen in Pennsylvania zu befassen«. Es sei dafür zu sorgen, dass die körperliche Unversehrtheit und das Leben vor allem der älteren Gefangenen geschützt werden, die besonders von der damals grassierenden Covid-19-Pandemie betroffen waren. Trotz weltweiter Proteste gegen die medizinische Vernachlässigung hat sich die allgemein prekäre Lage der Menschen im US-Gefängnissystem und die persönliche Situation von Mumia Abu-Jamal im Staatsgefängnis Mahanoy in Frackville, Pennsylvania, seitdem nicht zum Besseren verändert, wie die aktuell neu eingereichte Petition hervorhebt. author: Julius Gavroche
title: Giorgio Agamben: When  the house is on fire
content:
Louisa Gouliamaki/Reuters


With fires literally raging across the world, we return to a 2020 essay by Giorgio Agamben.


Other languages:

Italiano

,

Español

,

Français

,

Nederlands

,

Português

,

Russian

,

Deutsch

,

Greek

, Magyar

,

Türkçe


“Nothing I’m doing makes any sense if the house is on fire.” Yet even when the house is on fire it is necessary to continue as before, to do everything with care and precision, perhaps even more so than before—even if no one notices. Perhaps life itself will disappear from the face of the earth, perhaps no memory whatsoever will remain of what has been done, for better or for worse. But you continue as before, it is too late to change, there is no time anymore.


“What’s happening around you / is no longer your business”. Like the geography of a country that you must leave behind forever. Yet how does it still affect you? Precisely now that it is no longer your business, now that everything seems over, everything and every place now appears in its truest guise, somehow they all touch you even more intimately—just as they are: splendor and poverty.


Philosophy, a dead language. “The language of poets is always a dead language…it is a strange thing to admit: a dead language that one uses to provide greater life to thought.” Perhaps not a dead language, but a dialect. That philosophy and poetry speak in a language that is less than language is the measure of their rank, of their special vitality. To weigh and judge the world by measuring it against a dialect, a dead language that nevertheless pours forth anew, in which not even a comma can be changed. Keep speaking this dialect, even now that the house is on fire.


Which house is on fire? The country where you live, or Europe, or the entire world? Perhaps the houses and cities already burned down in some enormous fire—who knows how long ago—that we pretended not to notice. Of most of them all that remains are pieces of walls, a fresco, a patch of roof, names, so many names, already gnawed upon by flames. Nevertheless we carefully cover it all over with whitewash and falsified words, so that it looks intact. We live in houses and cities incinerated from one end to another as if they were still standing upright; people pretend to live in them and stroll in masks through ruins as if they were still in the familiar neighborhoods of a bygone era.


Today the flame has changed its form and nature, it has become digital, invisible and cold—but precisely for this very reason it is even closer still and surrounds us at every moment.


That a civilization—a barbarism—can sink, never to rise again, is nothing new. Historians are accustomed to identifying and dating caesuras and shipwrecks. But how can we bear witness to a world that is falling into ruin with eyes blindfolded and face covered, a republic collapsing with neither lucidity nor pride, but in abjection and fear? The blindness is all the more desperate since the shipwrecked claim to be governing their own shipwreck, they swear that everything can be controlled technically, that there is no need for either a new god or a new sky, only prohibitions, experts and doctors. Panic and villainy.


What would a God be to whom neither prayers nor sacrifices were addressed? And what would a law be that knew neither command nor enforcement? What is a word that has neither meaning nor command, but is truly held in the beginning—indeed, before the beginning?


A culture that feels it is at its end, that it has no life left, attempts to govern its decay in the only way it knows how, through a permanent state of exception. The 

total mobilization

 in which Jünger saw the essential character of our time should be understood from this perspective. People must be mobilized, they must feel themselves in a state of emergency at every moment, regulated down to the last detail by those who maintain the power to declare such an emergency. But whereas in the past mobilization sought to gather people together, today it aims to isolate them, to distance them from one another.


How long has the house been burning? How long since it burned down? Certainly a century ago, between 1914 and 1918, something happened in Europe that poured flames and madness upon everything that once seemed to remain intact and alive; then thirty years later, the flames again spread everywhere, and ever since have continued to burn without pause, submerged, barely visible beneath the cinders. title: Serok Barzanî pêşwaziyê li Konsula Giştî ya Brîtanyayê li Hewlêrê kir
content:
Roja Yekşemê 09ê Tebaxa 2026an, Serok Mesûd Barzanî pêşwaziyê li Xatûna Holly Fair, Konsula nû ya Brîtanyayê li Hewlêrê kir. Di vê hevdîtinê de birêz Konsula Giştî ya Brîtanyayê kêfxweşiya xwe bi hevdîtina Serok Barzanî û destbikarbûna xwe wek Konsula nû ya Brîtanyayê li Herêma Kurdistanê nîşan da. Herwiha Konsula Brîtanyayê bal kişand li ser wê yekê ku dê berdewam be di hewldana ji bo berdewamî û girîngîdana zêdetir bi peywendiyên di navbera Herêma Kurdistanê û Brîtanyayê de û heyraniya xwe bi pêşketinên Herêma Kurdistanê di warên cihêreng de nîşan da. Rewşa siyasî ya Iraqê û peywendiyên di navbera herdu hikûmetên Herêma Kurdistanê û Iraqa Federal mijareke din a hevdîtinê bûn. author: Mag
title: Textilarbeiterinnen in Bangladesch kämpfen für eine Anhebung des Mindestlohns um mehr als 200 % und fordern internationale Unterstützung
content:
Dossier


„

Eine Allianz aus 11 Verbänden und Gewerkschaften des Bekleidungssektors in Bangladesch hat sich dem Garment Workers‘ Trade Union Center (GWTUC) angeschlossen, um für eine Anhebung des Mindestlohns auf 25 000 BDT (ca. 215€ / 235US$) pro Monat zu kämpfen. Das klingt vielleicht nicht nach viel. Aber wenn man bedenkt, dass der derzeitige Mindestlohn für die Beschäftigten in der Bekleidungsindustrie des Landes bei mageren 8 000 BDT liegt, wäre eine Erhöhung um mehr als 200 % ein echter Meilenstein für die vier Millionen Beschäftigten in dieser Branche. Die überwiegende Mehrheit davon sind weibliche Arbeitskräfte. In Bangladesch gibt es rund 4000 Bekleidungsfabriken, von denen die meisten für Marken wie Adidas, H&M, Nike, Marc O’Polo und Zara produzieren. Der GWTUC ruft andere Gewerkschaften und Einzelpersonen auf, sich mit den Bekleidungsarbeitern zu solidarisieren

…“ engl.

Aufruf vom 20.4.2023 bei Global May Day


 mit weiteren Infos:


Textilindustrie in Bangladesch: Näher dem Abgrund näher. Mehr als 450 geschlossene Betriebe seit August 2024, rund 240.000 Beschäftigte entlassen – Regierungschef empfängt nur Kapitalseite


„Auch im Juli war der Textilsektor die große Stütze der Exportwirtschaft: Waren im Gesamtwert von 4,72 Milliarden US-Dollar gelangten von Bangladesch aus auf den Weltmarkt, wovon 3,88 Milliarden auf Produkte der Textilindustrie entfielen. Nicht verhehlen kann dieses Zwischenergebnis zum Auftakt des neuen Finanzjahres, dass die Branche unter Druck steht. Gegenüber dem Vergleichsmonat 2025 sanken die Textilexporte um 1,92 Prozent, so das Branchenportal Bangladesh Textile Today am Donnerstag. Dass sich Bangladeschs Textilindustrie in einer bedrohlichen Krise befindet, ist inzwischen allerdings ein alter Hut. Keinen Zweifel daran lässt ein Bericht, den die Menschenrechtsvereinigung »Justice Makers Bangladesh in France« (JMBF) am 15. Juli veröffentlicht hat. Darin kommt das Autorenteam zu dem Schluss, dass allein im ersten Halbjahr 80 Textilfirmen dichtgemacht oder reichlich Personal abgebaut haben. Den Verlust beziffern sie auf 20.783 Jobs. Betrachte man die vergangenen zwei Jahre, hätten sogar 240.000 Beschäftigte – die übergroße Mehrheit Frauen – ihren Arbeitsplatz verloren. Insgesamt arbeiteten in der Branche schätzungsweise vier Millionen Menschen. (…)


Der Jobverlust ist indes nur die Spitze des Eisberges. Die Näherinnen müssten sich zudem mit unzähligen Fällen ausgebliebener Lohnzahlungen, unbezahlter Überstunden, einbehaltener Feiertagszuschläge und mit insgesamt verschlechterten Arbeitsbedingungen herumschlagen. Das alles sei keine Summe von Einzelfällen, sondern ein strukturelles Problem, zitierte das indische Portal Nation Press aus dem Bericht. Wer mit friedlichem Protest gegen solche Ungerechtigkeiten aufbegehre, müsse mit brachialer Repression durch die Polizei rechnen, die bereits Tränengas und Gummigeschosse gegen Streikende und Demonstrierende eingesetzt habe. (…)


Die technokratische Übergangsadministration unter Friedensnobelpreisträger Muhammad Yunus hatte andere Prioritäten als Hilfe für Näherinnen. Vereinzelte Hoffnungen, nach dem Wahlsieg der konservativen Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) bei den Wahlen im Februar 2026 könnte es besser werden, haben sich auch nicht erfüllt. Premier Tarique Rahman ist auf einen neoliberalen Kurs eingeschwenkt. Am 22. Juli traf er sich in seinem Amtssitz mit dem Dachverband Bangladesh Textile Mills Association (BTMA). Am Tisch saßen nur die Fabrikbesitzer, nicht aber Gewerkschaftsvertreter; statt um die Nöte der Arbeiterinnen ging es um die »globale Wettbewerbsfähigkeit« der Branche. Als »Meilenstein« wurde bereits im April eine Arbeitsrechtsergänzung gepriesen, die den Beschäftigten mehr Organisationsrechte einräumt und Grundsätze zu Entlassungen fixiert – ohne aber sklavenähnliche Arbeitsbedingungen zu unterbinden, wie Kritiker anmerkten. Zudem fehlt den zuständigen Behörden das Personal, um punktuelle Gesetzesverbesserungen effektiv in den Fabriken gegen das Kapital durchzusetzen. Jüngst sind auch in Bangladesch zudem viele Preise rasant gestiegen, insbesondere seit dem Krieg der USA und Israels gegen den Iran. Viele oft nur von einem Verdienst lebende Familien können die Lebenshaltungskosten kaum noch stemmen.“


Artikel von Thomas Berger in der jungen Welt vom 8. August 2026

author: Unknown
title: YÖK: Öğrencilik hakkını kaybedenler yeniden öğrenime dönebilecek
content:
Yükseköğretim Kurulu (YÖK), Resmî Gazete’de yayımlanarak yürürlüğe giren “Yükseköğretim Kanunu ve Bazı Kanunlarda Değişiklik Yapılmasına Dair Kanun” ile yükseköğretim kurumlarında çeşitli nedenlerle öğrencilik hakkını kaybedenlere yeniden öğrenime dönme imkanı sağlandığını bildirdi.


Öğrenci affına ve yükseköğretime ilişkin düzenlemeleri içeren “

Yükseköğretim Kanunu ve Bazı Kanunlarda Değişiklik Yapılmasına Dair Kanun

” Resmî Gazete’de yayımlanarak yürürlüğe girdi.


YÖK’ten, kanunun detaylarına ilişkin yapılan yazılı açıklamaya göre, düzenlemeyle, yükseköğretim kurumlarında çeşitli nedenlerle öğrencilik hakkını kaybedenlere yeniden öğrenime dönme imkânı sağlandı.


Bu kapsamda, hazırlık, intibak, ön lisans, lisans tamamlama, lisans ve lisansüstü öğrenim kademelerini kapsayan düzenlemeden, kanunda belirtilen istisnalar dışında kendi isteğiyle ilişiğini kesenler de yararlanabilecek.


Kanunda açıkça istisna tutulan durumlar dışında, kendi isteğiyle ilişiğini kesenler dahil olmak üzere her ne sebeple olursa olsun ilişiği kesilen öğrenciler yeniden üniversiteye dönebilecek. Bir yükseköğretim programını kazandığı halde kayıt yaptırmayanlar da yeniden öğrenim hakkından yararlanabilecek.


Başvuru için dört ay süre tanındı


Öğrencilerin yeniden öğrenim hakkından yararlanabilmeleri için kanunun yürürlüğe girdiği tarihten itibaren dört ay içinde başvuru yapmaları gerekiyor. Başvurular, öğrencinin ilişiğinin kesildiği veya kayıt hakkı kazandığı yükseköğretim kurumuna yapılacak. Düzenlemeden yararlanan öğrenciler, 2026-2027 eğitim öğretim yılında öğrenimlerine başlayabilecek.


Kanunun yürürlüğe girdiği tarihte askerlik görevini yapmakta olanlar da düzenlemeden yararlanabilecek. Bu kapsamdaki kişilerin, terhislerini takip eden 2 ay içinde ilgili yükseköğretim kurumuna başvurmaları gerekiyor.


Yeniden öğrenime başlayanların askerlik ertelemeleri ise 7179 sayılı Askeralma Kanunu çerçevesinde yapılacak.


Yatay geçiş ve açıköğretim imkânı da getirildi


Düzenlemeyle yeniden öğrenci statüsü kazananlara belirli şartları sağlamaları halinde yatay geçiş imkânı da tanınıyor. Buna göre öğrenciler, ÖSYS/YKS puanlarının giriş yılı itibarıyla aynı veya farklı bir diploma programının aynı türden taban puanına sahip olması halinde bu programlardan birine yatay geçiş talebinde bulunabilecek.


Farklı bir diploma programından yatay geçişle kabul edilecek öğrenci sayıları, ilgili programa kayıtlı öğrenci sayısı ve üniversitenin fiziki koşulları dikkate alınarak belirlenecek.


Düzenlemeden yararlanarak bir yükseköğretim kurumunda öğrenci statüsü kazananlar, başvurmaları halinde Anadolu Üniversitesi, Ankara Üniversitesi, Atatürk Üniversitesi ve İstanbul Üniversitesi bünyesindeki açıköğretim ön lisans veya lisans düzeyindeki eşdeğer programlara yatay geçiş yapabilecek. Bu geçişe ilişkin usul ve esasları belirlemeye YÖK yetkili olacak.


Bazı suçlardan mahkûm olanlar kapsam dışı


Geniş bir öğrenci grubuna yeniden öğrenim hakkı tanıyan düzenleme, bazı istisnalar da içeriyor. Buna göre düzenlemeden yararlanamayacaklar şöyle sıralandı:

author: Unknown
title: JINNEWS: 25 women and one child killed in July
content:
JINNEWS published its tally of male violence for July. According to data compiled from reports in the press, 25 women and one child were killed in July, while 17 women and two children died under suspicious circumstances.


The tally noted that in the vast majority of cases, the perpetrators of femicides were men close to the women. Accordingly, seven women were killed by their husbands, four by men they were in the process of divorcing, four by their partners, and three by men from whom they had divorced.


One woman was killed by a man she had previously been in a relationship with, one by her neighbor, one by a co-worker, one by her nephew, one by her stepson, and one by her stepbrother. In one case, the relationship between the perpetrator and the woman could not be determined.


According to JINNEWS data, the highest number of femicides was recorded in Istanbul, Dîlok (Antep) and Adana, with three cases each.


These were followed by Riha (Urfa), Düzce and Konya, with two cases each. One woman was killed in each of the following provinces: Isparta, Manisa, Karabük, Antalya, Trabzon, Kırklareli, Bedlîs (Bitlis), Bursa, Muğla and Kilis.

author: Unknown
title: Second Paris Massacre trial begins on 23 February
content:
Retired train driver William Malet killed Evîn Goyî (Emine Kara), one of the representatives of the Kurdish women’s movement, musician Mîr Perwer, and association member Abdurrahman Kızıl in an armed attack carried out on 23 December 2022, in front of the Ahmet Kaya Kurdish Cultural Center in Paris’s 10th arrondissement. Three other people were also wounded.


Malet, who was taken into custody following the attack, spoke during the investigation of his “pathological hatred” of foreigners. According to court records, he was charged with murder and attempted murder, with aggravating circumstances based on race, ethnic origin, nationality or religion.


Approximately one year before the attack, in December 2021, Malet carried out a sword attack at a migrant camp in Paris. After spending about a year in pretrial detention over that incident, he was released on 12 December 2022. Eleven days later, he carried out the attack on the Kurdish cultural center.


Psychiatric assessments conducted as part of the investigation found no serious mental illness, although personality disorders and a certain degree of impairment of his judgment at the time of the attack were alleged.


In an indictment dated 22 July 2025, prepared by three judges, it was determined that there was sufficient evidence for Malet to stand trial for the racially motivated killing of three people and attempted murder. However, the failure to classify the incident as a terrorist crime prompted reactions from Kurds and numerous political circles.


The Democratic Council of Kurds in France (CDK-F) maintains that the center was deliberately targeted and says the attack was “terrorist” in nature. Despite these demands from the Kurdish side, there continue to be reactions to the failure to question French intelligence services about the possible external links to the attack.


William Malet will stand trial before the Paris Assize Court from 23 February to 8 March 2027, on charges of “murder and attempted murder on the grounds of origin, ethnicity or religion.”


The 2022 attack took place approximately nine years after three Kurdish women activists were killed, also in Paris’s 10th arrondissement, in 2013.


Sakine Cansız (Sara), one of the founders of the PKK, Fidan Doğan (Rojbîn), the Paris representative of the KNK, and Leyla Şaylemez (Ronahî), a member of the Kurdish Youth Movement, were shot in the head and killed on 9 January 2013, at the Kurdish Information Office in central Paris.


In the investigation into that attack, all traces pointed to Ankara. Although the direction of the investigation indicated that the massacre had been carried out on Ankara’s orders, no further progress was made, particularly because of the issue of state secrets. France refused to lift state secrecy as part of the investigation.

author: Unknown
title: FEDA and DAKB: It is our duty to do what is expected of us for democracy
content:
The Alevi community, the Democratic Alevi Federation (FEDA) and the Democratic Alevi Women’s Union (DAKB) said that, now that the Framework Law has been submitted to Parliament,  developments are being closely followed.


In a statement, the two organizations said: “It is well known that the Alevi community, which has experienced all forms of massacres and genocides, has a vital need for democracy and peace. Moreover, in every process, peace and democracy are also indispensable for the Alevi community in terms of faith. It is expected that the framework law submitted to Parliament will bring an end to the conflict and pave the way for peace, while creating opportunities for democratic developments. Therefore, as members of the Alevi community and adherents of the Reya Heq faith, we support this law. We offer this support to the will put forward for the construction of a democratic society, once again with the belief that we will no longer be subjected to massacres, genocides and all forms of assimilation.


However, it is understood that the law has been seriously criticized by the democratic public and prominent figures, and that it contains mistakes and shortcomings. In this regard, it is clear that the law has very significant shortcomings concerning Alevis as well. First and foremost, defining the issue in terms of ‘terrorism’ and treating it separately from the democratization process is not in keeping with the spirit of the intention to resolve the problem. The regulation containing these expressions falls far short of representing the recognition of a right."


The statement added: "The road to democracy runs through peace. Likewise, peace can only be guaranteed through democracy. Therefore, separating these two concepts from one another does not serve a solution.


As FEDA and DAKB, we cannot ignore this historic development concerning the future of our country and our peoples. Of course, this law will not resolve the problems of the entire democratization process, foremost among them the Kurdish question. However, the passage of this law is not a development that we will oppose because of its various shortcomings. It is our duty and responsibility to open this door that has been left ajar all the way, and to do whatever is required of us to move towards peace and democracy along this path."

author: Unknown
title: Ocak: My mother never gave up, from Dersim to Galatasaray
content:
Emine Ocak, one of the leading figures of the Saturday Mothers' struggle for truth and justice and the mother of Hasan Ocak, a symbol of the victims of enforced disappearance in custody, was commemorated at the Human Rights Association (IHD) Istanbul Branch on the first anniversary of her death. Together with the family of Rıdvan Karakoç, who was also forcibly disappeared in custody, the Ocak family waged a long-running campaign against enforced disappearances that challenged the state's policies of uniformity and enforced silence, racism disguised as nationalism, labor exploitation, torture, massacres and what they described as the state's fascist character. Emine Ocak, who survived the Dersim Massacre and later devoted her life to the struggle for truth and justice, went on to lead years of civil disobedience protests in Galatasaray Square after her son was forcibly disappeared in Istanbul. Hüseyin Ocak spoke to ANF about the life and legacy of his 90-year-old mother.


My mother was just 18 months old during the Dersim Massacre


Hüseyin Ocak said his mother, Emine Ocak, had lived through massacres, repression and resistance from the very beginning of her life. He said she was born in the village of Xaltan, in Nazimiye, Dersim, and that when the Dersim Massacre began in 1937, her family fled into the surrounding mountains to escape the military.


He said his mother and her twin sister, Sevgi, were only 18 months old at the time. Ocak said: "While the family was hiding in the forest, they feared the babies' cries would reveal their location. They even considered killing my mother and her twin sister. They said, 'They will find us here and kill us all. Rather than all of us dying, let's kill these two children.' My grandmother refused. She said, 'I will take the children somewhere else. If they find anyone, let them find us and kill us. You survive.' She took my mother and her twin sister and hid in the opposite direction from where the rest of the family was sheltering. At that time, soldiers were burning villages and shooting villagers they came across. When my grandmother returned to the village with the two babies, she found it burned to the ground and saw that my mother's two uncles had been killed there. She then tried to rebuild her life. What I mean is that my mother faced the threat of death from the very moment she opened her eyes to the world."


We became targets of fascists in Elazığ


Ocak said his mother and her family moved to the village of Çukur in central Dersim in 1943. He said she married his father, who had also moved there from Nazimiye, when she was just 15 or 16 years old. Ocak also said: "In 1973, my parents moved to Elazığ (Xarpêt), where they once again became targets, this time of fascists. I was 10 years old then. We were fighting for our lives. It was one of the most violent periods, and we lived with the fear that our home could be bombed at any moment. Fascists repeatedly attacked us, and we were detained many times because of the events taking place there. My brother Ali Ocak lost his hearing as a result of torture. Our lives were always marked by hardship. My brother Hasan Ocak, who was later forcibly disappeared in custody, also witnessed those difficult years. He completed primary school, secondary school and high school in Elazığ, then enrolled at the Siirt Education Institute. After graduating, he moved to Istanbul in 1985."


Ocak said the family was also forced to leave Elazığ after the 12 September 1980 military coup and added: "We were a well-known family and were constantly under threat. I was the first to move to Istanbul as a university student. Later, my brothers Ali and Hasan joined me. In 1987, we brought the entire family to Istanbul. But we never found peace there either. Hasan was forcibly disappeared in custody ten years after arriving in Istanbul."


Hasan's last stop was my shop


Ocak said the last person Hasan spoke to before his detention was their mother by phone, and that he later stopped by his shop. He added: "At the time, I was running a shop in Laleli. Hasan came by, and we planned to meet again at home that evening. But after he left my shop, he never came home. It was Newroz on 21 March, and many people were being detained and arrested. We believe Hasan was taken into custody somewhere between Aksaray and Topkapı, because we were living in Avcılar. A lawyer also heard police officers saying, 'We have caught Hasan Ocak, we're bringing him in.' Hasan …

title: Fenerbahçe Lukaku ile anlaştı: Gözler bonservis pazarlığında
content:
Fotoğraf: Илья Хохлов/Wikimedia Commons CC BY-SA 3.0

Fenerbahçe, yeni sezon öncesi hücum hattını güçlendirmek için forvet arayışlarını sürdürüyor. Sarı-lacivertliler, Napoli forması giyen Belçikalı golcü Romelu Lukaku ile prensip anlaşmasına vardı.

Kulüp ile oyuncu arasındaki görüşmelerin olumlu sonuçlandığı, transferin önündeki temel engelin ise Napoli ile bonservis konusunda anlaşma sağlanması olduğu belirtildi.

Fenerbahçe, Lukaku’nun transferi için Napoli’ye 6 milyon euroluk bonservis teklifi sundu. İtalyan kulübünün bu teklifi kabul etmediği ve taraflar arasındaki görüşmelerin sürdüğü bildirildi.

Sarı-lacivertli yönetimin, Napoli ile bonservis bedeli konusunda yeni bir teklif üzerinden pazarlık yapması bekleniyor.

Fenerbahçe yönetimi, Lukaku transferinin gerçekleşmemesi ihtimaline karşı alternatif isimlerle de temaslarını sürdürüyor.

Borussia Dortmund forması giyen Serhou Guirassy ile Aston Villa’nın golcüsü Ollie Watkins, sarı-lacivertlilerin transfer listesinde bulunuyor.

Yönetimin, bu iki oyuncudan biri için uygun mali koşullar oluşması halinde transfer planında değişikliğe gidebileceği belirtiliyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Vize serbestisi için önemli adım: 6 kriterle ilgili çalışma başlatıldı
content:
Fotoğraf: https://kaboompics.com//Pexels

Avrupa Komisyonu'nun 2025 Schengen vize istatistiklerine göre Türkiye'den yapılan başvurular yüzde 8 artarak 1,26 milyonu aşarken ret oranı yüzde 14,6 seviyesinde kaldı. Türk vatandaşlarına en yüksek ret oranı uygulayan ülkeler şöyle sıralandı:

Cumhurbaşkanı Yardımcısı Cevdet Yılmaz, Türkiye'nin Avrupa Birliği ile yürüttüğü vize serbestisi uygulamasında kalan 6 kriter için çalışma başlatıldığını açıkladı. Yılmaz, Avrupa'daki siyasi iradeyi de görmek istediklerini belirterek; "Kişisel verilerin korunması en önemli maddelerden biri bu. Geri kabul ve terör tanımı ile ilgili bir mesele var. KVKK konusunda Adalet Bakanlığımıza teşekkür ediyorum. Akın Bakanımız, bir bilim kurulu oluşturdu, çalışma yürüttü, ben de koordine ediyorum. Dışişleri, Adalet, İçişleri bütün bakanlıklarımızı bir araya getirdik, toplantılar yaptık. O kurulda bu kanun tartışıldı. Bu biraz mutfak çalışmasıydı. Burada yeni bir yaklaşım geliştirildi. Kurumlarımız tarafından şimdi Dışişleri Bakanlığımız üzerinden Avrupa kurumları ile istişareler yapılacak" dedi.

Türkiye, AB ile yürüttüğü vize serbestisi uygulamasında 6 kritere takıldı. 13 yıldır sağlanamayan kriterler şu şekilde:

- Terörle mücadele yasasında değişiklik,

- AB Polis Örgütü (Europol) ile operasyonel işbirliği anlaşması imzalanması,

- Avrupa Konseyi bünyesindeki Yolsuzluğa Karşı Devletler Grubu'nun (GRECO) yolsuzlukla mücadele alanındaki önerilerinin uygulanması,

- Kişisel verilere yönelik yasal düzenlemelerin Avrupa standartlarıyla uyumlu hale getirilmesi,

- Suç bağlantılı konularda tüm AB üyeleriyle işbirliğine gidilmesi,

- Türkiye üzerinden kural dışı şekilde AB ülkelerine geçiş yapan kişilerin geri alınmasına ilişkin Geri Kabul Anlaşması'nın (GKA) tüm unsurlarıyla uygulanması.

Çerçeve yasanın TBMM Adalet Komisyonu'ndan geçmesi ardından terörle mücadele ve vize serbestisi konusunu değerlendiren Cumhurbaşkanı Yardımcısı Yılmaz, Türkiye'nin Avrupa Birliği'yle (AB) yürüttüğü vize serbestisi uygulamasında kalan 6 kriter konusunda bir çalışma başlattığını duyurdu.

"Kişisel verilerin korunması en önemli maddelerden biri bu. Geri kabul ve terör tanımı ile ilgili bir mesele var. KVKK konusunda Adalet Bakanlığımıza teşekkür ediyorum. Akın Bakanımız, bir bilim kurulu oluşturdu, çalışma yürüttü, ben de koordine ediyorum. Dışişleri, Adalet, İçişleri bütün bakanlıklarımızı bir araya getirdik, toplantılar yaptık. O kurulda bu kanun tartışıldı. Bu biraz mutfak çalışmasıydı. Burada yeni bir yaklaşım geliştirildi. Kurumlarımız tarafından şimdi Dışişleri Bakanlığımız üzerinden Avrupa kurumları ile istişareler yapılacak. Bu konuda bizim Avrupa'daki siyasi iradeyi görmemiz lazım, onların da atması gereken adımlar var."

title: Tunç: A new period of struggle for the oppressed begins with Framework Law
content:
The effects of the bill brought to Parliament by the AKP government as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process continue to be felt. The content of the law is being debated across all areas of society. The public is eagerly awaiting the process that will follow the law’s entry into force.


In the Peace and Democratic Society Process initiated by Leader Apo, Turkey is preparing to take a step for the first time through a legal regulation. The law submitted to Parliament has attracted considerable public attention and continues to be debated in all its aspects.


Kurdish politician and writer Aziz Tunç, who was arrested during the KCK operations, spent a long time in prison and has been living in exile for many years, spoke to our agency about the law.


We reached this state thanks to negotiations


Stating that a historic process was underway, Aziz Tunç continued: “As has been stated repeatedly, this law has come before Parliament as an important stage in a historic process. During this process, the Kurdish freedom movement decided to continue its struggle for rights through democratic methods instead of armed struggle.


This decision brought an end to the conflict-ridden process marked by blood and suffering. At this stage of the process, the framework law being brought before Parliament also means that the existence and demands of the Kurds are being transferred onto a legal and political footing. As is known, it was not easy to reach this point. This law has emerged as a result of nearly two years of discussions and negotiations.”


A new period of struggle for the oppressed is beginning


Emphasizing that the law was not a magic law, Aziz Tunç said that a new period was beginning in the struggle of the oppressed with this law, and continued: “Of course, this law is not a magic law that solves everything. On the contrary, it is clear that the law contains none of the demands concerning democratic rights and freedoms. Yet democratization is both urgent and necessary for a just solution to the Kurdish question, as required by the process, and for the rights and freedoms demanded by all sections of society.


However, expecting every problem to be solved through a law is also not compatible with the social and political realities of the country. That is why Mr Öcalan has stated that this road is long and arduous, and that this law is the first step of a thousand-kilometre journey. Mr Öcalan has already played a very decisive role in bringing the process to this point. This needs to be specifically acknowledged. Therefore, with this law, a new period of struggle is beginning for all the oppressed.”


Clarification needed on implementation of certain articles


Noting that there are thousands of people living in exile simply because they engaged in political activity, Aziz Tunç continued: “Thousands of people who have been forced to live in exile simply because they engaged in politics are now experiencing the excitement of returning. It is understood that this law will provide such an opportunity. Those who went into exile in recent years were generally people who had reached a certain stage in their lives. This has made it difficult for them to adapt to the environments to which they moved. Therefore, the desire and intention to return are particularly strong among those who went into exile in recent years. However, although the current law is expected to provide an opportunity for return, there are ambiguities in the law and points that require clarification, particularly regarding how it will actually be implemented in practice.”

Texte paru dans le numéro 1885 du magazine mensuel de la Fédération Anarchiste (

FA

Le Monde Libertaire

fémonationalisme

IFP

Le réseau Atlas et le projet Périclès du milliardaire Pierre-Édouard Stérin participent à l'édification du «

D'autres initiatives voient également le jour dans les médias et le champ littéraire pour «

 

armer

Le réseau Atlas créé en 1981 par Anthony Fisher est un réseau «

 

libertarien

 

» et ultraconservateur finançant à travers le monde des structures visant à défendre l'économie de marché et à limiter l'État au simple accomplissement de ses fonctions «

 

régaliennes

 

» à savoir la police, la «

 

justice

 

», et l'armée. Ses fonds composés de contributions issues de sociétés comme Philip Morris, Pfizer, ExxonMobil ou Michelin financent en France de nombreuses initiatives dites d'extrême-droite, qu'elles se revendiquent du nationalisme, du souverainisme ou du libéralisme.


 La première d'entre elles fut dès 1981 l'Institut Économique de Paris (

IEP

1

IFP

partenaire de longue date du réseau Atlas

title: Tiryaki: Together we'll implement a model of governing, producing and sharing through municipalities
content:
DEM Party Êlih (Batman) MP and Deputy Co-Chair responsible for Local Government Mehmet Rüştü Tiryaki stressed that countries with strong local governments also have high standards of democracy.


“The more democracy there is at the local level, the more democracy there is in that country. The stronger local governments are, the stronger that country’s democracy is,” Tiryaki said.


 


Tiryaki noted that local government in Turkey has a 150-year history, but said this process had not followed a course in which local democracy became stronger day by day. He stressed that in recent years, the powers of administrative tutelage over local governments had increased. “Local democracy and local governments have never been this weak in the history of this country,” he added.


We have 27 years of experience


Recalling that the DEM Party tradition has 27 years of experience in local government, dating back to 1999, Tiryaki said they had introduced practices during this period that would be written in golden letters in the country’s history. He said practices such as multilingual municipal administration, co-presidency and equal representation had set an example not only for Turkey but for the world.


Tiryaki said they had also made significant progress in the cultural sphere, opening kindergartens providing education in the mother tongue and transforming every municipality into a centre for culture and the arts. He added that they had governed municipalities together with the people. “We made municipalities institutions that belong to our people themselves. We created municipalities whose doors they could open, where they could meet managers at every level and where they could see that these institutions belonged to them,” he said.


Participatory budgeting in six municipalities


Tiryaki said they had recently introduced participatory budgeting, starting in Gımgım (Varto) and Amed’s Rezan (Bağlar) district, and that this year the practice had been expanded to six municipalities. He said it would be implemented in all municipalities in the coming years. He also noted that they organised public meetings in neighbourhoods and determined budget items together with residents.


Tiryaki said they viewed municipalities as communes and communes as municipalities. “We are discussing the principles of governance, production and sharing together with our people. We are talking about governing together with our people, producing together with our people and sharing what we produce. We will work to truly turn our municipalities into centres of the commune,” he said.


He added that, within this framework, they were conducting a broad discussion ranging from cooperatives to the restructuring of governance mechanisms.


The expanding role of local government


Tiryaki said modern municipalities were no longer limited to services such as waste collection, sewage, water, parks and gardens, but had assumed responsibilities across a broad range of areas, from services for people with disabilities and the elderly to culture, the arts, language and literature.


He said there was a strong social demand and a serious struggle both in Kurdistan and in Turkey to strengthen local governments. However, he pointed out that laws adopted in recent years had restricted the powers of local governments, while many decision-making mechanisms had been transferred to the central government.


Solving problems


Mehmet Rüştü Tiryaki said that local governments had assumed an almost central position in Abdullah Öcalan’s proposals concerning the Kurdish issue and the democratisation of Turkey, and continued: “If we can truly resolve the issue of local government in Kurdistan; if we can increase the powers of local governments, remove the reservations attached to international conventions, limit the powers of administrative tutelage, and turn them into governments that draw up their own budgets and make their own decisions, then we will also have resolved the fundamental century-old problem of this country, the issue for which efforts are being made to find a solution within the framework of the discussions on a ‘Peace and Democratic Society.’”


Tiryaki stressed that democratising local governments, abolishing the powers of administrative tutelage and organising municipalities as communes were important areas that could help resolve the country’s two fundamental problems, particularly the Kurdish issue and the problem of democracy.

title: Sendikal sıkışmışlığa karşı işçi iradesi
content:
Eskişehir – Odunpazarı Belediyesinde çalışan işçilerin bir süredir gündeminde sendika değişikliği var. Bir yanda yıllardır var olan ancak işçilerin hak arayışında silik bir figür olarak kalan yetkili sendika, diğer yanda yeni kurulan “bağımsız” bir yapı ve alanı boş bırakmamaya çalışan alternatif iddialar… İşçiler için asıl ihtiyaç kimin en doğrusu olduğunu seçmek değil kendi iradelerinin temsiliyetini garanti altına almak.

Yetkili sendika Belediye-İş yöneticileri ve işçiler, belediye yönetiminin işçilere yeni sendika Çağdaş-Sen’e geçmeleri yönünde baskı yapıldığını dillendiriyor. Bu iddianın sahadaki karşılığı ve doğruluk payı göz ardı edilemez. Nitekim yerel yönetimlerin sendikalaşma süreçlerinde bir sendikadan yana taraf olması ya da yönlendirici bir biçimde tutum alması sık rastlanan ve sendikal özgürlüğün altını oyan başlıca unsurlardan.

Ancak meseleye sadece “yönetim baskısı” penceresinden bakmak, tablodaki kimi gerçekleri de ıskalamak anlamına gelir. Çünkü Belediye-İş Sendikasının bugüne kadar sergilediği pratik işçilerin gözünde bu yapının meşruiyetini çoktan tartışmalı hale getirmişti. İşçilerin haberi ve onayı olmaksızın imzalanan Toplu İş Sözleşmeleri (TİS), işten çıkarmalar karşısında sessizliğe bürünmeleri ve işçilerin kadro mücadelesinde gösterilen atalet, hafızalardaki tazeliğini koruyor.

Yıllar boyunca şantiyelerde, park ve bahçelerde görünmeyen, işçinin feryadına ve taleplerine kulak tıkayan bu bürokratik mekanizma şimdi koltuğunu kaybetmenin verdiği endişe sebebiyle sahaya inmiş ve işçileri Belediye İş’te kalmaya ikna etme turlarında. Çağdaş-Sen tehdidi uzun zamandır uyku modunda olan sendika şube başkanını ve yöneticilerini uyandırdı. Lakin bu ani uyanış işçiler nezdinde bir hak arama mücadelesinden ziyade koltuğu bırakmama çabası olarak okunuyor.

Tartışmaların fitilini ateşleyen bağımsız olarak kurulan Çağdaş-Sen ise kurulur kurulmaz işaret edilmişçesine Odunpazarı Belediyesinde örgütlenme yarışına girdi. Hızla şantiyelere inerek, işçilerle temas kurmaya çalışan bu yapı, bir yandan mevcut sendika ile bağını koparmak isteyen işçiler için bir çıkış yolu gibi görünürken diğer yandan arkasındaki “hızlı ve organize” hareket kabiliyetine dair soru işaretleri barındırıyor. İşçiler, yukarıdan tasarlanan ya da birilerinin eliyle yönlendirilen bir yapının işçinin çıkarlarını savunup savunmayacağı konusunda son derece kuşkulu. Çağdaş-Sen ile ilgili konuşan bir işçi örneğin şöyle diyor; “Dillerinde bir laf var Çağdaş Sen’de birlik olalım. Tamam, birlik olalım da ne vaat ediyorsun. Belediye İş’ten farklı olarak ne yapacaksın. Ortada ben bir fark göremiyorum. Kuru kuruya birlik olma çağrısı yapıyorlar. Hangi ilken var, neden sana katılalım buralarda bir açıklamaları yok”

Bu karmaşa yetmiyor olacak ki sahneye çıkmaya çalışan bir diğer aktör de DİSK’e bağlı Genel-İş Sendikası oldu. Odunpazarı işçilerine “Gelin bizde örgütlenin” çağrısı yapan Genel-İş yöneticileri, yaptıkları açıklamada kulağa hoş gelen, sendiakal mücadele ilkelerine dayalı bir söylem benimsiyor. Ancak işçilerin hafızası ve tecrübeleri etiketlerin ötesine geçmeyi zorunlu kılıyor. Ülke genelinde ve yerelde Genel-İş yönetiminin gerek pratiği gerekse işçilerin yaşadıkları sorunları ele alışı olsun, TİS masalarında atılan imzalar olsun Belediye İş’in pratiğinden çok da farklı sayılmaz. Bürokratikleşmiş sendikal anlayış, tabanın iradesini yok sayan merkezi kararlar Genel-İş’in de sıklıkla eleştirildiği alanlar. Dolayısıyla tabela değiştirmek dışında bir karşılığı olmayan bu çağrılarının işçilerin sorunlarını sihirli bir değnek misali dokunup çözemeyeceği aşikâr.

Tüm bu aktörler sahada rekabet ederken Odunpazarı Belediyesi işçileri içerisinde derin bir tedirginlik ve güvensizlik yayılıyor. Hangi sendikanın arkasında duracaklar, hangi sendika kendilerini gerçekten temsil edecek, net bir fikir birliğinden söz etmek mümkün değil. Bir yanda yıllardır belediyede örgütlü olan bürokratik merkez, diğer yanda yeni kurulan ve arkasındaki dinamikler tam olarak çözülememiş bağımsız bir sendika, öte yanda ise iddialı ama pratik sınavı sabıkalı bir başka sendika. Bu sıkışmışlık hali, işçiler arasında kafa karışıklığı yaratırken, asıl kaybedenin yine işçiler olacağı kaygınsı da körüklüyor. Belediye işçileri tepeden inmeyi alışkanlık haline getirmiş bu sendikal zincirlerin arasında adeta öğütülüyor.

Odunpazarı Belediyesi işçileri mevcut tartışmaları ve sendikal rekabeti bir kriz olarak değil, aksine mücadeleci bir sendikal çizgiyi inşa etmek için bir fırsat …

author: Dean Baker
title: Trump’s Truth Social Subscription Scheme Functions Like a Tax on Your 401K
content:
Since Trump’s posts often move markets, the feature essentially allows users to pay for insider trading knowledge.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation .

You may not have heard about this latest tax from Trump. That could be because he’s not going through Congress to get it. Also, this scam could get buried in the middle of his many other grifting schemes. Trump is starting a new special subscription service to his social media platform, Truth Social, where big investors will pay $100,000 a month for advance access to Trump posts that can move markets.

This means that the next time Trump posts that he will blow Iran off the map and sends oil prices soaring, the people who paid Trump’s fee will have the opportunity to buy oil futures before the jump. The same story applies on the way down, as when he posts that a deal with Iran’s leaders is imminent.

And the inside information goes well beyond oil prices. He may announce a big military contract with Lockheed or one of his sons’ companies, sending stock prices soaring. Or he could announce a big DEI investigation of Disney or some other Hollywood entertainment company, causing their stock to plummet.

There are an infinite number of ways that Trump Truth Social announcements can move markets. This subscription service allows rich investors around the country to get in on the action.

If it’s not clear how Trump’s scheme amounts to a tax on your 401(k), think more carefully. If Trump’s clients get the jump on a big rise in oil prices, that means that they get the money, not you. This is true even if, like the vast majority of small investors, you are not actively managing your funds.

The person who is managing whatever fund(s) you hold will pay the higher price for oil or stock or anything else the funds might buy because Trump’s accomplices got their first. The same applies on the way down. The fund will get less money because the Trump gang already sold the stock before your fund manager had the chance to do so.

At this point, we can’t know how much money is involved because we don’t know how many big investors are prepared to sign up for what is blatantly an insider trading scheme. But we can do some speculation.

First, we need to calculate how much money an investor would expect to make from a service where they are paying $1.2 million a year. Since this scheme would likely lead to civil and possibly criminal charges if the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) or Justice Department ever gets taken over by honest people, it seems a very big payoff would be required.

Any person paying Trump for insider information would need to expect substantial legal bills, and also the possibility of being forced to leave the country or face prison time. (Ask Martha Stewart .) Let’s say the payoff has to be at least 20 to 1, which would mean they would need to earn $24 million a year for their Trump Truth Social subscription to make sense.

Then we need to speculate on how many people are prepared to sign up for Trump’s racket. We know Wall Street is a cesspool, but this level of open corruption is probably too sleazy even for most of the big traders. Still, there could be a 1,000 Trump-loving sewer dwellers who don’t mind being open about their thefts.

In that case, the Trump insiders would be siphoning off $24 billion a year from other investors in the market. That is not huge in the context of a $7.5 trillion budget, but it is larger than many things we have big fights over.

For example, the AIDS program for Africa, which saved tens of millions of lives, and Elon Musk eagerly fed into the wood chopper, cost $6 billion a year. That’s roughly a fourth of Trump’s 401(k) tax. The cost of extending the subsidies in the ACA exchanges, which Trump and the Republicans ended, would have been a bit higher at $27 billion a year.

So, 401(k) holders and other small investors are paying a considerable chunk of money through this “tax” to Trump and his enrolled insiders. As I said, this tax is not going to Congress for approval, but we can assume that all the Republicans in Congress approve of it. If not, Trump would be impeached for such a blatantly illegal scheme, but we know the Republican motto: “If Trump Does It, It’s Good.”

author: Stephen Prager
title: Trump May Be Renewing His Push for Control of Greenland
content:
A Texas oil company with ties to Trump is preparing to drill for oil without permission from Greenland’s government.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

After appearing to back off earlier this year, President Donald Trump this week renewed his threats to seize Greenland . A Saturday report that a Texas oil company with ties to Trump had begun preparing to drill in the Arctic territory without permission has raised fresh concerns that his push for control of the island may already be moving beyond rhetoric.

As The Guardian reported , Greenland’s government issued a “strong warning” last week after learning that a Texas oil company called Greenland Energy had begun making unauthorized preparations for oil extraction in Jameson Land, a remote area of eastern Greenland, including bringing drilling materials ashore.

The company, founded last year, has claimed that Jameson Land may contain $1 trillion worth of crude oil and announced plans to drill two wells there — a project that requires approval from Greenland’s government.

Has Trump’s invasion of Greenland already begun? An American oil company connected to Donald Trump is preparing to sink wells in remote Greenland despite not having received permission from the local authorities. https://t.co/12w064lknY

The company also has ties to several Trump allies and associates. According to The Guardian :

Greenland Energy has retained Phil McGraw, better known as Dr. Phil, a prominent right-wing former chatshow host who served on Trump’s religious freedom commission, to make a documentary series that will “capture the mission of these modern-day wildcatters.”

It has also appointed as a director a US Navy veteran who is working on Golden Dome, the missile defense plan for which Trump says controlling Greenland is “vital.”

Larry Swets, Greenland Energy’s chair and a big shareholder, appears to enjoy access to Trump’s circle. He has said the oil project is “not related to American annexation.”

A Greenland Energy representative falsely claimed in June that the company had permission to place equipment on Jameson Land, before later saying there had been confusion.

But the following month, residents saw a barge arrive with drilling equipment. A Danish outlet confirmed that the delivery was intended for Greenland Energy.

Following the delivery, Greenland’s government said on July 30 that the company “did not have the necessary approvals from the mineral resources authority” and would receive a warning that “all future logistical matters must be advised and approved by the mineral resources authority—before they are carried out.”

Two days later, Trump posted an ominious digitally altered image to Truth Social depicting himself as a giant looming over a Greenlandic town, captioned “Hello, Greenland!”

A day earlier, Trump had appeared on the right-wing network Real America’s Voice, where host Steve Gruber reminded him that he had predicted Greenland would be under US control by the time he leaves office in 2029.

“You’ll be right,” Trump replied. “Greenland is important. Not from their standpoint, from our standpoint. You should make that bet.”

Before this week’s comments, Trump had spoken far less publicly about Greenland since January, when he threatened to use military force to take over the island if Denmark did not cede it. To pressure NATO allies, Trump threatened steep tariffs on several European countries, but backed off after Europe pledged retaliatory tariffs, causing panic in the financial markets .

President Trump just posted, "Hello, Greenland!" 👋 So… when is it happening? 😉 pic.twitter.com/gs4jRH7ZIS

“Let nobody think Trump has given up on taking Greenland,” said John O’Brennan, professor of European politics at Maynooth University in Ireland. He added that Greenland Energy’s unauthorized activity “is the latest act of lawlessness his acolytes are engaged in.”

Kenneth Roth, the former executive director of Human Rights Watch, responded to the story by asking , “Has Trump’s invasion of Greenland already begun?”

Historian Ruth Ben-Ghiat suggested it was possible. “Invasions,” she said, “often start with ‘technical’ projects that justify the presence of operatives and ‘technical experts’ who are also doing recon and advance prep.”
